title.rendered: iFixit iPhone 18 Pro teardown shows battery sizes and new variable aperture

content.rendered:
iFixit has torn down the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max and the inside tells the same story Apple did on stage, plus a few caveats, according to the iFixit teardown published September 20.

The teardown confirms battery sizes for the eSIM-only models sold in the U.S. and several other countries, gets close to the new variable aperture camera, and flags a repairability issue iFixit hasn’t seen this badly before.

Battery capacities are official for eSIM models

iFixit read the labels directly:

  • iPhone 18 Pro (eSIM): 4,288 mAh, 16.76 Wh, up 0.8% from 4,252 mAh on iPhone 17 Pro
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max (eSIM): 5,567 mAh, 21.751 Wh, up 9.4% from 5,088 mAh on iPhone 17 Pro Max

Those numbers apply to eSIM-only units sold in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and Kuwait. Models with a physical SIM tray in other regions have smaller cells, as earlier filings suggested. The iPhone 18 Pro still relies on Apple’s own playback claims for real-world battery life, so capacity alone doesn’t tell you how long it lasts.

Once you get past the display, the battery is actually a bright spot. Apple kept the screwed-in metal battery tray from last year. You remove the tray and battery together with 13 screws and no wrestling with strong adhesive. The cell itself uses electrically releasable adhesive, about 90 seconds at 12 volts, and lifts cleanly.

The variable aperture is tiny, precise, and not really fixable

Apple’s biggest camera change this year is a mechanical variable aperture on the main 48MP camera. iFixit found six polymer-composite blades, each about as thin as a human hair and barely more than a millimeter at the tip, driven by electromagnets independent of optical image stabilization.

One blade flew across the room while iFixit pried the lens stack open. That says a lot about repairability. The blades pivot and slide on pins with almost no tolerance, and the glues are gummy. iFixit calls component-level repair as close to impossible as it gets, if the aperture sticks, you’ll be replacing the entire main camera assembly. The module itself is modular and easy to swap, but Apple hasn’t posted parts pricing yet. The iPhone 17 Pro camera assembly was $249, so expect more this year.

For photographers, iFixit is also skeptical about the benefit. On a 1/1.3-inch-type sensor with a 6.8mm focal length, the four presets, f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8 and f/4.0, give you about 7.3x more light at the widest versus f/4.0, but not the big background blur you’d get from a full-frame camera at the same f-number. Their test shots show legible background even at f/1.48. It’s real control, but subtle on a phone sensor.

A better cooling system, with a trade-off

The A20 Pro has moved to the outside of the dual-layer logic board, sitting directly against a vapor chamber Apple says is three times larger by surface area than before. A spongy thermal interface pad helps conduct heat evenly, and the chamber spreads it across the body. That move should help sustained performance for gaming and on-device AI.

It comes with a cost. The NAND storage now sits inside the board sandwich, so any storage-level or deep board repair starts with separating the layers, more heat, more labor, and more risk before you even reach the fault. Data recovery is also harder because the data is encrypted to that NAND.

The display frame cracked and iFixit is not sure why yet

Here’s the surprise. The plastic frame around the display cracked or pulled away on three of the four phones iFixit opened. The phones still worked, but a damaged frame won’t sit flush after reassembly and could compromise water resistance.

iFixit is cautious here. The same frame has been used since iPhone 15 Pro without this much trouble, and other teardowns haven’t reported the same damage. Four phones is too few to call it a trend. Adhesive strength, heating time, iFixit heated one intact unit for 25 minutes at 70-72°C, technique, or a change in plastic could all be factors. The larger vapor chamber may also be pulling heat away from the seam, making the adhesive harder to soften.

The teardown is otherwise front-entry only. The rear glass opens, but there’s nothing serviceable inside aside from the wireless charging coil. The USB-C port is a separate part but buried under screws and adhesive, a step back from the more accessible layout on the iPhone 16 Pro.

iFixit gives both phones a provisional 7 out of 10 for repairability. The score credits the tray-mounted battery and modular camera, but docks points because almost every repair still goes through that glued display. For now, the display frame issue doesn’t drag the score down further, iFixit wants more data.

One last modem oddity

All versions now carry Apple’s C2 modem except the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max, which still uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80. iFixit notes this is likely the tail end of Apple’s prior agreement to use Qualcomm chips through 2026. Apple put it in the model with the largest battery, so extra power draw is less noticeable. This will likely be the last iPhone to ship with a Qualcomm modem.

excerpt.rendered: iFixit’s iPhone 18 Pro teardown confirms eSIM battery sizes, shows the 6-blade variable aperture up close, larger vapor chamber cooling, and a new display-frame cracking flag.

title.rendered: Apple scrapped a shorter Apple Pencil for iPhone Duo before launch: Report

content.rendered:
Apple built a smaller Apple Pencil specifically for the iPhone Duo and then dropped it before mass production, according to Bloomberg.

Mark Gurman reports in his Power On newsletter that the Duo was supposed to launch with a shorter, stubbier Pencil designed to magnetically attach to the hinge side of the foldable. The project ran into technical problems ahead of mass production, so Apple scrapped it.

Instead, Apple said at its September 9 event that the iPhone Duo will support the existing USB-C Apple Pencil later this year, but not at launch.

That delay is not just marketing. Gurman notes getting the iPad Pencil to work on the Duo is not as simple as flipping a switch. Apple still has to ship new software and run extensive internal testing to make the Pencil work on both the 5.4-inch outer display and the 7.6-inch inner display. He expects the update to arrive fairly late in 2026.

The shift is notable because Gurman had flagged the stubby prototype weeks before the event, while also saying it was unlikely to ship. That call turned out to be right.

Why Apple had to fall back to USB-C

The Duo was designed from the start to support Pencil input, but the plan changed from a bespoke accessory to compatibility with hardware people already own. The USB-C model is the lowest-cost Pencil in the lineup and charges over USB-C, not by magnetic attachment.

Apple’s own pages for the iPhone Duo confirm the October launch window, with preorders starting October 16 and availability on October 23, and no Pencil included in the box. Pencil support is listed as coming later this year.

Code spotted in iOS 27 also points to hover support for the foldable, suggesting Apple wants the experience to feel like it does on iPad, where the tip is tracked just above the display.

What this means if you planned to draw on Duo

You won’t need to buy a new Pencil if you already own the USB-C version. You will, however, have to wait. Apple hasn’t given an exact date, and Gurman’s reporting suggests you should treat "later this year" as December rather than October.

If you don’t already own a Pencil, there’s little reason to buy one now just for Duo until Apple confirms which models are supported, Gurman specifically names USB-C, not Apple Pencil Pro or Apple Pencil (2nd generation).

A dedicated hinge-mounted Pencil would have been tidier for a pocketable foldable, but Apple is betting that software compatibility beats another accessory to carry and charge. Whether that feels like a compromise will depend on how well the full-size Pencil handles on a phone that folds. For now, the practical way to plan is to consider only the accessories that actually fit the Duo’s hinge rather than waiting for a custom Pencil.

title.rendered: How to update your iPhone to iOS 27 (Step-by-step guide)

content.rendered:
Key takeaways:

  • iPhone models supporting iOS 27: Only iPhone 11 and newer and the iPhone SE (2nd generation and later).
  • Preparation before installing latest iOS version: Back up your iPhone, clear enough storage, and stay plugged into power with Wi-Fi to avoid failed updates.
  • Ways to install latest iOS: You can update over the air, enable automatic downloads, or connect to a Mac via Finder if storage is too tight.
  • Precautions for smooth updating: Always back up, ensure stable Wi-Fi, and keep your iPhone charging to prevent corruption or interruptions during installation.

Apple has officially released iOS 27, bringing a major software update to compatible iPhones. The new version introduces Apple’s next-generation Siri AI, additional Apple Intelligence features, Liquid Glass customization, redesigned experiences across several apps, and a range of system improvements.

iOS 27 is available starting September 14, 2026, and comes pre-installed on Apple’s latest iPhone models, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. Owners of compatible older iPhones can manually download and install the update.

However, to do that, you must first ensure that your iPhone supports iOS 27. If it does, take care of a few things in advance to ensure a smooth upgrade experience. Here’s everything you need to know about installing iOS 27 on your iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • Does your iPhone support iOS 27?
    • iOS 27 vs Apple Intelligence: There's an important difference
  • How to prepare your iPhone for iOS 27
    • 1. Back up your iPhone
    • 2. Free up enough space
    • 3. Plug in and connect to Wi-Fi
  • 3 ways to install iOS 27 on your iPhone
    • 1. Manually Install iOS 27 Over the Air (OTA)
    • 2. Make Your iPhone Install iOS 27 Automatically
    • 3. Install the latest iOS using a Mac (Optional)
  • Enjoy the new features in iOS 27

Does your iPhone support iOS 27?

The good news is that Apple hasn’t dropped any additional iPhone models from the iOS 27 compatibility list.

Just like iOS 26, iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and newer, along with the iPhone SE (2nd generation and later). Apple’s official compatibility list includes both older models and the latest 2026 iPhones.

This means that iOS 18 was the last major iOS update for the iPhone XS, XS Max, and iPhone SE (1st generation), launched in 2019.

Complete list of iPhones that support iOS 27:

  • iPhone SE (2nd & 3rd generation)
  • iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, iPhone 11 Pro Max
  • iPhone 12, iPhone 12 mini, iPhone 12 Pro, iPhone 12 Pro Max
  • iPhone 13, iPhone 13 mini, iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 13 Pro Max
  • iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Plus, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone 14 Pro Max
  • iPhone 15, iPhone 15 Plus, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17e
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max

If your iPhone isn’t on this list, it cannot be upgraded to iOS 27.

iOS 27 vs Apple Intelligence: There’s an important difference

Before you update, there’s one important distinction worth knowing.

Supporting iOS 27 doesn’t automatically mean your iPhone supports Apple Intelligence. Apple’s AI features, including the new Siri AI, require newer hardware.

Apple Intelligence in iOS 27 is available on:

  • iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16 and later
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 17 series
  • iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • iPhone Duo

So, an iPhone 11 can run iOS 27 but cannot run Apple Intelligence.

How to prepare your iPhone for iOS 27

As mentioned, before you begin the latest iOS update process, you must perform a few actions to ensure no data loss or interruptions.

Here’s what you should do before installing iOS 27:

1. Back up your iPhone

This is the single most important step. Although an iOS update normally preserves your apps, photos, messages, and settings, having a recent backup gives you a way to recover your information if something goes wrong.

To back up with iCloud:

  1. Go to Settings → iCloud → iCloud Backup.
  2. Tap Back Up Now.

To back up with a Mac:

  1. Connect your iPhone with a cable.
  2. Open Finder and select your iPhone in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Back Up Now.

Wait until the backup finishes before starting the installation.

2. Free up enough space

The iOS 27 installer requires several gigabytes of free space to temporarily unpack it. If your iPhone is nearly full, the update may fail or freeze. To clear space on your iPhone, you can:

  • Deleting unused apps
  • Removing downloaded movies or TV shows
  • Deleting unnecessary large video files
  • Clearing old message attachments
  • Moving photos and videos to another storage service
  • Removing offline music or podcast downloads

Once done, check your available space by heading to Settings → General → iPhone Storage.

3. Plug in and connect to Wi-Fi

It’s best to download iOS 27 using a reliable Wi-Fi connection. A stable connection reduces the chance of the download being interrupted and also avoids using a large amount of cellular data.

Also, plug your iPhone into a charger before starting the installation. Apple’s automatic update system can download and install updates overnight when the iPhone is charging and connected to Wi-Fi.

3 ways to install iOS 27 on your iPhone

Whether your iPhone receives the latest iOS update over the air or not, there are three quick ways to download and install it on your iPhone.

1. Manually Install iOS 27 Over the Air (OTA)

As mentioned above, installing the latest iOS on your iPhone is pretty simple and can be done in just a few taps:

  1. Open Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Now wait for your iPhone to fetch the iOS 27 update.
  3. Hit the Download and Install button once the update appears.
  4. Enter your iPhone passcode if prompted.
  5. Agree to Apple’s terms and conditions.
  6. Wait for the download to finish. Your iPhone will restart and complete the installation.
Note If you previously enabled the Automatic Updates feature, then instead of the Download and Install button, you may see the Update Now or Update Tonight button as your iPhone might have automatically downloaded the update.

The entire process can take some time depending on your internet connection, iPhone model, and Apple’s server load.

If iOS 27 doesn’t appear, restart your iPhone and try again.

2. Make Your iPhone Install iOS 27 Automatically

You can also set your iPhone to download iOS 27 as soon as it’s available and install it overnight automatically, so you wake up with your iPhone running the latest iOS.

Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Here, tap Automatic Updates.
  3. Then, toggle on Automatically Install.
  4. Further, you can toggle on Security Responses & System Files to automatically install them with each iOS update.

Now, your iPhone will automatically download and install the latest iOS update and system files overnight once it’s available. Make sure it has at least 50% battery, is connected to a stable Wi-Fi network, and is locked. Apple says you’ll be notified before an automatic installation takes place.

3. Install the latest iOS using a Mac (Optional)

If you can’t free up enough space on your iPhone for the OTA update, you can connect it to your Mac and update via Finder. The reason is that OTA (over-the-air) updates require your iPhone to download and temporarily unpack the full iOS installer on its internal storage, which can require several gigabytes of free space.

Using Finder lets your Mac download and unpack the iOS update to the computer’s storage, then install it directly on your iPhone.

Here’s how:

  1. Connect your iPhone to your Mac using an MFi-certified cable.
  2. Now, open Finder and select your iPhone in the left sidebar.
  3. Next, go to General and click the Check for Update button on the right, and your Mac will start checking for the iOS 27 update.
  4. When the update appears, click the Download and Install button and follow the on-screen instructions.

If you’re updating an iPhone using a Windows PC, Apple provides the update process through its Windows software. Older Mac versions using macOS Mojave or earlier can also use iTunes for device updates.

Enjoy the new features in iOS 27

And that’s it; simply follow any of the methods detailed above, and you’ll have your iPhone running the latest iOS in no time. Remember, updating to a brand-new iOS release is exciting, but it’s even better when it goes smoothly.

So, make sure to back up your data, free up space, update your apps, and you’ll be ready to enjoy everything iOS 27 has to offer without any hiccups.

keyPoints.title: Preparation Before Installing iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Before updating, ensure your iPhone is backed up, has enough free storage space, and is connected to power and a stable Wi-Fi network to prevent disruptions.

keyPoints.title: Methods to Install iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: You can install iOS 26 via over-the-air update, automatic updates, or using a Mac with Finder if storage space is limited.

keyPoints.title: Supporting Devices List
keyPoints.explanation: Supported devices include iPhone SE (2nd & 3rd gen), iPhone 11 to 17 series, and Pro models, among others, with support finally returning to a pattern of more recent models.

keyPoints.title: Ensuring Smooth Update Experience
keyPoints.explanation: Follow recommended steps such as backing up data, freeing up space, and connecting to power to ensure a smooth installation of iOS 26 and enjoy its new features.

title.rendered: 10 Things you can do in GTA 6 that you couldn’t do in GTA 5

content.rendered:
We’re just weeks away from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and the hype surrounding Rockstar Games’ next magnum opus is off the charts. Over the past couple of weeks, the developer has revealed plenty of new GTA 6 details about what players can expect from Vice City and the state of Leonida. From a more immersive world to new activities and mechanics, it’s clear that the game will take the series to a completely new level compared to its predecessor. So, if you’re wondering what GTA 6 will let you do that GTA 5 didn’t, here are some of the biggest features you should look forward to.

1. Manage a full-blown relationship

One of the things you can do in GTA 6 that you couldn’t do in GTA 5 is managing the relationship between our protagonists, Jason and Lucia. How close they become and whether their relationship stands the test of time will come down to your actions.

You will be able to take them shopping, go on drives, commit robberies, and participate in various other activities to strengthen their bond. Neglecting their relationship could cause it to fall apart over time, which will have a direct impact on certain missions and story elements.

Unlike GTA 5, where Michael, Trevor, and Franklin did have a dynamic that was out of your control, GTA 6 seems to give players a much bigger say over how its protagonists interact and shape the story. It’s a much deeper system that adds RPG-like elements to the game.

2. Stop at gas stations to refuel

Gas stations in GTA 5 didn’t really serve much of a purpose, but Rockstar is changing that in GTA 6. This time around, we’re going to see functional gas stations where players can refuel and even repair their vehicles. That’s not all, as electric vehicles will also get access to dedicated charging stations around the game.

Whenever you decide to refuel or recharge your vehicle, a cutscene lasting around 10 seconds will play. Rockstar has stated that it doesn’t want fuel management to become a burden for players, which is why fuel consumption has been deliberately slowed down across all vehicles. Whether you like this feature or not, there’s no denying that it adds another layer of realism to the game.

3. Build a reputation as a criminal

GTA 6 will allow you to build your reputation as a criminal in Leonida with the new Criminal Profile system. It’s somewhat akin to the Honor system we saw in Red Dead Redemption 2, but it works a bit differently. The system will track what sort of criminal you end up being.

If you manage to de-escalate situations without causing chaos, you’ll be a professional. However, if you choose to take everyone out and cause destruction, your Criminal Profile will reflect that.

There are four different Criminal Profile states in the game: Professional, Aggressive, Violent, and Psycho. However, if you commit serious crimes, your profile will go beyond Psycho, and this change will be irreversible for the playthrough. Both Jason and Lucia will have their own individual Criminal Profiles.

4. Use your vehicle to store weapons

Say goodbye to the days of GTA 5, where you could carry infinite weapons and switch between them using the weapon wheel. With GTA 6, Rockstar is taking a realistic approach by requiring players to use their vehicles to store their weapons in the trunk. Every personal vehicle in the game will be able to carry your selected loadout as well.

This seems like a negative change on paper, but it’s going to completely change how vehicles are used and how missions are tackled. Instead of scrolling through the weapon wheel to find the right weapon for the situation, you’ll now have to think ahead about which vehicle to take and what weapons you want to bring along to deal with your targets.

5. Hit the gym to stay in shape

If you’re fond of staying fit and hitting the gym in real life, you’ll be able to do the same in GTA 6. Both Jason and Lucia will physically change depending on how much you play and what you eat. If you eat too much, for example, you can expect both protagonists to gain weight and look bigger.

This can be dealt with by hitting the gym. Players will be able to work out and exercise their characters to lose weight, and even build muscles. This means staying in shape will become another aspect of managing Jason and Lucia throughout the game.

It’s not just working out either, as other aspects of their lifestyle, such as getting enough sleep, can also affect the characters. This is a major change from GTA 5, where working out and maintaining your character’s fitness affected their hidden stats rather than their actual physical appearance in the game.

6. Explore a variety of new activities in leonida

Side activities aren’t exactly new to the GTA franchise, as previous games have featured tons of them. However, GTA 6 is amping up things by offering tons of new ones for players to enjoy.

What are we talking about? Well, for instance, the GTA 6 Extended Look revealed that players will be able to use VR headsets, watch in-game shows and commercials on their TVs, participate in car and bike races on dedicated tracks, try wrestling, read newspapers, go base jumping, hit clubs, take part in shooting ranges, go fishing, and even participate in backyard wrestling.

The activities we’ve mentioned above are just scratching the surface. Some activities that are worth looking out for are scuba diving and kayaking. With so much to do across Leonida, you won’t have to always focus on the main story missions.

7. Turn dirty money Into clean cash

GTA 6 will feature three different types of money: funds stored in your bank account, physical cash, and money kept in your duffel bag. Any money deposited in your bank account will be safe, just like in previous games. However, carrying cash comes with risks, as you’ll lose it if you die before depositing it at an ATM.

What’s interesting is how the game handles the money stored in your duffel bag. You’ll need to take it to a fence, essentially a black-market middleman who will take the stolen goods off your hands and pay you in return. This means money earned through robberies won’t be instantly credited to your account. You’ll need to take steps to turn your stolen loot into usable funds.

8. Reach a six-star wanted level

GTA 6 will bring back the franchise’s iconic wanted system, allowing players to cause chaos across Leonida, attracting different levels of police attention. The more trouble you cause, the more wanted stars you’ll earn, which will bring more forces after you. However, Rockstar is bringing several changes to make the system more immersive, such as NPC witnesses and police officers remembering your face, vehicle, and other details.

One of the biggest changes is the return of the six-star wanted level. This GTA 6 feature isn’t new, as it was present in older games but was removed in GTA 5. It’s currently unclear what kind of law enforcement response players can expect after reaching six stars, but one thing’s for certain: escaping the police at that level won’t be an easy task.

9. Dual-Wield your weapons

<insert image named “GTA6Weapons” >

Based on all the screenshots and leaks surrounding GTA 6, it seems like dual-wielding weapons is another potential feature that could make its way to the game. As the name suggests, this would allow players to wield two weapons at the same time, such as pistols or even shotguns, and fire them at the same time.

However, it’s crucial to remember that Rockstar Games hasn’t officially confirmed dual-wielding in GTA 6. There’s always a chance that the feature could be scrapped before the game’s final release.

10. Keep up with leonida on social media

Social media has become a huge part of our everyday lives, and GTA 6 looks set to bring that same influence to the game. Players will be able to access social media platforms through their phones, where they can watch short-form videos of people partying, pulling off stunts, and getting into all kinds of situations across Leonida. You will also be able to watch influencers and follow their accounts.

However, social media won’t be just about entertainment. It will also allow players to discover what’s happening across the state. You could come across livestreams of ongoing events and then travel to the location yourself to see what’s happening or even get involved.

Wrapping up

GTA 6 is shaping up to be a much more immersive experience than GTA 5, with Rockstar introducing several new mechanics and activities that could change how players interact with the world. From managing Jason and Lucia’s relationship and keeping them in shape to refuelling vehicles, storing weapons, and building a criminal profile, there’s plenty to explore beyond the main story.

With a more detailed world, expanded activities, social media, and a revamped wanted system, Leonida looks set to offer plenty of reasons to keep exploring even after completing missions. While some features, such as dual-wielding, remain unconfirmed, everything Rockstar has shown so far points toward a significantly deeper open-world experience than its predecessor.

  • GTA 6 Vehicle Customisation
  • Fortnite x Persona 5: Release date and time

title.rendered: Siri AI not showing on your iPhone? Here’s how to enable it in iOS 27

content.rendered:
Installed iOS 27 on your iPhone expecting Apple’s all-new AI-powered Siri, but still seeing the familiar Siri experience? You’re not alone.

Apple has officially released iOS 27, and Siri AI is now rolling out as a beta. But updating isn’t enough to unlock the latest Apple Intelligence features. From hardware limitations to language settings and regional restrictions, there are several reasons why Siri AI may still be missing on your iPhone.

The good news? Most of them are easy to check. Here’s everything you need to know if Siri AI is still missing from your iPhone.

Why Siri AI isn’t available on your iPhone

Unlike other iOS 27 features that become available immediately after an update, Siri AI is part of Apple’s phased rollout. That means installing iOS 27 doesn’t automatically replace the existing Siri experience.

If the new Siri isn’t showing up on your iPhone, it’s usually because one of the eligibility requirements hasn’t been met. Here’s what you should check.

1. Your iPhone must support Siri AI

The first thing to check is your iPhone model. Running the latest iOS 27 update doesn’t automatically make your iPhone compatible with Siri AI.

While iOS 27 can be installed on iPhone models starting with the iPhone 11 series, Apple Intelligence requires significantly more on-device processing power. As a result, the new Siri experience is limited to supported iPhones, including the iPhone 15 Pro/15 Pro Max and iPhone 16 or later models.

Before trying anything else, make sure your device is one of the supported models.

2. Join the Siri waitlist

Just like Apple Intelligence at launch, the new Siri AI experience is available through a waitlist. Eligible users must request access, and once Apple approves the request, the required AI models are downloaded to the iPhone in the background.

After the download is complete, the upgraded Siri experience becomes available automatically. Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings and head to Siri.
  2. Here, tap Try New Siri. A Siri with Apple Intelligence (Beta) banner will appear.
  3. Now, tap the Join Waitlist button underneath the banner.
  4. Next, tap Continue to confirm.

A successful waitlist request changes the New Siri section in Settings to “Joined Waiting List.” That’s the only confirmation you’ll get until Apple approves your account.

3. Check your Siri language

Joining the waitlist doesn’t guarantee immediate access. Apple is enabling the new Siri gradually, with support limited to select regions and Siri languages during the beta period.

If the Joined Waiting List status isn’t changing, try switching Siri Language to English (U.S.) from Settings > Siri > Language. Several users have reported that these settings make the Join Waitlist option appear and help them receive access sooner.

Apple also says support for:

  • French
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish

is coming in October as previewed in the iOS 27.2 beta. So, you can enjoy your personal digital assistant in your own language.

4. Check your region

Regional availability is another important factor.

Apple says Siri AI will not initially be available in the European Union on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS. Apple is working on bringing the feature to those platforms while addressing regional requirements.

However, Siri AI and other new Apple Intelligence features are not currently available in China while the company works through regulatory requirements.

So if you’re in a region where Siri AI hasn’t been enabled yet, try changing your Region to United States from Settings > General > Language & Region. Once Apple expands support to your region, you can switch back to your preferred settings without losing access.

What happens on your iPhone after you’re approved?

After Apple approves your request, you will get a notification that it’s available. The “Joined Waiting List” message disappears from the Siri AI (Beta) section, and the features begin appearing on your iPhone.

Your iPhone will automatically download the required AI models in the background, so you don’t need to enable anything manually.

How to check if Siri AI is finally live

Apple doesn’t leave much room for guesswork once your waitlist request is approved. The first sign is inside Settings > Siri, where the Joined Waiting List status is replaced by a Try New Siri option.

A quick glance is enough to tell the difference. The familiar full-screen Siri animation is replaced by a Dynamic Island interface that includes a Search or Ask field for both voice and text interactions.

You’ll also find a dedicated Siri app that keeps your conversations in one place, as well as a Siri tab inside the Camera app, letting you ask questions about whatever you’re pointing the camera at. If none of these additions are available, your iPhone is still running the older Siri experience.

One more thing: Siri AI is still a beta

Even though iOS 27 is now publicly available, Siri AI itself is still being released as a beta. That means Apple can continue changing the feature, its availability, and how individual capabilities work.

Apple has also warned that some Apple Intelligence features relying on server-side models are subject to daily usage limits. Those limits can vary based on factors such as request complexity, system demand and Apple’s policies.

So if a particular Siri AI feature doesn’t behave exactly as expected, that doesn’t necessarily mean there’s something wrong with your iPhone.

Summing up

Installing iOS 27 is only the first step toward getting Apple’s new Siri AI experience. If the feature isn’t showing up, check whether your iPhone is supported, join the Siri waitlist, and make sure Apple Intelligence is available in your region and preferred language.

Once your request is approved, Apple will notify you and roll out the new experience automatically. Until then, the Joined Waiting List status in Settings is the only indication that your request is in the queue.

Did the new Siri AI show up after joining the waitlist? Share your experience in the comments.

  • Apple Intelligence can build Shortcuts for you in iOS 27

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: These Apple devices are compatible with Siri AI

content.rendered:
For years, Apple promised a smarter, more capable Siri. The company previewed a major Siri overhaul at WWDC 2024, but several of the most ambitious features were delayed as Apple continued working on its next-generation artificial intelligence system.

That wait is now over. With the release of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple has officially begun rolling out Siri AI, a completely reimagined version of its voice assistant powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence.

But there’s an important catch: not every Apple device that supports the latest software can use Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Here’s the list of compatible iPhone, iPad, and Mac models that support Siri AI.

Apple’s biggest Siri upgrade yet

The new Siri AI is much more than a voice assistant refresh.

The assistant can understand personal context, allowing it to find relevant information across messages, emails, photos and other parts of your device. It also has on-screen awareness, meaning it can understand what you’re currently viewing and take actions based on that information.

You can also ask it to perform actions across Apple’s apps. Siri is also integrated into the Camera app through Siri mode, allowing users to ask questions about objects or information in front of the camera.

This is the Siri that Apple showed off two years ago and then repeatedly delayed. Now it’s finally arriving with the iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, and visionOS 27 releases. However, Apple is rolling out Siri AI as a beta, initially in English. French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish support is scheduled to expand in October.

Availability also depends on region. Apple says Siri AI will not initially be available in the European Union on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS, while Apple Intelligence and Siri AI are also unavailable in China as Apple works through regulatory requirements.

The catch: Siri AI requires Apple Intelligence

Here’s where the story gets interesting.

The new Siri requires significantly more on-device processing power than traditional Siri, particularly for the large language and generative AI models involved. It also relies on Apple’s AI infrastructure, which requires newer chips such as the A17 Pro and later models.

As a result, Apple’s compatibility list is much narrower than the list of devices capable of running iOS 27 or the latest Apple operating systems.

Apple’s current Apple Intelligence compatibility list includes the following iPhone models.

iPhone

  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17, iPhone 17e
  • iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max

That means owners of the standard iPhone 15, iPhone 14 lineup, iPhone 13 lineup, and older devices will miss out on Apple’s most advanced AI assistant even if they support iOS 27.

iPad

  • iPad Pro: M1, M2, M4, M5, or newer models.
  • iPad Air: M1, M2, M4, or newer models.
  • iPad mini: A17 Pro or newer models.

Base-model iPads (like the iPad 11th Gen) running standard A-series chips do not support Siri AI.

Apple also says that its most powerful on-device model and certain features, like expressive, naturalistic Siri voices and advanced dictation, require iPad models with the M4 chip or later and at least 12GB of unified memory.

This means that simply owning an M1 iPad does not necessarily guarantee access to every Apple Intelligence feature.

Mac

Apple Intelligence is supported on Macs powered by Apple silicon:

  • MacBook Air (M1 and later)
  • MacBook Pro (M1 and later)
  • iMac (M1 and later)
  • Mac mini (M1 and later)
  • Mac Studio (M1 Max and later)
  • Mac Pro (M2 Ultra)
  • MacBook Neo (A18 Pro)

However, Apple’s most powerful on-device model and certain related features require M3 or later Macs with at least 12GB of unified memory.

Apple Watch

Apple’s latest watchOS 27 update brings Apple Intelligence-powered Siri AI to Apple Watch.

Compatible models include:

  • Apple Watch Series 12, Series 11, Series 10, and Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4, Ultra 3, and Ultra 2
  • Apple Watch SE (3rd generation)

Note: You need to pair the Apple Watch with a nearby Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone model to use Siri AI on the watch.

Vision Pro

  • Vision Pro (M2 chip)
  • Vision Pro (M5 chip)

Apple also mentioned that CarPlay got some Siri AI features. Similar to Apple Watch, it requires an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone model connected to your vehicle.

Why this matters more than another iOS update

For many years, camera quality was the main motivation to buy a new iPhone. This became battery life and displays, and now Apple is hinting that AI will be the most important difference between generations.

If Siri AI becomes as useful as Apple claims, with personal context awareness, app actions, and conversational intelligence, many users may feel pressured to upgrade sooner than expected.

That’s a major shift in how Apple sells the future of the iPhone.

Siri got better, but limited!

Apple finally delivered the Siri overhaul users have been waiting for. The assistant is smarter, more capable, and far closer to modern AI chatbots than anything Apple has shipped before.

But the compatibility list tells an equally important story.

Siri AI isn’t just a software feature; it’s becoming a hardware privilege. And for millions of iPhone owners, Apple’s most important AI upgrade may also be the clearest sign that their current device is no longer part of the company’s long-term AI future.

What do you think about the new Siri overhaul? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title.rendered: Lil Wayne skins in Fortnite: How to get them and all cosmetics

content.rendered:
After much anticipation over the past several days, Lil Wayne finally joined the roster of musician skins in Fortnite on Saturday, September 12. This event marked the debut of the award-winning rapper in the highly popular multiplayer title, after industry peers such as Eminem, Travis Scott and Snoop Dogg, among others.

In the time since its arrival, the Lil Wayne cosmetics in the Fortnite Shop have driven demand and, at the time of writing, are charting among the best-selling items in the game. They will remain available for purchase until September 22, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. Read on to learn more about the Lil Wayne skins and related content.

Steps to get the Lil Wayne skin in Fortnite

There are two different skins inspired by Lil Wayne available in the Shop right now. Both the “Lil Wayne” skin and the “Weezy” skin are up for grabs for 1,500 V-Bucks each. Alternatively, you can also get both skins and relevant cosmetics in a single discounted purchase by going for the Lil Wayne Bundle priced at 3,600 V-Bucks.

The following steps show how you can claim one of the aforementioned Lil Wayne skins in the game.

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Then, scroll down to the “Lil Wayne” section and select your desired skin.
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

All Lil Wayne cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Lil Wayne

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Also includes: Mili Bricks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

2. Weezy

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Also includes: Weezy Board
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

3. Young Money Stage (glider)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

4. Milli Bricks (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

5. Weezy Board (back bling)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

6. Weezy Boardbreaker (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

7. Tha Guitar (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

8. 6 Foot 7 Foot (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

9. Lollipop (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

10. YM Burner (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

11. Lollipop (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

12. A Milli (2023 Remix) [jam track]

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

13. 6 Foot 7 Foot (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

14. Weezy’s Pose

Exclusively available in: Lil Wayne Bundle

Rounding up

Big-name collabs often seem to bring a surge of player interest in Fortnite at the time of their announcement, and the Lil Wayne partnership is no exception. Such crossovers not only provide existing players another incentive to spend more time in the game but also draw some attention from potential players who may be intrigued because their favourite artist collaborated with the game.

In 2026 itself, we have seen major real-life celebs, such as Lil Wayne, Olivia Rodrigo, and Addison Rae, join the impressively vast list of Fortnite skins. With still a few months left, it will be exciting to see which famous personalities the game leverages next to boost its numbers.

FAQs

Can I get the Lil Wayne skin for free?

No, Lil Wayne can only be unlocked as a Fortnite outfit by spending V-Bucks in the Shop.

Which popular rappers have appeared in Fortnite before?

A variety of rappers, including Eminem, Travis Scott, Snoop Dogg, Ice Spice, and Lil Tecca, have been released as skins in the game so far.

Besides rappers, which popular musicians have appeared in Fortnite before?

Other non-rapper musicians in Fortnite who have their own in-game skin include Ariana Grande, The Weeknd, Sabrina Carpenter, Billie Eilish, Bruno Mars, Lisa, Metallica, and many more.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro vs iPhone 17 Pro: What’s the difference?

content.rendered:
The iPhone 18 Pro improves the camera, battery life, and sustained performance, but it is not a major redesign. Its biggest change is a variable-aperture main camera, followed by new video controls, a smaller Dynamic Island, and a 2TB storage option. The display size, optical zoom, front camera, materials, and core iOS experience remain familiar.

If you own an iPhone 17 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro makes sense if you will use its camera controls, need more battery, or regularly game and edit video on your phone. Otherwise, the iPhone 17 Pro still has a sharp 120Hz display, three 48MP rear cameras, and support for the same current iOS features. iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders are open, with sales starting September 18, so the comparison below uses Apple’s published specifications and claims rather than independent head-to-head testing.

iPhone 18 Pro vs iPhone 17 Pro at a glance

Apple’s India ratings for the nano-SIM/eSIM models differ from its U.S. eSIM figures: the 18 Pro is rated for up to 34 hours of video playback and 31 hours streamed, while the 17 Pro is rated for 31 and 28 hours. These are maximum playback estimates, not typical screen time.

Design and display: same size, smaller Dynamic Island

The two Pro models have the same dimensions and a 6.3-inch OLED display with 2622 × 1206 resolution, 460ppi, Always-On support, and ProMotion up to 120Hz. Both reach up to 3,000 nits outdoors and have an anti-reflective coating. You do not get a larger panel, sharper text, or a higher refresh rate by choosing the 18 Pro.

The main front-facing change is a smaller Dynamic Island. Apple says it can show up to three Live Activities at once, making timers, deliveries, and rides easier to check at a glance. The display itself remains the same size and resolution.

The 18 Pro uses the same aluminium unibody style as the 17 Pro and is available in black, silver, glacier, and burgundy. The 17 Pro comes in silver, Cosmic Orange, and Deep Blue. Both phones measure 71.9 × 150 × 8.75mm, but the 18 Pro weighs 211g. That is 5g more than the U.S. 17 Pro or 7g more than the India version, so the new model is slightly heavier in the hand despite matching its predecessor’s size.

Cameras: a more flexible main lens, familiar zoom cameras

The 48MP main camera is the biggest upgrade. The iPhone 18 Pro can change its aperture between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4. Its six-blade iris can open wider in dim light and narrow down when you want more of a group in focus. The camera can make that adjustment automatically, or you can choose an aperture yourself in the new Pro controls.

The iPhone 17 Pro has a 48MP main camera with a fixed ƒ/1.78 aperture. It still takes detailed photos and uses Night mode and computational photography, but it cannot physically change how much light the lens lets in or offer the same direct control over depth of field. Apple also says the 18 Pro uses a new main-camera sensor and processing pipeline for better low-light photos and detail; we will need retail camera comparisons to know how large that difference looks in everyday shots.

The other cameras are largely carried over. Both phones have a 48MP ultra-wide camera with a 120-degree field of view, a 48MP telephoto camera with 4× optical zoom and 8× optical-quality zoom, and an 18MP Centre Stage front camera. In other words, the 18 Pro does not give you a longer optical zoom or a better selfie camera. The 17 Pro already has a capable triple-48MP setup, as we explain in our guide to iPhone 17 Pro camera features.

The 18 Pro’s Camera app adds manual settings for aperture, shutter speed, and white balance, plus a histogram for checking exposure. Photographic Styles gain texture and grain controls alongside colour adjustments.

For video, Cinematic mode now records up to 4K Dolby Vision at 60fps, compared with 30fps on the 17 Pro, and you can apply Cinematic effects after capture to clips shot at up to 60fps. The 18 Pro also adds stabilised 4K Dolby Vision Time-lapse recording and raises the maximum digital video zoom from 15× to 24×. That extra zoom is digital cropping, not a new optical lens. The 17 Pro is still capable: both phones record regular 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 120fps with the main camera and support formats such as ProRes RAW and Apple Log 2.

For photographers who need to verify an image’s origin, the 18 Pro also adds opt-in Apple Reference Image capture, which stores signed sensor data with a reference image. Apple says capture will not be available at launch in China or the EU, making it a specialised tool rather than a mainstream upgrade reason.

Software and ecosystem: the 17 Pro gets the new features, too

The iPhone 18 Pro ships with iOS 27, but the 17 Pro is also on Apple’s iOS 27 compatibility list. Both phones can use the current software and stay in the same Apple ecosystem for features such as AirDrop, iCloud, and Apple Watch pairing.

Siri AI is not an 18 Pro exclusive. Apple’s supported-device list includes iPhone 16 models and later, which covers the 17 Pro. Siri AI is rolling out in beta, and some features vary by language and region, but buying the newer phone is not necessary just to get Apple’s latest assistant.

The 18 Pro’s faster Neural Engine may process supported on-device AI tasks more quickly, but that is a hardware-performance advantage rather than access to software the 17 Pro cannot run. For most owners, iOS and ecosystem features will feel more alike than different.

Performance and connectivity: more headroom for long sessions

The iPhone 18 Pro runs on A20 Pro, while the 17 Pro uses A19 Pro. Both chips have a six-core CPU, but the 18 Pro moves from a six-core to a seven-core GPU and uses a dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says A20 Pro is built on a 2-nanometer process, has 50% more memory bandwidth, offers up to 40% faster graphics, and doubles AI processing power compared with A19 Pro, according to its launch announcement.

Thermal management changes as well. The 17 Pro already has a vapour chamber; the 18 Pro’s redesigned chamber has three times the surface area, and Apple claims it enables up to 40% higher sustained performance. That could matter during long gaming, video-editing, or AI sessions, where heat can slow a phone down. It does not mean everyday tasks such as messaging or opening social apps will be 40% faster. These are Apple figures; independent retail-phone tests are still needed.

Wireless basics are similar: both use Apple’s N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread, and both support 5G. The cellular modem changes. An iFixit teardown identifies a Qualcomm modem in the 17 Pro, while Apple says the 18 Pro introduces its C2 modem with AI-assisted network-quality improvements. Apple’s faster-upload and lower-energy comparisons are against its C1X modem, not a direct 17 Pro test, so they do not establish how much better reception or battery life will be in real-world use. Wait for network tests before choosing between the phones on that basis.

Both retain USB-C with USB 3 data rates up to 10Gbps, plus MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging up to 25W. There is no major change to the ports or wireless-charging ceiling.

Battery and charging: three more rated hours, quicker wired top-ups

Apple rates the U.S. eSIM version of the 18 Pro for up to 36 hours of video playback and 33 hours of streamed video. The equivalent 17 Pro ratings are 33 and 30 hours. In India, Apple lists 34 and 31 hours for the nano-SIM/eSIM 18 Pro, versus 31 and 28 hours for the 17 Pro. The like-for-like gain is three hours in both comparisons.

Those numbers come from Apple’s playback tests, so they do not mean the 18 Pro will last exactly three hours longer during your normal day. Screen brightness, gaming, camera use, signal strength, and other factors affect battery life. Independent battery tests are still needed to show how much the rating difference translates to everyday use.

Wired charging is a clearer change: Apple estimates the 18 Pro can reach 50% in around 15 minutes with a 60W-capable adapter, while the 17 Pro needs around 20 minutes with a 40W-or-higher adapter. Both adapters are sold separately. Wireless charging is essentially unchanged: both phones support MagSafe and Qi2 up to 25W and can reach 50% in about 30 minutes with the required adapter and MagSafe charger.

Durability and long-term ownership: no new water-resistance rating

Both phones use an aluminium unibody, Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, and Ceramic Shield on the back. They also carry the same IP68 rating: up to 6 meters for 30 minutes in controlled conditions. The 18 Pro is not a durability upgrade over the 17 Pro. Apple notes that water resistance can decline with normal wear, and liquid damage is not covered under warranty, so treat the rating as protection against accidents rather than permission to take either phone swimming.

Apple says the 18 Pro uses 40% recycled material overall, including 85% recycled aluminium in its enclosure. The 17 Pro’s launch materials listed 30% recycled content. That is a manufacturing difference, not a claim that one phone is tougher or easier to repair.

Both phones can run iOS 27 today. In its EU product information, Apple lists a minimum of five years of operating-system security, corrective, and functionality updates for the 18 Pro and 17 Pro. The period is measured from when Apple stops placing each model on the market. That is not a promise of five major iOS releases, and Apple does not give a calendar end date for either phone’s support. The more concrete ownership advantage is storage: the 18 Pro adds a 2TB option for large photo and video libraries, while the 17 Pro tops out at 1TB.

Price and availability: the launch premium is $100 in the U.S.

In the U.S., the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, compared with the 17 Pro’s $1,099 launch price. In India, Apple’s current store listing starts at ₹1,64,900, while the 17 Pro launched at ₹1,34,900. The 17 Pro’s current price depends on retailer offers, so compare the quote you can actually get rather than treating its launch price as today’s price.

Pre-orders for the 18 Pro began on September 12, 2026, and availability begins September 18. The 17 Pro’s current price depends on the retailer, so compare the quote you can actually get. A substantial discount makes the older model attractive if you do not need variable aperture, the new video controls, or the 2TB tier. For more buying context, see our iPhone buying guide.

Which iPhone should you buy?

Keep the iPhone 17 Pro if its battery still gets you through the day, you like its camera, and you do not need the 2TB option. Its display, zoom cameras, front camera, iOS 27 support, and Pro video features remain current.

Choose the iPhone 18 Pro if you will use the variable aperture for low-light or group photos, want the new video controls, need faster wired charging and a longer battery rating, or often push the phone with games and editing. The modem may become another reason after independent testing, but Apple’s current claims do not provide a direct 17 Pro comparison.

For most iPhone 17 Pro owners, the 18 Pro is a worthwhile camera and endurance upgrade, not an urgent one. If you are buying your first Pro iPhone, the 18 Pro is the better-equipped model; a discounted 17 Pro can still be the better value for everyday use.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro vs Google Pixel 11 Pro: Which phone should you buy?

content.rendered:
The iPhone 18 Pro is the better fit if you already use an Apple Watch or Mac, or want its advanced video formats. The Google Pixel 11 Pro costs $100 less in the U.S. and adds Google’s camera and Gemini tools. Its 5x optical telephoto and 10x optical-quality zoom give it more reach on paper than the iPhone’s 4x optical and 8x optical-quality options, but neither spec sheet tells us which phone takes better zoomed photos.

The timing matters: Pixel 11 Pro has been on sale since August 25, while iPhone 18 Pro reaches stores September 18. Pixel has independent reviews; the iPhone has not had retail testing yet. If you’re deciding mainly on battery, camera quality, or sustained performance, wait for the first head-to-head tests.

iPhone 18 Pro vs Pixel 11 Pro: quick comparison

These are the U.S. list prices for each phone’s 256GB model. Brightness and battery figures come from different manufacturer tests, so treat them as specifications rather than direct wins.

Design and display: Pixel is lighter, iPhone is shorter

Both phones have a 6.3-inch screen and the same listed width. The Pixel is 7g lighter and 0.35mm thinner; the iPhone is 2.7mm shorter. Those are small differences, so try them in a case if weight or pocket fit matters to you.

Their materials differ. Apple uses an aluminium unibody with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back. Google pairs an aluminium frame with Gorilla Glass Victus 2 on both sides and a matte rear panel. Those glass names tell you what covers each phone, not which one is more likely to survive a drop.

On paper, the Pixel panel is denser at 495ppi versus 460ppi and has a higher listed peak brightness: 3,600 nits versus Apple’s 3,000-nit outdoor peak. Apple lists an anti-reflective coating; Google lists an anti-scratch screen shield. Both support adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz, so scrolling and animation should feel smooth. The brightness figures use different test conditions, though, and don’t settle which screen is easier to read outdoors.

In its display test, Tom’s Guide measured the Pixel at 2,860 nits. An Android Central reviewer also flagged the Pixel’s low-frequency PWM dimming, which may bother people sensitive to screen flicker. If OLED displays have caused you discomfort before, try the Pixel in person. No one has published a comparable retail iPhone 18 Pro test.

Cameras: Pixel has a longer native telephoto lens; iPhone adds aperture control

The Pixel’s dedicated telephoto camera starts at 5x optical zoom, compared with 4x on the iPhone. But both phones crop in further while advertising “optical-quality” reach: Pixel lists 10x and iPhone lists 8x. Google’s 120x Pro Zoom is digital, as is Apple’s zoom beyond 8x. Those high numbers help frame a faraway subject, but they aren’t a promise of clean detail. In TechRadar’s Pixel review, 120x results became hit-or-miss and more artificial as the reviewer pushed past about 30x.

The iPhone’s standout photo change is its variable-aperture 48MP main camera. It can switch among f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4, automatically or through manual controls. Opening the aperture lets in more light; closing it keeps more of a group or landscape in focus. The phone also gives you controls for shutter speed and white balance, plus ProRAW capture. This is more direct control on paper, but review samples will show how much it improves everyday photos.

Magic Capture is the Pixel’s standout tool for quick action, such as a child running or a pet jumping. Google says it analyses around 400 frames with on-device intelligence and Gemini, then saves a well-timed 12MP photo, applies edits such as crop and unblur, and keeps the video too. Android Central’s reviewer praised it after using it repeatedly. Camera Looks lets you adjust the image style before shooting. Google also says Instant Night Sight takes low-light photos up to 4.5 times faster than on Pixel 8, 9, and 10 models, though that doesn’t tell us how its night shots compare with the iPhone. Both phones can shoot close-ups: the Pixel has Macro Focus on its autofocus 48MP ultrawide, while the iPhone supports 48MP macro photos.

For video, the iPhone has the stronger list of creator formats: 4K Dolby Vision at up to 120fps on its main camera, Apple Log 2, and ProRes RAW. Recording ProRes at 4K120 requires an external drive, so that top-end mode isn’t a casual point-and-shoot setting. Pixel records standard 4K at up to 60fps and offers 8K24/30 through Video Boost, along with a teleprompter and tools for editing social clips. The 8K mode runs through the cloud rather than saving a finished 8K video right away. Google Photos backup is required, the recording is capped at 10 minutes, and boosting can take time. The Video Boost instructions say the initial clip is 1080p SDR. That’s a different workflow from the iPhone’s 4K recording formats, which are available directly in the camera app.

Pixel has a 42MP autofocus selfie camera with a wider field of view and 4K60 video. The iPhone’s 18MP Centre Stage camera can keep you framed during calls, and it supports tap-to-zoom and Dual Capture. Megapixels alone can’t tell us which takes more natural selfies; that will take side-by-side samples from a retail iPhone.

Performance: everyday speed looks fine on Pixel; gaming tests raise questions

The iPhone’s A20 Pro has a six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, and hardware ray tracing. Apple also added a vapour chamber and claims up to a 40% sustained-performance gain over the iPhone 17 Pro. Pixel 11 Pro runs Google’s Tensor G6, which powers its camera processing and on-device Gemini features.

In TechRadar’s review, a 512GB/16GB Pixel handled ordinary multitasking, streaming, and casual games well; the base model has 12GB of RAM. More demanding graphics are less settled: Tom’s Guide’s benchmarks show stronger CPU scores than the previous Pixel generation, but no comparable GPU improvement, and a separate gaming test on the Pixel 11 Pro XL found limited gains over last year’s model. Since that was the larger XL model, it doesn’t establish how the regular Pro handles heat over time. iPhone 18 Pro hasn’t reached reviewers yet, so no fair speed or gaming contest is available.

For messaging, photos, maps, and everyday games, neither phone should feel short on power. If you buy a flagship mainly for long gaming sessions or benchmark-leading performance, wait for retail tests instead of treating Apple’s chip claims or Google’s benchmark charts as a final verdict.

Software and AI: choose the assistant and ecosystem you want to live with

iPhone 18 Pro ships with iOS 27 and Apple’s Siri AI, which entered beta on September 14. Siri is meant to understand personal context and what’s on your screen, but Apple says language and region support vary; English is first, and Siri AI isn’t available on iOS in the EU at launch. Many Apple Intelligence tasks run on the device, while more complex requests can use Private Cloud Compute.

Pixel 11 Pro comes with Android 17 and Gemini Intelligence. Google says Gemini can handle supported multi-step tasks across more than 40 apps. Pixel tools include Circle to Search, Live Translate for supported videos, and Gemini-powered camera features. Rambler removes filler words from voice dictation, while proactive cards can surface relevant details such as a flight update. Google lists these features in its Pixel 11 overview; availability depends on language, country, age, app, and sometimes subscription. For a broader platform comparison, see how iOS 27 and Android 17 differ.

Your existing devices may matter more than either assistant. Apple Watch works only with iPhone, and Google’s Pixel Watch doesn’t support iOS. Pixel can send files to Apple devices through Quick Share and AirDrop compatibility, but the iPhone recipient has to set AirDrop visibility to “Everyone for 10 Minutes.” Apple’s Move to iOS setup can transfer much of your data when switching. This Android-to-iPhone transfer guide explains what moves over. To send files from Android to Apple, use AirDrop-compatible Quick Share.

Battery and charging: Pixel has real-world test results; iPhone does not yet

Google advertises 30-plus hours for Pixel 11 Pro. In Tom’s Guide’s continuous 5G browsing test, it lasted 13 hours and 25 minutes. Android Central’s 45W charging test reached 51% after 30 minutes, while Google’s own estimate is up to 55% in that time with a 30W-or-higher PPS charger. TechRadar’s reviewer said the Pixel got through a full day even with heavy video streaming or gaming, but needed an overnight charge.

Apple estimates up to 24 hours of typical use, 36 hours of local video playback, or 33 hours of streamed video for iPhone 18 Pro. Its fast-charge claim is up to 50% in around 15 minutes with a separately sold 60W-or-higher AVS adapter. MagSafe can reach 50% in 30 minutes with a 35W-or-higher adapter, and both MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging reach up to 25W. Google claims up to 55% in around 30 minutes with a separate 30W USB-C PPS charger; Pixelsnap/Qi2.2 wireless charging also goes up to 25W.

These runtime figures aren’t a fair head-to-head: Google and Apple use different definitions and test methods. The Pixel has retail battery tests already; the iPhone’s numbers are Apple’s estimates from preproduction testing. Neither phone includes a wall adapter, so add a compatible one to your budget if you don’t already own one. Wait for the same lab to test both before choosing based on battery life.

Durability and software support: Google publishes the clearer timeline

Both phones carry an IP68 rating. Apple specifies a maximum depth of 6 meters for 30 minutes, while Google doesn’t list a matching depth figure. IP68 isn’t a promise against every kind of water damage, and neither phone has a matched drop or scratch test. If a cracked screen would be expensive to replace, a case is still a sensible buy.

Google commits the Pixel 11 Pro to seven years of Android OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates, counted from its first U.S. Google Store availability in August 2026. Apple hasn’t announced a fixed support period for iPhone 18 Pro. Google’s promise is easier to plan around, but it doesn’t prove Apple’s phone will stop receiving updates sooner.

Price and availability: Pixel costs less, iPhone offers more storage

The Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099 for 256GB in the U.S.; iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for the same storage. These are list prices before trade-ins, carrier deals, tax, or limited-time offers. Apple’s options go up to 2TB, while Pixel tops out at 1TB, which may matter if you keep a large photo and video library on the phone. Both U.S. models are eSIM-only, so check carrier support if you usually swap physical SIM cards. Apple’s iPhone specs say that directly; Google lists the Pixel as eSIM-only in its Store FAQ, but gives conflicting physical-SIM wording elsewhere on the same page. Confirm the exact Pixel variant if a SIM tray is essential.

Pixel is available now. iPhone 18 Pro goes on sale September 18 in its first markets, with some regions following September 25. If you need a phone today, the Pixel is the ready-to-buy option. If you can wait a few days, the iPhone’s retail reviews should make the camera and battery trade-offs easier to judge.

Which phone should you buy?

  • Buy the Pixel 11 Pro if you want Android now, use Gemini or Google’s camera tools, want a 5x optical lens, or value a published seven-year update policy. It also saves $100 at the U.S. starting price.
  • Buy the iPhone 18 Pro if you own an Apple Watch or Mac, want up to 2TB of storage, or plan to shoot and edit video with Apple Log 2 or ProRes formats.
  • Wait for iPhone 18 Pro reviews if you don’t have a platform preference and care most about photo quality, gaming performance, or battery life. The Pixel’s zoom and price are concrete advantages, but the iPhone hasn’t had the retail testing needed to call an overall winner.

In case you missed:

  • iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra comparison
  • iPhone Duo vs Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra comparison
  • Apple A20 Pro vs A19 Pro

excerpt.rendered: The iPhone 18 Pro favors Apple’s ecosystem and pro video, while the Pixel 11 Pro offers 5x optical zoom, Gemini, seven years of updates, and a lower U.S. price.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro battery replacement now costs $129 out of warranty

content.rendered:
Apple has raised the U.S. out-of-warranty battery service fee for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max to $129. The new figure appears in Apple’s iPhone repair price table, up $10 from the $119 fee for the iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone 17 Pro Max.

The battery fee is the same for both Pro models

Apple lists the following U.S. out-of-warranty service estimates for the new Pro iPhones:

The battery is the only repair in the table that costs the same on both models. Apple says it will inspect the device before confirming the final service fee. Taxes may apply, mail-in service may add a shipping charge, and Apple Authorized Service Providers can set their own prices.

The increase follows last year’s iPhone 17 repair pricing, which listed a $119 battery replacement for the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max. Apple had kept that fee unchanged from the iPhone 16 Pro generation.

Apple has not explained the $10 increase

Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro models use updated battery designs, and the company rates the U.S. eSIM-only versions for up to 36 hours of video playback on the iPhone 18 Pro and 45 hours on the Pro Max. Apple has not said whether the new battery designs, parts, or service process are behind the higher replacement fee.

For the wider hardware picture, this iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max guide breaks down the new models’ battery and charging claims.

That distinction matters because the $129 price is a service estimate, not a published explanation of Apple’s repair costs. It also applies to the U.S. table. Repair prices and taxes can differ in other countries.

AppleCare+ can remove the battery fee

Apple says battery service is included at no extra charge for an AppleCare plan when the battery’s capacity drops below 80%. Normal battery wear is not covered by Apple’s standard limited warranty, so owners without qualifying coverage will see the out-of-warranty price instead.

Before booking a repair, check the battery health and coverage status. This guide to checking whether an iPhone battery needs replacing explains what to look for beyond the percentage shown in Settings.

The new $129 fee is still lower than replacing a phone that otherwise works well, but it makes the cost of keeping an iPhone 18 Pro for several years a little higher. Buyers outside the U.S. should use Apple’s local repair page for the price that applies to them.

title.rendered: WhatsApp is rolling out a new way to search messages on iPhone

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is finally making one of its most-used features easier to access on iPhone. The messaging app has started rolling out a new in-chat search button, giving users a quicker way to find old messages within a conversation. The feature follows several weeks of beta testing and is now reaching some iPhone users.

WhatsApp has been testing the search shortcut

The new search button isn’t completely unexpected. Early last month we reported that WhatsApp began testing the feature in its iOS beta, where the search shortcut appeared in the bottom-right corner of the in-chat interface.

Until now, searching within a conversation required several steps. I had to open the chat, tap the contact or group name at the top, choose the search option from the chat information screen, and then enter my query after being returned to the conversation.

That works, but it feels unnecessarily complicated when all I want to do is find one old message. The new shortcut removes that detour.

The button now appears while scrolling up

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has moved beyond testing and is officially rolling out the feature to users. Interestingly, the final version doesn’t appear in exactly the same place as the button shown during beta testing.

Now, the search shortcut appears at the top when users scroll up through a conversation. Tap the button, enter a keyword, and WhatsApp can search through the conversation without forcing me to navigate through multiple menus first.

When you return to the latest messages at the bottom, it disappears. That makes much more sense than permanently adding another icon to an already crowded interface.

The shortcut is also being made available across different types of conversations, including individual chats, group chats, and channels.

The rollout is gradual

As usual, the feature isn’t appearing for every iPhone user immediately. WhatsApp is gradually rolling it out, so even if you don’t see the new search button yet, that doesn’t necessarily mean anything is wrong with your app.

excerpt.rendered: The in-app search button removes a few annoying steps from finding your old WhatsApp chats.

For years, parental controls have felt like digital duct tape. Using Family Sharing, parents could set a few restrictions, limit screen time, and hope for the best. Meanwhile, kids were navigating an internet that has become faster, smarter, more addictive, and in many cases, more dangerous.

With iOS 27, Apple has expanded parental controls beyond simple screen-time limits. The new system lets parents manage app and website access, set flexible schedules and category-based time allowances, control who children can communicate with, and add approval steps before children visit new websites or connect with new contacts.

Here’s everything you need to know about the new child safety features in iOS 27.

The real problem was never screen time

The debate around kids and technology has been stuck in the wrong place for years. Parents have been obsessing over how many hours children spend on devices while ignoring a more important question: What are they actually doing during those hours?

A child might spend an hour on a homework app and another hour on a social platform. Treating both activities as identical simply because they consume the same amount of time doesn’t give parents much useful context.

iOS 27’s new controls reflect this by adding category-based allowances, schedules, website approvals, and communication controls alongside traditional Screen Time.

Ask to Browse adds approval before new websites

The standout feature in iOS 27 is called Ask to Browse. Instead of allowing unrestricted web access, children must request permission before visiting new websites in Safari. Parents receive the request in Messages and decide whether the site should be accessible.

Apple says Ask to Browse is turned on by default for Child Accounts under 13. Parents can also pre-approve websites.

Some people will immediately call this overprotective. They’re wrong. Nowadays children aren’t just stumbling onto inappropriate websites anymore. They’re encountering AI-generated content, manipulative recommendation systems, misinformation, scams, extremist content, and communities designed to keep them engaged at any cost.

Giving an 11-year-old unrestricted access is risky. Ask to Browse introduces friction. And sometimes friction is exactly what safety looks like. However, for children who are ready for broader browsing, Limit Adult Websites provides a less restrictive alternative that filters adult content.

Apple is moving from reactive parenting to preventive parenting

Most parental controls activate after something has already gone wrong, such as:

  • The child installs the wrong app.
  • A stranger sends a message.
  • An inappropriate image arrives.

Parents discover the issue later.

Apple is trying to flip that model. iOS 27 has redesigned the initial child-account setup experience. Parents can choose only the essential system apps, use a recommended set, or select the apps they consider appropriate. Apps can then be added over time as the child is ready for more access.

This works alongside Ask to Buy, which still lets parents approve eligible app downloads, purchases, and in-app purchases.

Time Allowances are smarter than traditional app limits

Parents have long had the option to block apps after a certain amount of usage. The problem? Real life doesn’t work that neatly. Sometimes a child genuinely needs more time for homework, communication, or creative projects.

Apple’s new Time Allowance system lets parents control the time their kids spend in apps across categories, including Entertainment, Games, and Social Media. It will show limits suggested by experts based on your child’s age. They can also grant additional app access when needed without dismantling their entire Screen Time setup.

Along with it, iOS 27 introduces Screen Time Schedules to manage which apps are available during periods such as Before School, School, and After School, and lets you create different routines for weekdays and weekends.

Parents can also allow certain apps and contacts at all times, so important communication or other selected services remain available even when a category allowance has been reached.

Communication Safety now covers gore and violent content

One of the most significant updates is Apple’s expansion of Communication Safety. The system already helped detect and intervene when sensitive and explicit images were shared.

Now, it can blur images and videos containing detected gore or violent content in Messages and FaceTime for users under 18. The child encounters a safety intervention before viewing that potentially disturbing material.

That’s a bigger deal than it sounds. The modern internet isn’t just exposing children to sexual content. Violence has become normalized across social platforms, messaging apps, and viral content feeds.

iOS 27 also lets parents manage contacts for Phone, Messages, and FaceTime. A parent can require permission before a child connects with someone new, and the approval request can be reviewed from the parent’s device.

The redesigned Screen Time puts controls closer to the surface

Let’s be honest. Screen Time for the child’s account was basic. The data was there, but the insights weren’t.

Apple has redesigned the parental Screen Time experience to provide an at-a-glance view of a child’s device usage and most-used apps. Parents can use quick actions to adjust access in the moment instead of digging through multiple settings screens.

For example, parents can quickly pause or change access during meals, outdoor activities, or other periods when they want the device to take a back seat.

More requests can now arrive directly in Messages

The new approval workflow brings several child requests into one place. Depending on the settings, a child can request a new app or purchase, access to a new Safari website, additional device time, or permission to communicate with a new contact. Parents can approve or decline eligible requests from Messages or directly on the child’s device.

What parents should take away

iOS 27 doesn’t replace conversations, trust, or active parenting, but it gives families considerably more control over the digital environment around a child. Apple’s latest child safety features go beyond simply counting minutes by adding controls for websites, apps, schedules, app categories, communication, and sensitive content.

The most useful change for many families is the ability to start with a narrower set of apps and websites and gradually expand access. Parents can also make one-off approvals without completely changing the underlying setup.

If you’re setting up these controls now, update every device in the Family Sharing group to the latest iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27, where applicable. Then review the child’s allowed apps and websites, communication contacts, Time Allowances, and daily schedules.

You can even get help from Apple’s dedicated Child Safety website.
