title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Which flagship is better?

content.rendered:
Apple has launched its next Pro model, the iPhone 18 Pro, bringing a new A20 Pro chip, camera upgrades, iOS 27, and several other improvements. But it enters a market where Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra is already one of the most feature-packed flagship phones available.

So, how does Apple’s latest Pro iPhone compare with Samsung’s Ultra flagship? I’m putting the iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra side by side to see how they compare in design, display, performance, cameras, battery life, AI features, software, and pricing and which one deserves your money.

iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Specs comparison

Before getting into the experience of using these phones, here’s a quick comparison.

On the surface, Samsung appears to throw more hardware at me. But I wouldn’t make a buying decision from this table alone.

Design and build quality: Which feels more premium?

The first thing I’d notice switching between these phones is the size.

The iPhone 18 Pro is the easier phone to live with physically. Its 6.3-inch display makes it considerably more manageable than Samsung’s 6.9-inch Ultra. I can see myself comfortably using it one-handed, slipping it into a pocket and forgetting I’m carrying a Pro-level phone.

Apple offers the iPhone 18 Pro in black, silver, glacier, and the new burgundy finish. Galaxy S26 Ultra comes in four colours: Cobalt Violet, Sky Blue, White, and Black, along with two online exclusives: Shadow Silver and Pink Gold.

Another thing that caught my attention is the difference in thickness and weight. The Galaxy S26 Ultra measures just 7.9mm thick and weighs 214g, while the iPhone 18 Pro is 8.75mm thick and weighs 211g. In other words, the Samsung flagship is 0.85 mm thinner, but it’s just 3 g heavier than Apple’s smaller Pro model.

When it comes to protection, both phones use premium glass. The iPhone 18 Pro uses Ceramic Shield, which Apple designed to improve durability and help protect the phone from everyday drops and scratches. As for the Samsung flagship, the back of the phone is made from Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2.

My verdict: iPhone 18 Pro for comfort. Galaxy S26 Ultra for its slimmer design and larger form factor.

Display: Is bigger really better?

The display is one of the first things I notice when switching between two flagship phones, and both Apple and Samsung have opted for premium panels here. However, they take very different approaches.

The iPhone 18 Pro has a 6.3-inch OLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate. Its compact size is actually what I like about the device. The display is brighter, and the adaptive refresh rate makes scrolling and animations feel smooth. And it’s also easier to hold while typing or handling the device with just one hand.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra, on the other hand, is the one I’d pick for watching movies, gaming, browsing, or getting work done. Its 6.9-inch QHD+ display gives me noticeably more screen space, and Samsung’s Dynamic AMOLED 2X panel delivers the kind of punchy colours and deep blacks I expect from an Ultra phone.

Samsung also has another interesting advantage: Privacy Display. It can make the screen harder for people around me to see from an angle, which could be genuinely useful when I’m checking private messages or working on sensitive information in a crowded place.

My display verdict: Galaxy S26 Ultra wins.

Performance: A20 Pro vs Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5

This is the section where I would tell readers not to get obsessed with benchmark charts.

The iPhone 18 Pro is powered by Apple’s A20 Pro, while Samsung uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy.

The A20 Pro is particularly interesting because it is built using a 2nm process. It has a 6-core CPU with two new Super cores and four efficiency cores, along with a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators. Compared to the A19 Pro, the new Super cores can be up to 20% faster, while the GPU can deliver up to 40% faster graphics performance.

Apple has also given the A20 Pro a Dual 16-core Neural Engine to handle demanding on-device AI tasks and computational photography. What I find more interesting is that Apple isn’t only chasing peak performance. The iPhone 18 Pro has a new vapour-chamber cooling system to keep the A20 Pro running at high performance for longer periods.

Unlike Apple’s 6-core CPU, Snapdragon uses an octa-core CPU, with two high-performance Oryon cores and six performance cores. It is built on a 3nm process and is paired with Qualcomm’s Adreno 840 GPU.

Samsung has also tuned the chip specifically for the Galaxy S26 Ultra to deliver up to a 19% CPU performance improvement, 24% greater graphics processing and 39% faster NPU performance compared with the previous generation. I also like that Samsung gives the S26 Ultra up to 16GB of RAM,

That combination makes the S26 Ultra particularly interesting for gaming, multitasking and AI-heavy workloads.

The early benchmark results give the A20 Pro a clear lead in CPU performance.

The difference is particularly noticeable in single-core performance, where the A20 Pro is roughly 25% ahead of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy based on these results. Multi-core performance is much closer, but the iPhone still has the lead.

Which one feels faster?

I wouldn’t say one is simply “faster.”

The A20 Pro benefits from Apple’s tight control over the hardware and software stack. That matters for things such as:

  • Video editing
  • Gaming optimization
  • Camera processing
  • AI workloads
  • App performance
  • Sustained performance

My verdict: I would choose the A20 Pro for optimised performance and Apple’s ecosystem.

Camera comparison

This is where the iPhone 18 Pro vs Galaxy S26 Ultra comparison gets really interesting.

Samsung is still playing the hardware and versatility game. Apple is taking a more computational and creator-focused approach.

The iPhone 18 Pro gets a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, which is one of the biggest camera changes Apple has made in years. The aperture can move between f/1.48 and f/4.0, giving the camera more control over light and depth of field. The phone also gets new Pro camera controls.

The system includes:

  • 48MP Fusion Main
  • 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide
  • 48MP Fusion Telephoto
  • 4x optical and up to 8x optical-quality zoom

I particularly like the variable-aperture approach because it gives the camera a physical control that smartphone photography has largely avoided.

Samsung takes the “give me everything” approach.

The S26 Ultra includes:

  • 200MP main camera
  • 50MP ultrawide
  • 10MP 3x telephoto
  • 50MP 5x telephoto
  • Digital zoom up to 100x

And this is where Samsung has the advantage for me. If I’m travelling, shooting a concert, photographing architecture from a distance, or simply want more flexibility when framing a subject, those dedicated zoom cameras matter.

The 3x and 5x telephoto cameras give me options that a single telephoto system can’t replicate as effectively. However, more megapixels do not automatically mean better photos.

  • For zoom and versatility, I’d pick the Galaxy S26 Ultra.
  • For video, I’d lean toward the iPhone 18 Pro for its Dolby Vision recording, Smart Focus Tracking, and Audio Mix.
  • For everyday photography, I’d want to compare identical real-world shots before declaring a winner because both companies process images very differently.

Battery life and charging

Samsung S26 Ultra has the obvious hardware advantage here with a 5,000mAh battery. It also supports up to 60W wired charging and reverse wireless charging, which can be useful for topping up Galaxy Buds or another compatible device.

Apple takes a different approach. Rather than competing directly on battery capacity, it combines its silicon, operating system, and battery architecture to maximise efficiency.

The iPhone 18 Pro delivers major battery-life improvements, with the A20 Pro and updated battery design working together to deliver up to 36 hours of video playback. However, Samsung lists only up to 31 hours of video playback for the S26 Ultra.

My verdict: If I’m gaming for hours, navigating with GPS, recording lots of video and streaming content, I’d be more comfortable choosing the iPhone 18 Pro.

Software and ecosystem: iOS 27 vs One UI

When you are buying a $1,200-plus smartphone, you are often buying into an ecosystem, not just buying a phone.

The iPhone 18 Pro ships with iOS 27, which brings the new generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. One feature I find particularly interesting is Siri mode in the Camera app. I can point the camera at something, ask Siri about what I’m seeing, and get information or take an action based on it.

But for me, Apple’s biggest advantage remains the ecosystem.

If you already own:

  • MacBook
  • iPad
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods
  • Apple TV

Then an iPhone is just a more intuitive and sensible choice. AirDrop, Handoff, iCloud, Messages, FaceTime, and cross-device continuity create an experience that’s difficult for Samsung to duplicate. This is the very reason why I would recommend this device to existing Apple users.

Samsung takes the opposite approach. One UI is designed for people who want more control.

I can:

  • Customise the interface
  • Run multiple apps in split-screen
  • Use Samsung DeX
  • Take handwritten notes with S Pen
  • Share images directly with contacts using Quick Share.
  • Customise more aspects of the phone
  • Broadcast audio or even my voice to compatible nearby LE Audio devices using Auracast

Samsung has also committed to seven years of OS and security updates for the Galaxy S26 series.

My verdict: iOS 27 wins for simplicity and ecosystem integration. One UI wins for customisation and power users.

AI features: Apple Intelligence vs Galaxy AI

AI has become one of the biggest selling points of flagship phones, but I think this is one area where buyers should be careful. I don’t care how many AI features appear in a launch presentation. I care whether I actually use them.

Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro introduces the next generation of Apple Intelligence, including a new Siri AI designed to understand personal context, recognise what’s on screen and perform actions across apps. Apple is also emphasising privacy through on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute.

Other meaningful additions include:

  • Dedicated Siri app: Revisit previous Siri conversations and continue them across Apple devices using iCloud.
  • Write with Siri: Describe what you want to write and have Siri create or refine a draft.
  • New AI photo editing: Spatial Reframing, Extend, and an upgraded Clean Up tool give me more ways to edit photos after taking them.
  • Image Playground improvements: Create more realistic AI-generated images.

Samsung’s Galaxy AI is more aggressively integrated into the phone’s everyday workflows.

The S26 Ultra brings the new Bixby as a more conversational device agent. Instead of remembering the exact name of a setting, I can describe what I want in normal language, and Bixby can identify the appropriate setting or action. It can also search the web for up-to-date information directly within Bixby.

Also, Photo Assist lets you make multiple AI-powered photo edits without saving each version individually; you can then review the editing history and choose which versions to keep.

Samsung is also leaning heavily into AI-powered productivity and cross-app actions and integrating services such as Gemini and Perplexity. And that’s where I give Samsung the edge.

My verdict: Galaxy S26 Ultra wins for breadth and practical AI tools.

Connectivity and extra features

At this price, both phones have everything I expect from a modern flagship.

Both offer:

  • 5G
  • Wi-Fi 7
  • Bluetooth
  • NFC
  • USB-C
  • UWB

But the extras are where Samsung starts pulling away.

The S26 Ultra gives me:

  • S Pen
  • Samsung DeX
  • Privacy Display
  • Reverse wireless charging
  • Ultrasonic fingerprint scanner
  • Extensive multitasking
  • Android customization

The S Pen is still one of Samsung’s biggest differentiators. This allows me to take down my handwritten notes, edit my photos, annotate documents, and navigate precisely. I don’t have to buy a separate accessory and remember to carry it.

Apple’s biggest extras are ecosystem-related:

  • Face ID
  • MagSafe
  • AirDrop
  • Apple Watch integration
  • Mac continuity
  • Advanced camera controls
  • LiDAR
  • Apple’s satellite and emergency features where supported

So I see the difference this way: Samsung gives me more features on the phone itself, whereas Apple gives me a better-connected collection of devices.

My verdict: Galaxy S26 Ultra wins for individual features. iPhone wins if I already live inside Apple’s ecosystem.

Price and value for money

The iPhone 18 Pro begins at $1,199 for 256 GB in the US. Apple also provides promotional offers from eligible carriers, trade-in credits, and its Apple Upgrade leasing option. Eligible carrier deals can provide up to $1,200 in credits for certain iPhone 14 or newer trade-ins, depending on eligibility.

Samsung’s regular U.S. pricing starts at $1,299.99 for the 256GB Galaxy S26 Ultra, with 512GB and 1TB versions going higher. Samsung is also advertising trade-in incentives.

The iPhone 18 Pro is cheaper at standard pricing. But the Galaxy S26 Ultra becomes compelling once discounts are applied.

iPhone 18 Pro vs Galaxy S26 Ultra: Which one should you buy?

After looking at the two phones category by category, I don’t think there is a universal winner. And that’s actually a good thing. These phones are aimed at slightly different people.

I’d buy the iPhone 18 Pro if I:

  • Already own a MacBook or iPad.
  • Wear an Apple Watch or use AirPods.
  • Want a smaller flagship.
  • Care heavily about video recording.
  • Prefer iOS.
  • Want the new variable-aperture camera.
  • Want up to 2TB of storage.
  • Don’t need a built-in stylus.

The iPhone 18 Pro is the phone I’d recommend to someone who says, “I want a Pro iPhone, but I don’t want a giant phone.” That’s where Apple’s strategy makes perfect sense.

You should buy the Galaxy S26 Ultra if you:

  • Want the biggest display possible.
  • Take lots of zoom photos.
  • Want the S Pen.
  • Multitask heavily and want Samsung DeX.
  • Like Android customisation.
  • Want a large battery.
  • Use a Windows PC more than a Mac.
  • Want Samsung’s broader AI toolkit.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra is the phone I’d recommend to someone who wants a powerhouse.

My final verdict

If I had to spend my own money today, I’d pick the Galaxy S26 Ultra as the better overall flagship. It gives me a larger and more versatile display, more flexible camera hardware, S Pen, stronger productivity features, a large battery, and an extensive set of AI tools.

But I wouldn’t call the iPhone 18 Pro a worse phone. I’d call it the better choice for a specific kind of buyer.

If you already owned a MacBook, Apple Watch, and AirPods, the iPhone 18 Pro would be my pick. The ecosystem advantage is too significant to ignore. Buy the iPhone 18 Pro if you want a compact Pro iPhone, excellent video capabilities, and seamless Apple ecosystem integration.

The most important takeaway from this comparison: the best flagship isn’t necessarily the phone with the most impressive spec sheet. It’s the phone that fits the way I already live.

title.rendered: Apple Car Key code hints at support for Lincoln, Freelander, and Lucid

content.rendered:
Apple may be preparing to expand Car Key support to Lincoln, Freelander, and Lucid. Aaron Perris spotted the three automakers in Apple’s backend code, but the discovery does not include a release date, compatible vehicle list, or confirmation from Apple.

It is also not a first-time support announcement for every brand. Apple’s current public vehicle list already shows Car Key support for certain Lincoln and Lucid models, while Freelander does not appear on the list. The code may point to additional models, markets, or a staged rollout.

What the code discovery shows

The names appeared in a September 15 post from Aaron Perris. Similar backend references have preceded other Car Key additions, but code alone cannot tell us when a feature will launch or which vehicles will support it.

The discovery follows earlier references to GWM Tank and Haval. Our previous report on Volkswagen’s planned Apple Wallet car key support explains why these backend findings can be useful clues while still falling short of an announcement.

Apple’s public compatibility list currently marks selected Lincoln vehicles and Lucid entries as supporting car keys. Freelander is not listed there. That leaves several possibilities: Apple could be preparing more models from an already supported brand, adding support in another market, or getting the backend ready before an official rollout.

How Apple Car Key works

Car Key lives in the Wallet app. With a compatible vehicle, an iPhone or Apple Watch can lock, unlock, and start the car. Depending on the automaker and model, it can also support passive entry, remote locking, trunk controls, or sharing a key with another person.

Apple says setup usually begins in the automaker’s app, an email, or the vehicle’s display. After the key is added to Wallet, Express Mode may let you use it without opening the app or authenticating every time. The exact behavior depends on the vehicle.

Apple Support lists an iPhone XS or later, or an iPhone SE (2nd generation) or later, and a compatible Apple Watch as the usual device requirements. The phone and watch need to be signed in to the Apple Account associated with the key. Apple also says some functions vary by region and manufacturer, so a supported brand does not automatically mean every trim supports every feature.

When could the new support arrive?

There is no confirmed launch date for Lincoln, Freelander, or Lucid based on this code discovery. Apple and the automakers would still need to announce supported vehicles and make the feature available through software, vehicle systems, or an automaker app.

For now, owners should check Apple’s available vehicle list and the automaker’s instructions rather than assuming a particular car will work. The backend references are a sign that more Car Key support may be on the way, not a promise that it is ready to use.

For a broader look at Apple’s Wallet updates, see our guide to new iOS 26 Wallet app features.

title.rendered: Apple explains how iPhone 18 Pro’s Reference Image mode verifies photos

content.rendered:
Apple has explained the security system behind Apple Reference Image, an opt-in camera mode on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. It is designed to preserve evidence of the pixels the camera sensor captured, even as synthetic and edited images become harder to distinguish from originals.

Reference Image can help verify a photo’s capture history. It cannot prove that the scene itself was real or that the subject in front of the camera was genuine.

The camera signs the pixels immediately

In a technical post from Apple’s Security Research team, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro’s main camera sensor boots into a specialized Reference Image mode. The sensor cryptographically signs the pixel data immediately after capture and prevents firmware from changing it first.

The sensor metadata is signed too. The Secure Enclave Processor adds its own signature to device-generated information, such as the focal length and the boundaries used for digital zoom. Together, those records form a protected digital negative containing the pixels, sensor details, and secure timestamp bounds.

Apple’s timestamp system is designed to show when the image could have been captured. The device receives a cryptographic timestamp token through an Apple Push Notification service heartbeat, then asks for another token after taking the photo. Apple says the heartbeat averages about every 15 minutes, though network conditions can change that interval.

Private Cloud Compute develops the reference image

The signed digital negative is sent to Private Cloud Compute for steps such as demosaicing, tone mapping, and compression. Apple says the service can be verified through device attestation and an append-only log, while the system is designed to keep the image data private.

Apple says the final signature combines RSA-3072 with ML-DSA-87, a post-quantum signature algorithm. That technical combination matters less to most people than the result: the finished Reference Image is tied to signed sensor data instead of being an ordinary image file that can be silently changed after capture.

In Photos, the reference version appears alongside the regular photo. Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro announcement says developers can also work with the format through APIs on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.

What Reference Image can and cannot prove

The mode can help answer whether the pixels came from a compatible iPhone sensor and whether the signed capture data has been altered. It can also expose edits that break the provenance record.

It does not establish that the scene was truthful. If you photograph an AI-generated image on another screen, Reference Image can show that your iPhone sensor captured those pixels. It cannot tell you whether the face, document, or event shown on that screen was authentic.

That distinction is important. The feature is closer to a signed digital negative than a truth detector. For ordinary photos, our guide on how to get photo metadata on an iPhone explains what information a photo can carry and how to inspect it.

How to turn it on

Reference Image is opt-in and works through the iPhone 18 Pro main camera. Apple Support lists these steps:

  1. Open Settings and tap Camera.
  2. Tap Reference Image, then Add Reference Mode.
  3. Open Camera and swipe to Reference.
  4. Take the photo.

The mode is not available in every region. Apple says capture is unavailable in the European Union and China at launch, although people in the EU can still develop and view reference images on supported Apple devices. Check Apple’s current Reference Image instructions if the setting does not appear.

For more camera and hardware context, see our iPhone 18 Pro guide. Reference Image is a useful provenance feature, but its strongest claim is narrow: it helps show what the sensor captured, not whether the world looked exactly as the image suggests.

title.rendered: Apple’s M6 and M5 Ultra benchmark scores hint at fast new Macs

content.rendered:
Fresh Geekbench 7 results offer an early look at the Apple M6 and M5 Ultra chips headed for the new Mac mini and Mac Studio. The M6 result is stronger in single-core work, while the M5 Ultra result is more than twice as fast in multi-core work.

These are individual public benchmark uploads, not Apple-confirmed retail tests. They are useful for setting expectations, but they do not tell us how either chip will perform in sustained workloads or everyday apps.

M6 beats M5 Ultra in single-core

The Apple M6 Geekbench 7 result shows 4,071 in single-core and 22,783 in multi-core. Geekbench identifies the machine as Mac18,5 with a 12-core chip and 32GB of memory.

The M5 Ultra result shows 3,774 in single-core and 52,516 in multi-core. The record identifies a Mac17,15 with a 36-core chip and 256GB of memory.

The M6 score is about 8% higher in single-core. That kind of result can point to quicker response in lightly threaded tasks, such as opening apps or handling short bursts of work. The M5 Ultra’s multi-core score is about 2.3 times higher, which is the more relevant number for heavily parallel tasks such as large video exports, 3D rendering, and some AI workloads.

The comparison is not a fair contest between equal machines. M6 is a mainstream desktop chip for the Mac mini, while M5 Ultra is a workstation-class part designed for the Mac Studio. The large difference in CPU core count explains much of the multi-core gap.

What Apple has announced

Apple says M6 is the first Apple silicon chip built using a second-generation 2-nanometer process. It has up to a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU, and a 32-core Neural Engine. Apple says M5 Ultra scales to 36 CPU cores, 80 GPU cores, and up to 512GB of unified memory.

The new Mac mini and Mac Studio are scheduled to become available on September 22. If you are weighing the two products, our M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio comparison breaks down the more important differences, including size, memory, ports, and intended workloads.

The benchmark records do not show GPU scores, so they cannot tell us whether the M6 Mac mini is a better choice for graphics work or how the M5 Ultra handles demanding visual tasks. Apple’s launch claims also use different comparison points and workloads, so they should not be mixed with these Geekbench numbers as if they were one test.

Wait for independent testing before buying

Geekbench measures a short CPU workload. A public upload can show the performance of one pre-release or early system, but it cannot settle questions about fan noise, sustained speed, power use, thermals, storage, or app compatibility. It also does not show how the Mac mini and Mac Studio feel in normal use.

For now, the numbers suggest a simple split. M6 may offer excellent quick, single-core performance in a compact Mac mini. M5 Ultra is in another class when an application can use many CPU cores at once. The history of Mac processors puts that generational jump in a broader context.

The new Macs arrive September 22. Anyone buying on day one should wait for retail reviews if sustained performance, graphics, or thermals matter more than a single Geekbench result.

title.rendered: iPhone Duo vs Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra comparison: Which foldable should you buy?

content.rendered:
After years of anticipation, Apple has finally hopped onto the foldable smartphone bandwagon with the iPhone Duo. It’s the company’s first foldable that combines the classic Apple experience with the new A20 Pro chipset, a massive 7.6-inch foldable display, and several other flagship-grade features.

However, Apple isn’t entering an empty arena. Samsung has spent years polishing its foldable lineup, with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 now standing as the biggest name in the category.

So, if you’re planning to upgrade to a flagship foldable, here’s a detailed iPhone Duo vs. Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra comparison that breaks down everything you need to know to make the right call.

iPhone Duo vs Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra: Quick specs

Design and build

If a bigger display is your priority, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold Ultra 8 should be an obvious choice. It features an 8-inch inner display, which is slightly larger than iPhone Duo’s 7.6-inch screen, and its 6.5-inch cover display also beats Apple’s 5.4-inch outer screen. On paper, the extra screen size will make everyday tasks such as taking notes, typing, and multitasking much easier.

However, there are a few things to consider. When folded, the iPhone Duo is more compact and easier to hold in one hand. Not only that, but it features a matte coating for the inner display, which reduces creases and reflections. Although the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra comes with an anti-reflection coating, it doesn’t do quite as much to address these issues. The iPhone Duo also has the advantage of Apple Pencil support.

When it comes to the build quality, the iPhone Duo has a straight edge. It features a titanium frame with Cermaic shield, alongside an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance. This certainly makes the iPhone Duo heavier, but it gives it a more premium look compared to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, which comes with Armour Aluminium, Gorilla Glass, and an IP48 rating.

So, if you want a bigger screen and a lighter device, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is the better choice. However, if you want a more premium build, a better in-hand experience, and Apple Pencil support, the iPhone Duo is a far better option.

Cameras

The Samsung Z Fold 8 Ultra is far more versatile compared to the iPhone Duo when it comes to cameras, especially on the rear. The foldable features a 200MP main camera, a 50MP Ultrawide camera, and a dedicated 10 MP 3x telephoto lens. It also supports video recording at up to 8 K.

On the other hand, iPhone Duo features a double 40MP rear setup which consists of a primary and an ultrawide lens. It also supports Dolby Vision HDR, spatial video, and ProRes recording. However, the fact that the iPhone Duo lacks a dedicated telephoto lens puts it at a disadvantage when it comes to photographing distant subjects, where Samsung’s 3x optical zoom can deliver much better clarity and detail.

For video calls and selfies, the Samsung Z Fold 8 Ultra has a 10MP ultrawide camera on the inner display and a 10MP cover camera. However, the iPhone Duo comes with an under-display camera and a 12MP cover camera, which offers greater functionality.

If zooming capabilities and overall versatility of the camera are your priority, you can’t go wrong with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. However, for those who want better video recording, FaceTime, and professional camera features, the iPhone Duo will be the better option.

Performance and battery

When we talk about the iPhone Duo, it is powered by Apple’s A20 Pro Chip, which is also found in the iPhone 18 Pro. The chipset includes a six-core CPU, a seven-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a dual 16-core Neural Engine. On the other hand, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra packs Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5.

As of now, there are no benchmark tests available for the A20 Pro, so it’s hard to determine which device offers better overall performance. However, Apple’s A-series chips have traditionally outperformed Qualcomm’s Snapdragon processors in areas such as single-core performance and power efficiency.

Apple hasn’t revealed the exact battery capacity for iPhone Duo, instead claiming that it can last 24 hours in everyday use, with 31 hours of video playback on the inner screen and 44 hours of video playback on the outer screen. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra comes with a 5,000 mAh battery, which should provide enough juice for a full day of heavy use.

Charging speeds are fairly similar between both foldables. Apple states that the iPhone Duo can reach 50% charge when paired with a 60W charger in just 20 minutes. When it comes to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, Samsung claims the device can reach 67% in just 30 minutes using a 45W charger. However, keep in mind that the iPhone Duo doesn’t come with a charger in the box, so that needs to be purchased separately.

Software experience

Software can make or break the experience of a foldable, regardless of the hardware powering it. The iPhone Duo comes out of the gate with iOS 27, which has been redesigned for the foldable form factor. It brings features such as Split View, app pairs, adaptive layouts, and other foldable-focused improvements. It also benefits from the overall Apple ecosystem, including Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features.

The Samsung Z Fold Ultra 8 runs on One UI 9 based on Android 17. Samsung has spent years refining its software experience for foldable devices, and the experience shows. Users can run multiple apps side by side, and even use three-way split-screen layouts, which make the foldable useful for multitasking.

Ultimately, software preference is a personal choice. However, the iPhone Duo offers a cleaner and familiar experience, especially if you’re someone deep within the Apple ecosystem. If you own devices such as a MacBook, iPad, or Apple Watch, the foldable will fit right into the ecosystem. Features such as AirDrop, FaceTime, and Continuity make switching between multiple Apple devices feel like a breeze, which gives the Duo an advantage that Android foldables can struggle to replicate.

Storage and pricing

The iPhone Duo vs. Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra debate can go for hours, but one thing’s for certain: they both are not cheap. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model, with financing available for $83.29 over 12 months. Pre-orders for the foldable will begin in the U.S. on October 23.

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold Ultra 8 starts at $2,099 for 256GB of storage and is already available for purchase. However, buyers can get the foldable cheaper with the help of store promotions and trade-in offers.

Which foldable should you buy?

After comparing the iPhone Duo and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra across multiple factors, the next question is: which one should you buy? Well, the answer isn’t as straightforward as you might think, and the right choice depends on what you value the most in a foldable.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra makes more sense if you:

  • want a device focused on productivity and multitasking
  • plan to use Samsung DeX
  • want a larger outer and inner display
  • want more versatile camera hardware with zooming capabilities
  • want a light foldable for everyday use
  • need to buy a foldable immediately
  • prefer Android and Samsung’s ecosystem

The iPhone Duo can be a better purchase if you:

  • already have Apple products such as Mac, iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch
  • want stronger performance for demanding tasks and apps
  • want a foldable with higher durability
  • want to use Apple Pencil USB-C.
  • plan to use your phone for several years.

If I had to pick between these foldables, I’d personally go with the iPhone Duo. Its video recording capabilities, durable build, and integration with the existing Apple ecosystem give it multiple advantages for everyday use. Still, though, the Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 Ultra is solid for anyone who wants to multitask and take advantage of the flexibility of Android.

title.rendered: Fortnite x Ironmouse crossover: Everything you need to know

content.rendered:
There’s no shortage of wild crossovers in Fortnite, and now Epic Games is teaming up with none other than a popular VTuber, Ironmouse. The upcoming collaboration is all set to bring an Ironmouse skin, a sword pickaxe, and many other themed cosmetics to the game. So, if you’re hyped, here’s everything you need to know about the Ironmouse Fortnite crossover, including its release date and all the content it’s expected to bring to the table.

Fortnite x Ironmouse crossover release date & time

It’s time to mark your calendars, gamers, as the Fortnite x Ironmouse crossover will drop on September 18, 2026, as confirmed by the streamer through a teaser tweet. Everything that’s coming with the crossover, including the new items and cosmetics, will be released with the regular Item Shop reset. This happens at 5:00 PM PT, but if you’re unsure what time that translates to in your region, here’s a table to help you out –

What’s coming with Fortnite x Ironmouse crossover? 

The previous Fortnite Ironmouse Sprite collaboration certainly made an impact on the community, so it’s hardly a shock to see the popular VTuber return for another crossover.

Although the developer hasn’t officially revealed everything the crossover will include, the teasers that’ve been shared across Fortnite’s official social media channels have given us a good idea of what to expect. This includes the likes of an Ironmouse skin and a sword-style pickaxe.

Not only that, but reputable leakers such as FN_Assist have also shared details about additional cosmetics and items that could be available to purchase. Here’s what the Fortnite Ironmouse crossover is expected to include –

  • Ironmouse Icon Series Skin
  • Decora Mouse Skin
  • 2 Emotes
  • 1 Pickaxe
  • 1 Guitar
  • Additional items

All of these items we’ve mentioned above are expected to be a part of the Ironmouse Fortnite bundle. If you’re planning to grab them all, better save up, as the bundle is likely to cost somewhere between 2,000 and 2,800 V-Bucks. It’s likely that players will be able to purchase the cosmetics separately instead of opting for the full bundle.

However, it’s not necessary to spend V-Bucks to get the Ironmouse Fortnite skin. It can be unlocked for free by taking part in the Ironmouse Cup, which kicks off on September 15, 2026, at 8:00 AM PT.

Rounding up

The Fortnite x Ironmouse crossover is going to release on September 18, 2026. Based on everything we’ve seen from the official teasers and leaks, the crossover will bring special skins, back blings, pickaxes, emotes, and much more! So, for the fans of the popular VTuber, this is one Fortnite crossover that shouldn’t be missed.

FAQs

1. How to get Ironmouse skin in Fortnite for free?

Players can get the Ironmouse skin for free in Fortnite by securing a high finish in the Ironmouse Cup.

2. Is Ironmouse Sprite coming back?

Epic Games hasn’t confirmed whether the Ironmouse Sprite will return with the upcoming crossover.

3. How many V-Bucks will the Ironmouse skin cost?

It’s likely that the Ironmouse skin in Fortnite will cost 1,500 V-Bucks.

title.rendered: Best iPhone Duo accessories I’d actually buy

content.rendered:
The iPhone Duo is finally here, bringing Apple’s foldable design to the iPhone lineup. But a new form factor with two displays also means you need to rethink the accessories you buy, from cases and screen protectors to chargers, power banks, and car mounts. Not just products with “MagSafe compatible” slapped on the box.

With the iPhone Duo set to arrive on October 23, I’ve rounded up the accessories I’d consider buying to protect the phone, keep it charged, and make everyday use a little easier.

How I chose the iPhone Duo accessories

I didn’t want to fill this list with every accessory I could find. For a phone as unusual as the iPhone Duo, compatibility comes first.

  • Compatibility matters more. A regular iPhone case has one rigid body to protect. The Duo folds in half, has two displays, a hinge, and a completely different physical profile. An accessory can have a magnetic connection and still be a poor fit for the Duo.
  • I’m looking at how an accessory behaves when the phone is folded and unfolded. This is especially crucial when it comes to cases, screen protectors, wallets, mounts, etc.
  • I’m prioritising accessories that make the Duo easier to live with. The best iPhone Duo accessories shouldn’t make this already-expensive phone heavier, bulkier, or more awkward.

I looked for accessories that are specifically designed or listed for the Duo, while also considering everyday practicality.

Apple’s official accessories for the iPhone Duo

If I were buying the iPhone Duo on launch day and wanted the least amount of compatibility guesswork, I’d start with Apple’s own accessories.

  • iPhone Duo Case: If you want something simple and understated, go for Apple’s standard iPhone Duo Case. It has two parts and a PC build for protection. The matte coating prevents scratches and smudges. But the hinge remains open.
  • iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand: This is genuinely useful when I want to prop up the larger inner display to watch videos, read, or video call. The TechWoven material keeps the case thin and lightweight. You can also use wireless charging with the case.

Best third-party accessories you should get for your iPhone Duo

Apple’s accessories are the safest route, but I’d still look at third-party options. They provide more flexibility regarding protection, design, charging, and everyday functionality.

Best iPhone Duo cases

I’ve covered more options in my dedicated best iPhone Duo cases roundup, but these are the three I’d shortlist for different needs.

  • Spigen Slim Armour Pro S MagFit Case: This is my pick for serious protection without giving up MagSafe accessories. Its patented hinge protection and SecuLink design are built for repeated folding, while the 360° aluminium kickstand helps prop up the Duo in portrait or landscape mode.
  • elago Magnetic Clear Case: Show off the Duo’s design with this ultra-slim case. Its separate front and rear pieces provide a precise fit, while the built-in magnet supports wireless charging. But the hinge remains unprotected.
  • SIXBOX Ultra Wallet Case: It holds 2–3 cards or folded cash, adds a hidden magnetic stand and hinge protection, a 9H+ tempered glass screen protector, and even covers the camera lenses, making it a practical all-in-one iPhone Duo case for everyday use.

Best screen protectors for iPhone Duo

A screen protector is one accessory I wouldn’t skip on a foldable phone. With two displays to worry about, I’d rather spend a little extra on protection than discover a scratch after only a few weeks.

  • Spigen GlasTR EZ FIT Pro: I’d choose it for strong everyday protection. Its AluminaCore glass offers 10H+ scratch resistance and optical clarity, while the oleophobic layer prevents fingerprints. The EZ Fit Pro tray makes installation easier and more precise.
  • Ferilinso Dual Screen Protector: Its nano-ceramic inner display protector adds strong scratch and impact resistance, while the kit also includes sapphire camera lens protectors and back tempered glass for more complete Duo coverage.
  • ZAGG Glass Elite Privacy Screen Protector: I’d choose it if I regularly use my iPhone Duo in public. It blocks side-angle views while its aluminosilicate glass adds up to 5x stronger protection, and the ClearPrint coating helps keep fingerprints less noticeable.

Charging essentials

I wouldn’t build a complicated charging setup for the Duo. My ideal setup is one compact wall charger, a dependable USB-C cable, wireless charging at my desk, and a power bank for days when I’m away from an outlet.

  • Anker Nano 65W GaN II PPS USB-C Charger: Its 65W output and foldable design give me plenty of power without taking up much space in my travel bag. The GaN technology improves charging efficiency without overheating.
  • INIU 240W USB-C Cable: I’d keep it if I want a single cable that can handle my iPhone Duo and other USB-C devices. Its nylon braided exterior is better suited for everyday carry, while EMARK2.0 adds extra protection against overheating and overcharging.
  • ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Charging Station: Perfect to keep on your desk or use as a nightstand. Its foldable, compact design makes it travel-friendly, while 25W Qi2.2 magnetic charging and CryoBoost cooling deliver faster, cooler wireless charging.
  • TORRAS PearlGo 10,000mAh Power Bank: It would go straight into my travel accessories bag. You get 45W USB-C output, a dual cooling chip for efficient charging, a built-in 2.3ft retractable cable, an Apple Watch charger, and a compact portable design.

Travel accessories

This is where I’d expect the Duo to become particularly useful. The bigger screen of the Duo could work well for navigation and media, yet I would need the right accessories to use it comfortably in a car or while travelling.

  • Delobon Car Phone Holder: Built from sturdy aluminium alloy, you need to install it on the air outlet using the spiral hook. The gravity clamp and 360° rotation make switching between portrait and landscape viewing easy with one hand.
  • ESR OmniLock MagSafe Car Mount: I’d choose it for a more sophisticated magnetic car setup. Its 25W Qi2.2 charging and strong N52 magnets keep the Duo powered and steady, even on bumpy drives. Moreover, the CryoBoost cooling is a plus since using the navigation on charge heats up a phone.

Limitation: Not every MagSafe accessory fits iPhone Duo

This is the one thing I’d keep in mind before ordering anything for the iPhone Duo.

Just because an accessory says MagSafe compatible doesn’t automatically mean it’s a good fit for the iPhone Duo. The Duo has a completely different physical design, including a hinge and a folding mechanism, so magnetic alignment and clearance matter more. Many of my existing MagSafe accessories simply hang out of the phone as they are larger.

I’d specifically look for iPhone Duo compatibility before buying a case, wallet, charger, or car mount. You should also check whether the accessory works with the phone both folded and unfolded, if that’s relevant to how you plan to use it.

Final verdict: What I’d actually buy

If I were buying the iPhone Duo on launch day, I wouldn’t go for building an expensive accessory setup right away.

My setup will include Spigen Slim Armour Pro for protection, Spigen GlasTR for the screen, Anker 715 Charger for wired charging, and the ESR 3-in-1 wireless charger for my desk or bedside table.

For travel, I’d add the TORRAS PearlGo power bank and the ESR MagSafe car mount. That gives me everything I’d realistically need without filling my bag with accessories that rarely get used.

Apple’s foldable iPhone is still a new category, so I expect the accessory ecosystem to grow quickly after launch. For now, start with a few well-chosen essentials and see how the Duo fits into your daily routine before buying more.

Which iPhone Duo accessory are you planning to buy first?

title.rendered: Match overrides in Fortnite: All types, what they do, and where to find them

content.rendered:
Match overrides are a new game mechanic introduced in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4, which heavily influence the gameplay, usually for all players in a given match. This is only the second aspect added in the ongoing season that reasonably benefits the player who activates it, with the other one being Fortnite Override’s loot hacks.

Since being rolled out in Epic’s multiplayer title, the list of match overrides has grown, with new ones providing players more choice over which gameplay variables they want to change. The list below contains all match overrides available in Fortnite, their locations, and what they do.

Types of match overrides in Fortnite

There are a total of 16 different match overrides in the game, with only a random selection from them becoming available to choose at an override console during a match. While a few Rare and Mythic match overrides trigger a change for your squad exclusively, a majority of them affect all the players in the lobby. After activating an override of the former kind, your location is also revealed to others in the match.

The full list of match overrides, along with their respective function, is shared below.

  1. Action Hero: Triggers hangtime and boosts damage when you aim and shoot enemies in mid-air.
  2. Big Fish: Turns all fishing spots into golden fishing spots.
  3. Big Head Mode: Enlarges the head of every player in that match.
  4. Big Loot: Increases chances of getting epic or legendary loot from chests.
  5. Constant Heal: Triggers constant health and shield regeneration while out of combat.
  6. Extra Life: Unlocks an additional life for that particular match.
  7. Headshot: Increases headshot damage.
  8. Infinite Stamina: Unlocks infinite stamina bar.
  9. Loot Hack: Offers a loot hack item from the next chest you open.
  10. More XP: Boosts XP gained from eliminations, survival, and looting.
  11. Overshield: Provides a new or extra Overshield.
  12. Power Pickaxe: Provides greatly increased pickaxe damage.
  13. Prop Hunt: Unlocks the ability to turn into a prop if crouching still for several seconds.
  14. Sharpshooter: Improves weapons in terms of accuracy, recoil, and bloom.
  15. Sonic Speed: Boosts sprint speed over time.
  16. Speed Shooter: Unlocks faster fire rate and reload.

The Fortnite Override season originally kicked off with 12 match overrides. Then, after the Fortnite v42.10 update, Action Hero, Big Head Mode, Prop Hunt, and Sharpshooter were added to the mix. Similarly, you can expect more match overrides to join the list as subsequent updates are released.

Locations of match overrides in Fortnite

There are a total of seven different locations in the Fortnite Override Battle Royale map where you can find override consoles. However, only one such console is active and marked on the map at any given time.

You must be the first person to reach an active override console in order to enable one of the given match overrides. If someone has already activated a marked override console, it appears on the map with a green tick.

It’s worth noting that there are two CPU-controlled guards near any given override console. You can easily sneak past them and interact with the console, but if they spot you, they will open fire. Upon activating a console, your username is broadcasted to other players in the match.

The locations marked by a red circle on the map below are where you can find the override consoles in Fortnite Battle Royale.

Author’s take

Match overrides have undoubtedly inserted a fun way for players to tweak Fortnite’s rules, as per their liking, for the duration of a match. Some of them, such as Constant Heal and Sonic Speed, are purely utilitarian, whereas certain others, such as Big Head Mode and Prop Hunt, bring comedic-cum-strategic opportunities to the game.

The most powerful match overrides in my experience so far have been the Extra Life and the Power Pickaxe. While the former lets you play more naturally, thanks to the assurance provided by a bonus life, the latter is immensely useful for offence-heavy playstyles and can even eliminate enemies with just one hit of your pickaxe. So, when making a choice at the override consoles, it is advisable to take note of these things.

title.rendered: Loot Hacker sprites in Fortnite: How to find them and why you should use them

content.rendered:
Loot Hacker sprites are the latest sprite variant introduced in Fortnite Override. These sprites were added to the game on Thursday and, in the process, have boosted the game’s sprite count from 46 to 61 unique sprites.

These Loot Hacker sprites, when equipped, let you get Fortnite loot hack items from chests more easily by boosting the odds in your favour. The items in question include Wrecker Revolver, Deadeye Assault Rifle, Holo Twister Assault Rifle, Scorpion’s Kombat Kit, and Caduceus Staff. By levelling up a sprite of this variant, you can further increase the spawn rate of these loot hacks.

How to find a Loot Hacker sprite in Fortnite

Use cheat codes

While cheat codes in gaming generally let you bend a particular game’s rules in your favour, the ones in Fortnite are actually a primary way of obtaining sprites in Chapter 7 Season 4. These cheat codes come in various rarity tiers, usually offering sprites of that corresponding tier to players when properly interacted with.

Additionally, they are scattered all across the Battle Royale map in abundance, with only the rarest ones, such as a Legendary-tier golden cheat code, being the hardest to find. On the other hand, the Rare and Epic cheat codes that come in blue and purple respectively are rather widespread.

You can find loot hacker sprite variants in Fortnite by using these cheat codes. The highest concentration of these codes is in areas such as Heatwave Harbour, Cluster Coast, Shaken Sanctuary, and Green Hill Zone.

To make your quest for finding cheat codes more efficient, you can resort to using the Cheat Code Locator gizmo. If you don’t already have one, you can easily get a few for free by entering certain Fortnite lobby hacks such as “SurviveTheNight” and “FindItChat.” Another option is buying the gizmo, using Sprite Dust, from one of the Extraction Sites found throughout the island.

Open Rare Chests

Chests are not only a reliable source of good loot, but they are also a possible source of getting your desired sprite. Obviously, you can’t expect the standard chests to give a handsome reward, but the blue ones, aka Rare Chests, are where the money is at. In other words, Rare Chests and other high-tier chests have a good chance of giving you the Loot Hacker sprites.

The Pac-Man islands, the Battlewoods, and Stone Sanctum are some preferable spots on the Fortnite map if you are looking for the blue-colored chests. Besides using chests out in the open, you should also go for the ones that are locked behind vaults, since those are the chests that often provide the rarest of sprites.

Index it with the help of another player

A third, more straightforward way to get a Loot Hacker variant is to take the help of someone who has already extracted it. You can find such players who are willing to do this on Fortnite’s official Discord.

This method involves joining the same match with another player who has the sprite you want. Then, once the other player drops the sprite, you can go ahead and extract it. After the match, you will have to join another lobby with the same player and, this time, you would give the sprite back to its original owner. Since it’s already been indexed in your collection, you can recall that sprite at any time in exchange for Sprite Dust.

Why you should use Loot Hacker sprites in Fortnite

The current pool of loot hacks has a robust lineup of weapons and items. For offence, the Wrecker Revolver is a highly effective choice, whereas the Caduceus Staff is a potent healing tool for those looking to retreat and recover. Any of these items can make a fine addition in your loadout, especially when fully upgraded.

Since the entire purpose of the Loot Hacker variant is providing you with unlocked loot hack items as early in the game as possible, they are a great help for when you want to quickly get hold of them. Besides that, these sprites also offer their respective base benefit, which further amplifies the appeal of the Loot Hacker variants of Fortnite Override’s sprites.

Rounding up

Loot hacks are among the most game-changing features introduced in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4. It has certainly given players more incentive to extract sprites and collect Sprite Dust in order to unlock the loot hack items. Suffice to say, this new aspect of the game has given players more ways to approach a match and offered greater freedom for personalising their loadout.

As the season progresses further, it’s fair to expect the existing loot hack pool to change in the coming days. When that happens, it will be interesting to see how the new items compare to the ones they replaced. Moreover, such a change will also require players to master new loadouts each time, keeping them on their toes throughout the remainder of Fortnite Override.

title.rendered: How to Update Your AirPods to the Latest Firmware Version

content.rendered:
Updating your AirPods, AirPods Pro, and AirPods Max is essential to ensure you enjoy the latest features and improvements. Apple typically rolls out firmware updates automatically over the air, but you can force an update manually if necessary.

In this guide, I’ll explain how to update your AirPods firmware and check whether they’re running the latest version.

Table of Contents
  • How to Update Firmware on AirPods
  • How to Update AirPods Max Firmware
  • How to Check Your AirPods Firmware Version
    • Find Your AirPods Firmware Version on iPhone or iPad
    • Find Your AirPods Firmware Version on Mac
  • What Is the Latest AirPods Firmware Version?
  • Signing off…

How to Update Firmware on AirPods

In most cases, AirPods and AirPods Pro firmware updates happen automatically in the background without any notification. The updates are pushed over-the-air (OTA) when the AirPods are placed for charging or within the Bluetooth range of the associated iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

But in case you notice that AirPods are not updated as expected, you can manually force an update using the following steps:

  1. Place the AirPods in their charging case and connect the case to a power outlet using a Lightning cable or a Wireless charger.
  2. Make sure that your iPhone, iPad or Mac is connected to Wi-Fi and has more than 50% battery charge. Also, make sure Bluetooth is on and Low Power mode is off.
  3. Leave your iPhone, iPad, or Mac nearby. Make sure the case’s lid remains closed during the process.

It should complete the firmware update in the background, as there is no specific option to manually trigger it. After about 10 minutes, check whether your AirPods firmware has been updated. The latest AirPods firmware version will be found later in the post.

Note If you don’t own an Apple device, you can’t update your AirPods.

How to Update AirPods Max Firmware

Updating AirPods Max is similar to updating AirPods, but there are slight differences in the process. These over-ear headphones don’t need a charging case.

  1. Ensure the paired iPhone, iPad, or Mac is 50% charged and has Wi-Fi and Bluetooth enabled.
  2. If you have an iPhone or iPad, plug the charging cable into the AirPods Max, connect it to the power outlet, and keep it close to your device.
  3. If you have a Mac, plug the charging cable into the AirPods Max and connect them to your Mac.

Now wait for 30 minutes, then check your AirPods Max firmware version.

How to Check Your AirPods Firmware Version

After you complete the update, checking the current firmware version of your AirPods can help you confirm whether they are up to date. Here’s how to check it on your connected iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Find Your AirPods Firmware Version on iPhone or iPad

To check your AirPods firmware on your iPhone or iPad, be sure to update your iOS or iPadOS to the latest version. Then do the following:

  1. Go to Settings and select Bluetooth.
  2. Select the info (i) button next to the AirPods.
  3. You can see the version of your AirPods under the About section.

Find Your AirPods Firmware Version on Mac

First, make sure your Mac runs the latest macOS, then do the following.

  1. Click on the Apple icon in the top-left corner of your screen and select System Settings.
  2. Click on Bluetooth from the left panel.
  3. Locate your AirPods in the list, then click the info (i) icon next to them.
  4. Check the Version displayed in the information window.

What Is the Latest AirPods Firmware Version?

Apple often updates the firmware of the AirPods models to enhance connectivity, sound quality, and battery performance, fix bugs, and occasionally introduce new features like Spatial audio, head gestures, etc.

The recent 9A348 update for the AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2 brings support for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS Golden Gate features. You get a redesigned AirPods interface, an Adaptive mode slider, custom EQ controls, and compatibility with Apple’s new Siri AI.

Additionally, AirPods Pro 3 get support for Precision Finding via Apple Watch and GymKit for syncing heart rate data. The prior 8B25 update set the stage for integrating Live Translation in the European Union in iOS 26.2.

So, you must check and update your AirPods to get the best experience.

Here are the latest firmware versions:

  • AirPods Pro (3rd generation): 9A348
  • AirPods Pro (2nd generation) with MagSafe Charging Case (Lightning and USB-C): 9A348
  • AirPods Pro (1st generation): 6F21
  • AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation: 9A348
  • AirPods 4: 9A348
  • AirPods (2nd and 3rd generation): 6F21
  • AirPods Max 2: 9A348
  • AirPods Max (USB-C): 7E108
  • AirPods Max (Lightning): 6F25
  • AirPods (1st generation): 6.8.8

For the latest details on firmware updates, be sure to visit Apple’s official website.

Signing off…

Keeping your AirPods up to date ensures that you get the best possible performance and access to new features. While the process is designed to happen automatically, knowing how to check and confirm the latest firmware is useful.

Also read:

  • AirPods 4 vs. AirPods Pro 2: Which one should you buy?
  • How to fix AirPods static noise quickly
  • How to change AirPods settings on iPhone or iPad
  • How to Prevent iPhone from Auto-Switching Audio from AirPods to Your Car

keyPoints.title: Automatic Firmware Updates for AirPods
keyPoints.explanation: Most AirPods and AirPods Pro firmware updates happen automatically over-the-air when they are charging or near your connected device, without notifications.

keyPoints.title: Manual Firmware Update Process
keyPoints.explanation: To manually update your AirPods, place them in their charging case, connect the case to power, ensure your device has Wi-Fi and sufficient battery, and leave them near each other for about 10 minutes.

keyPoints.title: Updating AirPods Max
keyPoints.explanation: Updating AirPods Max involves connecting them to a charged iPhone, iPad, or Mac via a Lightning or USB-C cable and waiting about 30 minutes for the firmware to update.

keyPoints.title: Checking Your AirPods Firmware Version
keyPoints.explanation: You can verify your AirPods firmware version on an iPhone or iPad through Bluetooth settings or on a Mac via System Settings and Bluetooth, to ensure they are up-to-date.

keyPoints.title: Latest AirPods Firmware Versions and Features
keyPoints.explanation: The newest firmware, like 8A356, introduces features such as Spatial Audio, Sleep Detection, Charging Reminders, and improvements in noise isolation, available on latest models.

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Gym League Codes on September 21, 2026

Gym League turns every rep into muscle, meals, and a race toward the next gym. As you progress through the game, building enough strength to move forward can take a fair amount of time, especially when upgrades and new gyms start demanding more from your character. That’s where working codes can make a noticeable difference, giving you useful resources without forcing you to grind from zero every time you start a new session.

The right codes can provide free food and potions that help speed up your progress and make your training sessions more productive. Instead of spending all your time collecting resources, you can use these rewards to get a head start and focus on building your character’s strength.

All working Gym League codes

  • DIVINE: 20 minutes of 1.25x Muscle Gain Buff (NEW)
  • WORLD10: 20 minutes of 1.25x Cash Gain Buff (NEW)
  • ASCENSION: 500 Cash and 3 Breakfast of Champions (NEW)
  • FRESHSTART: 20 minutes of 1.25x Cash Gain Buff (NEW)
  • WELCOME BACK: 500 Cash and 3 Breakfast of Champions (NEW)
  • SORRYFORBUGSAD: Free rewards (NEW)
  • Update29: 3 Breakfast of champions, 3 Warriors lunch, and 3 Dinner of legends
  • halloweenpart2: 2 Pumpkin candy bag and 100 Candies
  • hauntedbalanced: 2 Breakfast of champions, 2 Warriors lunch, and 2 Dinner of legends
  • Halloweenpart1: 25 Blood Potions

Expired Gym League codes

100KACTIVE, 10KLIKES, 10KVIEWS, 150KLIKES, 150MVISITS, 1MMEMBERS, 1MVISITS, 2.5MFAVS, 20MVISITS, 2XEVENT, 400MVISITS, 5KLIKES, 5XMUSCLE, 650KLIKES, ANCIENT, BALANCE, BATTLEPOTION, BETTERGAMEPLAY, BETTERTOGETHER, BLIZZARDEVENTFIX, BLOODMOON, BONUSGAINS, BRAINROT, BUGFIXES, CHRISTMASGAINS, CLANS, COMPSFIX, COSMICGAINS, DEFLATION, DIVINEMUSCLES, DUNGEONGYM, EASYGAINS, FEELINGLUCKY, FIRSTTRAINER, FLAMING, FOLLOWGYMLEAGUERBLX, FROZEN, FRUITPIRATE, GLCOMEBACK, GYMGAMES, HALLOWEEN, HIDDENFOOD, HOLIDAYSEASONS, HUGEUPDATESOON, JUNGLE, JUNGLEGAMES, KEEPGRINDING, LATEXMAS, LEAGUE, LEAGUEOVER, LEAGUES2, LIGHTNINGEVENT, LIGHTNINGQUEST, MIDUPD, MINERATIONS, NEWGEARS, OLYMPUS, PIRATEBUGFIX, PLAYER456, POWERLEVEL, POWERLIFTING, POWERUPQOL, PRISONBOUND, PUMPKING, QOL2, QUALITYOFLIFE, RELEASE, SEASON3PASS, SHADOWS, SOLOLEVELING, SORRY, SORRYFORDELAY, SPARTAN, STARLIFT, SUMMERBODY, SUMMERFUN, SUMMERVIBES, TRADE, TRADE PUMPKING, TRADINGPLAZA, TWILIGHT, UNDEAD, UPDATE2, UPDATE28, UPDATE29P2, UPDATE29P3, UPDATE30, UPDATE30P2, UPDATE31, UPDATE31BUGFIX, WEREBACK, ZEROG

How to redeem Gym League codes

You need to be inside the Roblox experience before the code menu appears.

  1. Open Gym League on Roblox.
  2. Load into a server.
  3. Tap the Codes button at the bottom-left of the screen.
  4. Paste a code into the box and tap Submit.

If the code works, the reward should appear in your inventory immediately.

Why Gym League codes may not work

  • The code has expired or was incorrectly marked active by an older tracker.
  • You already redeemed it on that Roblox account.
  • A capital letter, missing character, or extra space changed the code.
  • A recent update has not reached the server you joined. Leave, rejoin Gym League, and try again.
  • You have a Roblox connection problem rather than a code problem. If you cannot rejoin the game, use this guide to fix Roblox Error Code 279.

Where to find more Gym League codes

New codes usually appear around updates, bug fixes, seasonal events, or player milestones. Watch the official Gym League Roblox page and the 1v2 Studios Discord server, which is the developer’s main community hub for announcements and code drops. The developer also posts on X at @GYMLeagueRBLX.

I’ll keep this page focused on codes with clear status and reward information, so you don’t have to burn time testing every old string you find in search results. If you want more free rewards, check out the latest Stay Hard Run codes, Pressure codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

title.rendered: X and SpaceXAI ask court to drop Apple from antitrust lawsuit

content.rendered:
X Corp. and SpaceXAI LLC have asked a Texas federal judge to dismiss their antitrust claims against Apple with prejudice, while leaving their claims against OpenAI in place. Their September 14 motion says the plaintiffs have resolved their claims with Apple and that Apple does not oppose the request.

The motion asks for dismissal under Rule 41(a)(2), which requires a court order. Judge Mark Pittman must approve the request before Apple’s claims are formally dismissed. If granted, the dismissal with prejudice would prevent X and SpaceXAI from bringing the same claims against Apple again. The filing does not explain the resolution or identify any settlement terms.

OpenAI remains in the case

The motion explicitly keeps the claims against OpenAI Foundation, OpenAI, L.L.C., and OpenAI OpCo, LLC. X and xAI first sued Apple and OpenAI in August 2025, arguing that Apple’s ChatGPT integration with Siri and Apple Intelligence gave OpenAI an advantage over rivals such as Grok. Their original complaint also challenged Apple’s App Store visibility for competing apps.

Judge Pittman denied Apple and OpenAI’s first motions to dismiss in November 2025, allowing the case to move into discovery. The court’s order did not decide whether the antitrust allegations were true.

Until Pittman rules, both Apple and OpenAI remain defendants. If he grants the motion, Apple would leave the case while the claims against OpenAI continue without a ruling on their merits.

excerpt.rendered: The motion says Apple has resolved its part of the case and does not oppose dismissal. The antitrust claims against OpenAI would remain if the judge grants it.

title.rendered: Gentler Streak and The Outsiders add Siri AI support in iOS 27

content.rendered:
With iOS 27 now available, Gentler Streak 5.13 and The Outsiders 1.8 add support for Apple’s new Siri AI, letting users ask about workouts, training readiness, body metrics, and sleep without opening either app. Gentler Stories CEO Katarina Lotrič described the updates in a September 14 report from 9to5Mac.

Users should include the app’s name in a request, such as "Show today’s workouts in Gentler Streak." Gentler Streak can answer questions about activity status, Go Gentler suggestions, daily body metrics, and the previous night’s sleep. The Outsiders can also report training readiness, today’s workouts, body metrics, and sleep.

Siri can explain what’s on screen

With either app open, users can ask Siri to explain a workout summary, health chart, or another screen. Apple’s App Intents framework and View Annotations API let developers connect app content and actions to Siri, then give the assistant context about what’s visible.

The updates also add on-device AI workout-title suggestions, refreshed icons with a Liquid Glass look, and layouts that adjust to different screen sizes and window positions, including iPad windows and iPhone Duo.

Apple says Siri AI is rolling out in English and is limited to Apple Intelligence-compatible devices. Installing the app updates alone will not unlock the feature for every iPhone running iOS 27. If Siri AI has not appeared yet, check the device and rollout requirements.

excerpt.rendered: Ask Siri about workouts, sleep, and training readiness without opening either app. The updates add on-screen awareness, AI workout titles, and adaptive layouts.

title.rendered: GTA 6 Online release date: Everything we know

content.rendered:
There’s no denying that the hype surrounding GTA 6 is at an all-time high right now. In the last couple of weeks, we’ve seen new gameplay footage, screenshots, and plenty of other information about what players can expect to see in Leonida. While Rockstar has given the community a close look at what can be expected from the single-player experience, what fans really want to know about is the GTA 6 Online release date. 

Considering the money-printer GTA Online has proven to be for the developer, it would be surprising if GTA 6 doesn’t get its own online mode. However, the real question is when it is going to hit the shelves. 

So, does GTA 6 Online have a confirmed release date? Here’s everything we know.

When will GTA 6 Online release?

Let’s get this right out of the way first: GTA 6 Online does not have a confirmed release date yet. As of now, GTA 6 is all set ot drop on November 19, 2026, and Rockstar has described the game as a “single-player experience” at launch. What this means is that the online component won’t be available right out of the gate, and players will be focusing on Jason and Lucia’s story as they explore Leonida.

For newer fans, this might come as a surprise, but Rockstar has a history of releasing its online modes separately from the base game. For instance, GTA Online launched exactly two weeks after GTA 5. Similarly, Red Dead Online beta arrived more than a month after Red Dead Redemption 2. Now, some might think that GTA 6 Online’s launch might follow a similar path. However, Rockstar hasn’t uttered a word about its plans for the game yet, and there are several reasons why GTA 6 Online might take even longer.

If you haven’t been keeping up, Rockstar has recently collaborated with Nopixel to bring Nopixel V to GTA Online. Although it’s roleplaying content, it gives players a completely new way to experience Los Santos. The timing for this project is interesting considering that GTA 6 is less than 100 days away, and yet Rockstar is actively promoting GTA Online. If that wasn’t enough, players who pre-order GTA 6 are also getting one month of GTA+ for the current GTA Online.

Rockstar isn’t moving away from GTA Online, and that’s because it’s way too profitable. Even though it’s more than 13 years old, the game continues to make millions of dollars in annual revenue. You’ll be shocked to know, but according to a Forbes report, GTA Online in 2020 managed to make $744 million from microtransactions alone. In recent years, the game has continued to bring in around $400 million annually.

With GTA Online performing so well, Rockstar probably doesn’t want to immediately pull the plug. GTA 6 Online will be a completely new experience, and it will undoubtedly overshadow the existing game. Fans have been itching for something new, and even if they spend a second exploring GTA 6, it would be hard to convince them to return to GTA Online.

That’s not the only thing. When GTA Online and Red Dead Online made their debut, both of these games were bare-bones. It’s only after Rockstar spent years adding new missions, activities, weapons, and other content that they became the massive online experiences known today. This has raised the expectations for GTA 6 Online as well. It won’t be a simple “add-on” to the base game.

It’s clear as day that Rockstar is focusing all of its resources on the single-player side of GTA 6. With all the factors we’ve mentioned above, GTA 6 Online will probably take longer to develop and launch. There’s a good chance Rockstar wants to see how the game performs at launch, its impact on the existing GTA Online player base, and then fully shift its attention to GTA 6 Online. As a result, a GTA 6 Online launch window of six months to a year after the release of the base game sounds quite realistic.

Will GTA 6 Online support 32-player lobbies?

Neither Rockstar Games nor the GTA 6 leaks that surfaced online a while ago have given us any concrete details about what’s being planned for GTA 6 Online. However, recent information from some court documents suggests that Rockstar might have been experimenting with 32-player lobbies for the game mode.

A few months ago, Rockstar found itself in court against the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain due to allegations of union-busting. The studio claimed that several developers were fired after allegedly leaking sensitive information about its games on Discord.

As People Make Games reported, based on documents presented during the case, one Rockstar employee mentioned that running a “large session” was challenging with 32 players. Rockstar’s legal team argued that this was confidential information about an upcoming project.

Now, fresh documents from Rockstar’s employment tribunal have surfaced online, with The Herald reporting that the developer described an “online 32-player format” as a “highly confidential” feature.

Of course, this doesn’t confirm that GTA 6 Online will launch with 32-player lobbies. However, this gives an insight into what Rockstar may have been experimenting with during development. The lobby size could make its way to the final version, but there’s a chance that Rockstar might have changed its plans. Only time will tell us what’s in store for GTA 6 Online.

Rounding up

Even though GTA 6 is just around the corner, Rockstar still hasn’t revealed its plans for the GTA 6 Online release date. Considering the success of GTA Online and Rockstar’s current focus on the single-player experience, many speculate that the online mode could arrive anywhere from six months to a year after the debut of the base game.
