title.rendered: iPhone Duo vs Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold: Which foldable should you buy?

content.rendered:
Apple has finally entered the foldable phone market with iPhone Duo, but Google is already on store shelves with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Both phones give you a phone-sized outer screen and a larger tablet-like display inside, but they make very different trade-offs.

Here is the short version: buy the Pixel 11 Pro Fold if you want a foldable now, a larger display, a lighter design, and a more flexible zoom camera. Wait for iPhone Duo if you already use an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Pencil and want a foldable that fits naturally into that ecosystem. Apple’s phone also offers a 2TB storage option and a strong video feature set, but it costs $100 more at list price and does not arrive in the U.S. until October 23.

iPhone Duo vs Pixel 11 Pro Fold specs at a glance

Apple announced iPhone Duo on September 9, 2026. Google announced the Pixel 11 Pro Fold in August, and it is already available in the U.S.

These are official specifications, not independent test results. Apple and Google measure battery life differently, so the battery claims should not be treated as a direct winner-takes-all comparison.

Design and displays

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is the better fit if you want the biggest canvas. Its 8-inch inner display is larger than the iPhone Duo’s 7.6-inch screen, and its 6.5-inch outer display is also much more spacious than Apple’s 5.4-inch cover screen. That extra room should make typing, reading, and multitasking more comfortable without opening the phone every time.

The size advantage does not make the Pixel bulky. At 8.4 ounces, it is 0.56 ounces lighter than iPhone Duo. Google also lists the Pixel at 0.4 inches thick when folded, compared with 0.44 inches for Apple’s phone.

Apple takes a different approach. iPhone Duo is shorter and wider when open, with a 7.6-inch inner display in a 6.48 x 4.64-inch body. The phone also supports ProMotion up to 120Hz on both displays, an Always-On display, Dynamic Island, and Apple Pencil USB-C support. Apple lists up to 3,000 nits of outdoor peak brightness, while Google lists up to 3,600 nits peak brightness on both Pixel displays.

The choice is simple: get the Pixel for more screen space and lower weight, or choose iPhone Duo if you prefer Apple’s display features and want to use an Apple Pencil with the foldable. The Pixel is the more practical mini-tablet, while the iPhone is the more compact Apple device when folded.

Cameras: Pixel wins zoom, iPhone wins video flexibility

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold has the more versatile camera hardware. Its rear system includes a 48MP main camera, a 10.5MP ultrawide camera with autofocus and Macro Focus, and a dedicated 10.8MP 5x telephoto camera with optical image stabilization. Google also supports Super Zoom up to 30x.

iPhone Duo uses two 48MP rear cameras: a main camera and an ultrawide camera. The main camera gives you 2x optical-quality telephoto framing, but there is no dedicated telephoto lens. Its official optical-quality range runs from 0.5x through 2x, with up to 10x digital zoom.

That makes the Pixel the safer pick for concerts, sports, travel, and distant subjects. The dedicated 5x camera gives it a real hardware advantage instead of asking the main camera to crop aggressively.

Apple’s response is video. iPhone Duo can record 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 120 frames per second with its Fusion Main camera. It also supports Center Stage, Dual Capture, and Audio Mix features designed for people who record themselves and their surroundings. The Pixel records rear video up to 4K at 60 frames per second and adds Video Boost, Night Sight Video, and 10-bit HDR.

Choose the Pixel for zoom and camera flexibility. Choose iPhone Duo if video recording, FaceTime, and Apple’s camera tools matter more than having a dedicated telephoto lens.

Software and ecosystem

This is the decision that will matter most after the hardware comparison. iPhone Duo runs iOS 27, while the Pixel 11 Pro Fold runs Android 17. Our iOS 27 vs Android 17 comparison covers the wider software differences, but the foldable choice is mostly about the devices and services you already use.

If you have a Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, or an iPad, iPhone Duo should feel familiar from day one. FaceTime, iMessage, AirDrop, Apple Intelligence, and Apple Pencil support all work in the same Apple environment. The trade-off is that Apple’s phone is eSIM-only, so anyone who relies on a physical SIM should check with their carrier before buying.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is the more flexible multitasking device. Google highlights Split Screen, Drag & Drop, Instant View, app bubbles, Gemini features, and Circle to Search. It also includes seven years of Android version updates, security updates, and Pixel Drops. The Pixel supports one physical Nano-SIM alongside eSIM, which makes it easier to move between carriers or use a backup line.

If you are switching from Android to Apple, read our guide on how to transfer data from Android to iPhone before you buy. The transfer is manageable, but your watch, messaging habits, and app purchases may affect the real cost of changing ecosystems.

Performance and battery

iPhone Duo uses Apple’s A20 Pro chip. Apple lists a six-core CPU, a seven-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a dual 16-core Neural Engine. Pixel 11 Pro Fold uses Google Tensor G6 with 16GB of RAM and a Titan M3 security chip.

Those chip names do not tell us which phone will feel faster in every app. Apple and Google optimize their processors for different workloads, and iPhone Duo is not available for independent testing yet. For now, the safe conclusion is that both phones have current flagship hardware, while the real performance gap will have to wait for hands-on reviews.

Battery claims are similarly difficult to compare. Apple says iPhone Duo lasts up to 24 hours in typical use and lists up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display or 31 hours on the inner display. Google gives the Pixel 11 Pro Fold a 24-plus-hour claim and lists a typical 4,806mAh battery.

Apple says iPhone Duo can reach 50% in about 20 minutes with a 60W-capable adapter. Google says the Pixel can reach 50% in about 30 minutes with a 30W USB-C PPS charger or higher. Apple sells its adapter separately, so remember to budget for a compatible charger if you do not already have one.

Durability and long-term ownership

Both phones have an IP68 rating, but that does not make either one waterproof or immune to damage. Foldable hinges and large flexible displays still deserve more care than a regular slab phone.

iPhone Duo uses a titanium foldable design with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and a Ceramic Shield back. Google says the Pixel uses a new gearless hinge, a glass fiber composite back, and ultra-strong ceramic outer cover glass. Google also says the Pixel is three times more durable than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold in its internal testing. That is a generational claim, not a direct durability test against iPhone Duo.

The Pixel has the clearer published software-support promise: seven years of OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates. Apple has a long history of supporting iPhones for years, but the iPhone Duo specifications page does not give a fixed support duration in the same way.

U.S. price and availability

iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 with 256GB of storage. Preorders open October 16, and the phone goes on sale in the U.S. on October 23. The top 2TB model gives Apple a storage tier Google does not offer.

Pixel 11 Pro Fold starts at $1,899 with 256GB and is already available. Google offers 512GB and 1TB versions, but no 2TB model. Google Store promotions and trade-in values can change, so use the $1,899 list price for a fair comparison and treat any discount as a temporary bonus.

The $100 difference matters at this price, especially because Google also gives you larger displays and a dedicated telephoto camera. That gives the Pixel an advantage for shoppers who want a foldable without paying extra for Apple’s ecosystem.

Which foldable should you buy?

For most people buying a foldable phone today, the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold is the better choice. It costs less, is lighter, has larger displays, includes a dedicated 5x telephoto camera, supports a physical SIM, and is available now. Its seven-year update promise also makes the ownership case easier to explain.

Buy the Pixel 11 Pro Fold if you:

  • want the larger inner and outer displays;
  • care about zoom, travel, or close-up photography;
  • want a lighter foldable for daily use;
  • need a physical SIM option;
  • want to buy the phone now; or
  • prefer Android multitasking and Gemini features.

Buy iPhone Duo if you:

  • already use an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, or iPad;
  • want Apple’s video tools and Dolby Vision recording;
  • plan to use Apple Pencil USB-C;
  • want up to 2TB of storage; or
  • are willing to wait until October 23 for iOS on a foldable.

My pick is the Pixel 11 Pro Fold for most foldable shoppers and iPhone Duo for committed Apple users. The Pixel is the better value and the more capable camera phone on paper. iPhone Duo is the more interesting choice if your daily life already runs through Apple, but wait for independent reviews before paying $1,999 for a first-generation foldable.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max: What’s new and should you upgrade?

content.rendered:
Apple has finally pushed its Pro lineup forward with the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The new model is faster, smarter, and more capable than the predecessor, but the differences aren’t obvious at first glance.

Both phones share a similar design and many of the same features, so I wondered what has actually changed and whether it’s worth upgrading. To find the answer, I’ve compared the iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone 17 Pro Max across the camera, performance, battery life, AI features, price, and more to see where the new model really stands out.

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max: Quick comparison

The interesting part is that several headline specifications remain unchanged. The real difference is what Apple has improved underneath them.

Design and display: What actually changed?

If I were upgrading purely for the screen, I wouldn’t.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max retains the familiar 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR display, 120Hz ProMotion, Always-On display, and 3000-nit peak outdoor brightness. The dimensions are also essentially unchanged at 163.4mm tall, 78mm wide, and 8.75mm thick. Although it’s ~16 grams heavier than the 17 Pro Max.

The biggest visible change is actually the Dynamic Island. Apple has redesigned it to occupy less space while displaying more information. The iPhone 18 Pro Max can show up to three Live Activities simultaneously, which could make things such as sports scores, navigation and music controls more useful at a glance.

The material story also stays familiar. The iPhone 18 Pro Max uses an aluminum unibody with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back. The new finishes are Black, Silver, Glacier and Burgundy, replacing the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s Cosmic Orange and Deep Blue options.

My takeaway: the iPhone 18 Pro Max doesn’t offer a design overhaul. It’s a refinement. The smaller Dynamic Island is the change I expect to notice most in everyday use.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: The biggest performance upgrade

This is where I feel the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts to separate itself from its predecessor.

The new A20 Pro is built using a 2-nanometer process and features a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says it has 50% more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, while the GPU can be up to 40% faster. This same chip powers the new foldable iPhone Duo.

But the raw speed isn’t the part I find most interesting.

Apple has redesigned the chip packaging and paired it with a next-generation vapor chamber, which can deliver up to a 40% gain in sustained performance over the previous generation. That matters because sustained performance is what I care about when a phone is rendering video, playing a demanding game, or processing AI workloads for several minutes.

The Neural Engine is another major change. A20 Pro has 32 Neural Engine cores in total, giving it twice the AI processing capability Apple attributes to A19 Pro. That extra headroom is particularly important as Apple pushes more AI processing directly onto the iPhone. We have shared a more detailed breakdown in our A20 Pro guide.

For everyday apps, I don’t expect the iPhone 18 Pro Max to suddenly feel twice as fast. But for gaming, video editing, and on-device AI, this is one of the more meaningful generational upgrades.

Camera: The upgrade I’d pay attention to

If I had to pick one reason to buy the iPhone 18 Pro Max over the iPhone 17 Pro Max, I’d pick the camera.

The headline feature is Apple’s new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture. This is something the iPhone 17 Pro Max doesn’t have. The aperture can move between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4.0.

Why does that matter? A wider aperture can let in more light, while a narrower aperture can give you greater depth of field. Apple says the system can automatically adjust for lighting and depth of field, while photographers can manually select the aperture from the Camera app.

New Pro controls allow manual adjustment of aperture, shutter speed, and white balance, alongside a histogram. Moreover, Photographic Styles 3 adds new texture and grain controls, and Smart focus tracking helps capture moving subjects.

The rest of the camera system remains familiar. The iPhone 18 Pro Max still has 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide and 48MP Fusion Telephoto cameras, with 4x and 8x optical-quality telephoto options. The 18MP Centre Stage front camera also carries over.

There are meaningful video upgrades too, including the ability to apply Cinematic effects after recording and new 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapse capabilities.

If you bought the iPhone 17 Pro Max mainly for its camera, the iPhone 18 Pro Max gives you the clearest reason to consider upgrading.

Battery life and charging: How much better is it?

Battery life is another area where the iPhone 18 Pro Max makes a noticeable numerical jump.

The iPhone 17 Pro Max offers up to 39 hours of video playback. The iPhone 18 Pro Max reaches up to 43 hours, a four-hour increase. Apple attributes the improvement to a larger battery combined with the efficiency gains of its new silicon.

Charging is faster, too. The iPhone 18 Pro Max can get around seven hours of video playback from a five-minute wired charge, according to Apple’s testing. Moreover, you can get up to 50% in around 15 minutes when using a 60W-capable adapter or higher with Adjustable Voltage Supply.

This is the sort of upgrade I appreciate more than a benchmark score. If I leave home with a nearly empty phone, a few minutes connected to a charger suddenly become much more useful. For heavy users, the battery upgrade alone makes the iPhone 18 Pro Max more attractive.

AI and Siri: iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max

This is where the A20 Pro upgrade becomes more relevant. Both phones support Apple Intelligence, but the iPhone 18 Pro Max launches with iOS 27 and the new Siri AI experience.

Siri AI is designed to understand personal context across apps such as Messages, Mail, and Photos. It can also use on-screen awareness, answer questions, and interact with what you’re seeing through the Camera app.

Apple is also adding more AI-powered tools across iOS 27, including improved Clean Up, Image Playground, Spatial Reframing, and Safari’s Notify Me feature.

The important distinction is that the iPhone 18 Pro Max has considerably more AI processing headroom, thanks to the A20 Pro’s Neural Engine and Neural Accelerators.

That doesn’t mean the iPhone 17 Pro Max suddenly becomes useless for Apple Intelligence. Instead, I see the 18 Pro Max as the better long-term choice if AI is going to become a major part of how I use my phone.

Connectivity with the new Apple C2 Modem

The iPhone 18 Pro Max also gets Apple’s C2 modem system, replacing the previous generation’s C1X.

C2 works alongside the A20 Pro and introduces AI-powered improvements intended to improve cellular quality and reliability. Apple says it can deliver faster uploads in selected markets while consuming 15% less energy than C1X. It also supports mmWave in the US.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max also retains Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip.

I wouldn’t upgrade from an iPhone 17 Pro Max solely for the modem. But improved cellular efficiency, reliability, and upload speeds are the kind of behind-the-scenes upgrades that can make a flagship feel better over years of ownership.

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max: Price difference

This is where the decision becomes more complicated.

The iPhone 17 Pro Max launched at $1,199, with 256GB storage. It was also available in 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB configurations.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299 in the US and continues to offer 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage options.

The bigger point is that the iPhone 17 Pro Max is still an extremely capable phone. If retailers offer meaningful discounts on it, the older model could become the better value.

What hasn’t changed?

This is an important part of the comparison because the iPhone 18 Pro Max isn’t a complete redesign.

The following remain broadly familiar:

  • 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR display with ProMotion up to 120Hz
  • Always-On display
  • Aluminum unibody construction
  • 48MP Ultra Wide camera
  • 48MP Telephoto camera with up to 8x optical-quality zoom
  • 18MP Centre Stage front camera
  • Camera Control
  • Action button
  • USB-C
  • Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread
  • 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage options

The iPhone 17 Pro Max already introduced a major camera and thermal-performance overhaul, so Apple isn’t starting from scratch with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

That’s why I’d describe this generation as a deeper refinement rather than a visual revolution.

My verdict: Should you upgrade?

If I already owned an iPhone 17 Pro Max, I wouldn’t upgrade just because the number changed from 17 to 18. But I would seriously consider the iPhone 18 Pro Max if camera photography, sustained performance, battery life, or AI were priorities for me.

Buy iPhone 18 Pro Max if you:

  • Want the best iPhone camera Apple currently offers.
  • Shoot a lot of photos or video.
  • Play demanding games or edit video on my phone.
  • Want maximum battery life.
  • Like to use the newest Siri AI features.
  • Are upgrading from an iPhone 15 Pro Max or older.

Keep the iPhone 17 Pro Max if:

  • You’re already happy with its camera.
  • Battery life already feels like enough.
  • Don’t care much about AI features.
  • Mostly use your phone for messaging, social media, and streaming.
  • You are getting the 17 Pro Max at a significant discount.

My bottom line: the iPhone 18 Pro Max is not the kind of upgrade that makes the iPhone 17 Pro Max obsolete. Instead, Apple has taken an already powerful flagship and attacked the areas that matter most over a long ownership period, such as camera flexibility, sustained performance, battery life, charging, cellular efficiency, and AI.

If I were buying a Pro Max today and the price difference were reasonable, I’d choose the iPhone 18 Pro Max. But if I already owned the iPhone 17 Pro Max, I’d upgrade only if I genuinely cared about the new camera system or AI capabilities.

So, would you upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, or stick with the iPhone 17 Pro Max for another year? Let me know which one you’d choose.

title.rendered: Apple Watch Ultra 4: Everything you need to know about

content.rendered:
After months of anticipation and rumours, Apple has finally revealed the Apple Watch Ultra 4. Although it doesn’t pack major hardware upgrades compared to its predecessors, Apple has brought on tons of new features, design overhauls, and AI capabilities that will undoubtedly enhance the overall experience of the wearable.

So, if you’re wondering what’s new, what’s changed, and whether it’s worth the upgrade, here’s a complete breakdown of the Apple Watch Ultra 4.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 specifications at a glance (Detailed overview)

Designs & colours: What’s new

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 sticks to the classic design that has defined the Ultra lineup. It brings back a familiar rectangular display and titanium build, but with minor upgrades such as a larger and brighter screen. The company is also putting effort into sustainability, stating that the new wearable is made up of 45% recycled materials, with the titanium case made entirely from recycled titanium.

In terms of finishes, Apple is offering two different options: Natural Titanium and Black Titanium. The company has also introduced new colour options for Trail Loop, Alpine Loop, and Ocean Bands, which means more customisation options for users. For those who want a premium touch, they can also choose the Apple Watch Hermes edition. This one comes with a Grand H titanium band featuring a built-in extension system.

Battery and charging: A major battery boost

Apple has gone all out when it comes to the battery life upgrades for Apple Watch Ultra 4. Now, users will be able to get 50 hours of battery life under normal use, which means just a single charge can get you around two days of use.

Those who switch to Low Power Mode can expect the wearable to last up to 84 hours. Apple has also brought in improvements to the Extended Workout and Max Extended Workout modes, which make Apple Watch Ultra 4 the right choice for longer activities and endurance workouts.

Charging speeds have also been given a look. Now, Apple Watch Ultra 4 can get 18 hours of additional battery life with just 15 minutes of charging. Users will now be able to easily top up their wearable whenever they’re running low, and quickly get back into the action.

Performance: New S11 chip

Under the hood of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is the new S11 chip. This features a 4-core Neural Engine and 64GB of storage. As you’d expect, Apple has dubbed it its most powerful chip ever used in a wearable. While that might not sound like much on paper, it’s actually the foundation for many of Ultra 4’s new health, audio, AI, and tracking capabilities. The chip is also responsible for the new Siri experience in watchOS 27.

Health sensing system

The major highlight of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is its new Health Sensing System. It’s powered by the wearable’s sensors, S11 chip, and advanced algorithms to collect and interpret health data. Now, the watch can take your heart rate readings every five seconds, which gives it more data to analyse and monitor your heart throughout the game.

The system also brings frequent heart-rate variability (HRV) measurements into the play, which will give users a great understanding of their body’s overall wellness and recovery. This works right alongside the Readiness score, which will estimate how well a person is prepared for the day ahead. Apple has also made upgrades to step tracking, which means it will be more accurate than ever before.

Audio Intelligence

Another thing that’s worth keeping an eye out for is Audio Intelligence. What’s this about? Well, it makes use of the wearable’s built-in microphone, the new S11 chip, Apple Intelligence, and other components to bring four unique features to the table:

  • Sound Recognition: If you’re someone who leaves your iPhone behind, the Ultra 4 can now detect important sounds such as doorbells, sirens, and alarms, and send you an alert.
  • Live Rewind: Missed something in a conversation? A double press of the Digital Crown will let you pull up a text snippet of the previous 15 seconds.
  • Siri Recap: Apple Intelligence can now summarise everything you’ve been discussing with someone else and give you a summary.
  • Shazam: You no longer have to wonder what song is playing around you. The wearable can identify the track and display the result.

Of course, a wearable listening to conversations and sounds around you raises privacy concerns. However, Apple has assured that Audio Intelligence isn’t designed to record and store things. The S11 chip comes with a Secure Enclave that keeps all the audio processing completely isolated. Once it’s been used, the audio will be instantly deleted.

Availability and pricing

Despite speculation that the current hardware shortages and rising prices could push the Apple Watch Ultra 4 price sky-high, Apple has kept things unchanged. The wearable starts at $799 in the U.S, which matches the launch price of its predecessor.

When it comes to monthly plans, the Ultra 4 can be financed at $66.58 per month over 12 months. Pre-orders are now available live in more than 50 countries, and the wearable will officially hit the stores on September 18, 2026.

Final thoughts: Should you upgrade?

The biggest question now is whether or not the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is worth the upgrade. Ultimately, that comes down to what you’re looking for from your wearable. If a longer battery life, more advanced health tracking, and new Audio Intelligence features are important to you, the Ultra 4 is undoubtedly a good pick.

However, if you’re someone already rocking a previous-generation Apple Watch Ultra, there’s no reason to upgrade. Sure, the Ultra 4 does bring major improvements, but they don’t completely change the experience or design. However, if you’re someone coming from an old Apple Watch, the Ultra 4 has enough features to make the upgrade completely worth it.

excerpt.rendered: Apple Watch Ultra 4 doesn’t completely reinvent the Ultra, but its longer battery life, smarter health tracking, and new AI features make it an interesting upgrade.

title.rendered: Apple A20 Pro: Everything You Need to Know About the New iPhone Chip

content.rendered:
Apple introduced A20 Pro with iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max on September 9. The same chip also appears in Apple’s technical specifications for iPhone Duo.

Apple says A20 Pro is built using the latest 2-nanometer process technology. It combines a 6-core CPU, a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. The company also claims higher memory bandwidth, faster graphics, and twice the AI processing of A19 Pro.

Those numbers come from Apple’s own comparisons. They describe Apple’s intended gains, but they are not independent benchmark results. A20 Pro’s real gaming performance, thermals, and battery efficiency will need hands-on testing after the new iPhones ship.

What A20 Pro includes

Apple’s iPhone Duo technical specifications provide the clearest breakdown of the chip:

The CPU handles general app and system work. The GPU handles graphics and games, while the Neural Engine and Neural Accelerators are aimed at machine-learning tasks such as Apple Intelligence features and computational photography. The core count tells us how Apple has built the chip, not how every app will perform.

What Apple’s 2nm claim means

Apple says A20 Pro is built using the latest 2-nanometer process technology. A process node is a manufacturing generation, not a performance score by itself. It does not tell us the chip’s clock speeds, its real power draw, or how quickly a particular game will run.

TSMC’s 2nm page offers general context. TSMC describes its N2 process as using first-generation nanosheet transistor technology and says volume production began in the fourth quarter of 2025. Apple does not name TSMC or specify that transistor structure on its A20 Pro pages, so TSMC’s description should not be read as independent confirmation of Apple’s exact implementation.

Apple’s A20 Pro comparisons with A19 Pro

Apple’s Newsroom announcement gives three headline comparisons with A19 Pro:

  • 50% more memory bandwidth.
  • Graphics performance up to 40% faster.
  • Double the AI processing power.

Apple ties the AI claim to the new Dual 16-core Neural Engine and its 32 total cores. More memory bandwidth can help move data between the chip and memory, while the larger GPU and Neural Accelerators give Apple more hardware for graphics and machine-learning workloads.

The important qualifier is “Apple says.” These are company comparisons, not independent tests. They also do not mean every app will run 50% faster or that every game will show a 40% frame-rate increase.

The package and cooling design matter too

The process node is only part of A20 Pro’s design. Apple says the package is inspired by its M-series chips, with the silicon die placed side by side with memory. That moves memory out of the chip’s thermal path and lets A20 Pro attach directly to a next-generation vapor chamber.

Apple says the vapor chamber has three times the surface area of the previous generation on iPhone 17 Pro. With new thermally conductive materials and the new package, Apple claims up to 40% better sustained performance than the previous generation.

That claim is separate from the up-to-40% graphics comparison with A19 Pro. The graphics number describes Apple’s chip comparison. The sustained-performance number describes Apple’s claim for the chip and cooling system against the previous iPhone Pro generation. Neither is an independent test. For background, the earlier iPhone 17 Pro vapor-chamber design shows why heat management matters during long workloads, but its gaming results do not tell us how A20 Pro will perform.

What A20 Pro could change in daily use

Camera processing

Apple says the Neural Engine accelerates computational photography. That could give the new camera pipeline more room for tasks such as image processing, low-light adjustments, video effects, and Apple’s Reference Image features on iPhone 18 Pro. The final photo still depends on the camera sensors, lenses, software, and Apple’s image processing choices. A20 Pro’s core count alone cannot prove better photos.

Apple Intelligence and Siri AI

The Dual 16-core Neural Engine is designed for on-device AI models. Apple says A20 Pro brings double the AI processing power of A19 Pro, while Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute for heavier work.

That hardware headroom should matter most as iOS 27 expands Siri AI and Apple Intelligence across apps, photos, the Camera app, and system actions. It does not make every Siri request local, and it does not remove software, language, or regional availability limits. Apple is rolling out Siri AI as a beta with iOS 27.

Graphics and gaming

The 7-core GPU, Neural Accelerators, hardware ray tracing, and larger vapor chamber give A20 Pro the hardware Apple is using to target demanding games and longer AI workloads. That combination targets the kind of long, demanding work where heat can limit performance.

Real frame rates, surface temperatures, throttling, and battery drain still need independent testing. Apple has not published those results for A20 Pro.

Battery efficiency

Apple calls A20 Pro its most powerful and efficient iPhone chip design yet and links the new iPhones’ battery improvements partly to more efficient Apple silicon. That does not isolate the chip’s contribution. Battery size, the display, the C2 modem, software, and the workload all affect how long an iPhone lasts.

A20 Pro is separate from N1 and C2

A20 Pro is the main application processor. It is not the wireless or cellular modem hardware.

Apple says iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max use N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Apple also identifies C2 as its next-generation cellular modem system. The iPhone Duo specifications list A20 Pro, N1, and C2 as separate components too.

In practice, these chips work as part of the same phone, but they have different jobs. A20 Pro handles apps, graphics, camera computation, and on-device AI. N1 handles wireless networking. C2 handles cellular connections and their related power demands.

Which iPhones get A20 Pro?

Apple lists A20 Pro in iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. The phones do not have identical designs, batteries, displays, or cooling systems, so the same chip name does not guarantee identical sustained performance across all three models.

For context, U.S. iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max preorders begin at 5 a.m. PT on September 12, with availability on September 18. iPhone Duo preorders begin at 5 a.m. PT on October 16, with availability on October 23.

title.rendered: Download official iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max wallpapers

content.rendered:
Apple has officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, bringing new colours and a fresh set of wallpapers to match. If you love Apple’s wallpapers, you don’t have to wait for the new iPhone to enjoy them. Here, you can download the official iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max wallpapers in high resolution for free and give your current iPhone a fresh look.

iPhone 18 Pro lineup brings fresh new colours

Apple’s latest Pro models come in Black, Silver, Glacier, and the new Burgundy finishes, with colour-matched back glass. So, the wallpapers below are designed around that same understated, glowing aesthetic.

The wallpapers have that distinctive Apple feel with dark gradients, soft lighting, curved shapes, and just the right amount of glow to make the Lock Screen look luxurious without competing with my icons or widgets.

If you want the iPhone 18 Pro feel on your existing iPhone, these are worth trying.

Download iPhone 18 Pro stock wallpapers

I’ve included all the official versions so you can switch the personality of your iPhone depending on your mood.

Download: Black | Glacier | Silver | Burgundy

The wallpapers have the same subtle curves and glowing edges, which work surprisingly well with iOS 27’s redesigned Liquid Glass interface.

  • Black: The most dramatic option, with a deep charcoal background and subtle white highlights.
  • Glacier: A soft icy-blue version that gives the Lock Screen a brighter, cleaner appearance.
  • Silver: The minimalist choice, with an almost-white metallic glow.
  • Burgundy: My favourite of the four, with a rich red wine tone that matches Apple’s new Pro finish.

Tap the Download button above to save the wallpapers in the original resolution to your device gallery.

What’s new in iPhone 18 Pro?

The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max bring a mix of performance, camera, and design upgrades that make Apple’s latest Pro lineup more capable and polished.

At the heart of the new models is the A20 Pro chip, which delivers faster performance and improved capabilities for demanding tasks and AI features. Apple has also upgraded the main camera with a 48MP Fusion sensor and variable aperture, giving users more control over their photos.

The Pro models also get improved battery life and a redesigned Dynamic Island that can show more Live Activities. However, in terms of design, Apple retained the iPhone 17 Pro’s camera plateau. For me, the new Burgundy finish is among the most eye-catching changes, giving the iPhone 18 Pro a distinctly fresh look.

Final thoughts

You don’t need to buy an iPhone 18 Pro to enjoy its new look. Just download your favourite wallpaper, set it on your iPhone, and give your Lock Screen a fresh makeover.

Know someone excited about the iPhone 18 Pro? Share these wallpapers with them; they’ll thank you later!

You might also like:

  • Download the official iPhone Duo wallpapers

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max: Everything You Need to Know

content.rendered:
Apple has announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max with a variable-aperture main camera, the A20 Pro chip, and a new vapour chamber. Both models share the same Pro camera system and core hardware. The Pro Max adds the larger display and Apple’s 45-hour video playback claim.

For U.S. buyers, preorders begin Friday, September 12, at 5:00 a.m. PT. Availability starts Friday, September 18.

Price, storage, and release date

Both models start with 256GB of storage. Apple also lists 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB capacities for each size.

Apple’s U.S. Store page lists both models and their current configurations. The official iPhone 18 Pro page confirms the 5:00 a.m. PT preorder time and September 18 availability.

Design and Dynamic Island changes

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max use an aluminium unibody with colour-matched back glass. The four finishes are black, silver, glacier, and burgundy.

Apple lists Ceramic Shield back glass and Ceramic Shield 2 on the front. The phones also retain Camera Control and the Action button. The 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR displays support ProMotion up to 120Hz.

The Dynamic Island is smaller and can show up to three Live Activities at the same time. That could be useful for keeping a score, directions, and music controls visible without switching between apps. Face ID still sits behind the display area for unlocking and authentication.

A20 Pro and the new vapour chamber

Apple says A20 Pro is built on the latest 2-nanometer process and has a 6-core CPU, a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the CPU is faster than the competition, while the chip has 50 per cent more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, a GPU up to 40 per cent faster than A19 Pro, and twice the AI processing power through the new Neural Engine.

A20 Pro also powers iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable iPhone. The two phones have different displays, batteries, and thermal designs, so the same chip does not mean identical performance. Our A20 Pro guide breaks down the chip separately.

Those are Apple comparisons, not independent benchmark results. The same applies to Apple’s thermal claim. The next-generation vapour chamber has three times the surface area of the previous generation, and Apple says it enables up to 40 per cent better sustained performance than iPhone 17 Pro.

If you are weighing the upgrade against the previous generation, iPhone 17 Pro: Everything You Need to Know provides useful context for the earlier chip and cooling design.

Both models also use Apple’s N1 wireless chip, which enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. The C2 modem system adds Apple’s stated improvements to cellular quality and reliability, faster uploads than C1X, 15 per cent lower energy use, and mmWave support in the U.S.

Three 48MP rear cameras with variable aperture

The main camera is a 48MP Fusion sensor with a variable aperture. Apple gives it four settings: f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4.0.

The widest f/1.48 setting lets in more light. The narrower f/4.0 setting gives more depth of field, which can help keep more of a group or scene in focus. The camera can adjust automatically, or you can choose an aperture yourself through the new Pro controls.

The rest of the system includes a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera for 0.5x and macro shots, plus a 48MP Fusion Telephoto camera with 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom options. Apple lists 16x as the total optical-quality zoom range.

Pro controls put aperture, shutter speed, white balance, and a histogram within easier reach in the Camera app. Photographic Styles 3 adds texture and grain controls alongside tone and color adjustments. Smart focus tracking can keep a moving subject in focus, even when it leaves the frame and returns.

Apple Reference Image is another unusual addition. Apple says the Main camera can sign sensor data at capture, while Private Cloud Compute creates an unalterable reference image that appears beside the main photo in Photos. Users can compare the two images to check whether edits were made.

For a comparison point, the iPhone 17 Pro camera breakdown covers the earlier 48MP camera system and its 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom options.

Video features for creators

The new camera system adds several changes that matter beyond still photography:

  • You can apply Cinematic effects after recording regular video, with support for video shot at up to 60 fps.
  • Low-light video can adjust the aperture and frame rate to produce brighter footage in dark scenes.
  • Time-lapse supports 4K resolution and Dolby Vision HDR.
  • Audio Mix can separate voices and music from unwanted background sound.
  • Pro video tools include ProRes RAW, Apple Log 2, genlock for multicamera sync, and 4K 120 fps Dolby Vision.
  • Dual Capture records from the front and rear cameras at the same time.

Both phones also have an 18MP Centre Stage front camera, ultra-stabilised video, and Centre Stage for video calls.

Battery life and charging

The U.S. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are eSIM-only and do not have a physical SIM tray. Apple says the eSIM-only design leaves room for a larger battery and adds two hours of video playback compared with versions that include a physical SIM tray.

Apple rates the U.S. eSIM-only iPhone 18 Pro for up to 36 hours of video playback and the iPhone 18 Pro Max for up to 45 hours. The Pro Max figure is six hours higher than Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro Max comparison. Apple also lists up to 30 hours of use per charge for the Pro Max under a new battery usage model. That is a different measure from video playback.

Charging is faster, too. Apple says both models can reach 50 percent in around 15 minutes with a compatible power adapter. Wireless charging can reach 50 percent in 30 minutes. On the Pro Max, a five-minute wired charge can provide around seven hours of video playback.

These are Apple’s published battery and charging claims, not a promise of normal daily battery life.

iOS 27 and Apple Intelligence

The iPhone 18 Pro models feature iOS 27, Apple Intelligence, and Siri AI. Apple says iOS 27 and Apple Intelligence become available on September 14. Siri AI begins rolling out in beta in English on the same day.

Siri AI can use personal context, take actions in apps, and answer questions about what the camera sees. iOS 27 also brings Apple Intelligence tools for photo editing, Image Playground, Safari, Messages, Mail, and Shortcuts. Apple’s system uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute, with availability varying by language and region.

For the wider software picture, Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27 cover the features that will also reach other supported iPhones.

For U.S. shoppers, the split is simple. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 with a 6.3-inch display, while the $1,299 Pro Max gives you a 6.9-inch screen and Apple’s up-to-45-hour video playback claim.

excerpt.rendered: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max start at $1,199 in the U.S. Here’s what changes with the camera, A20 Pro, design, battery, and iOS 27 update.

title.rendered: AirPods 5: Price, features, ANC, and everything you need to know

content.rendered:
Apple has just announced the new AirPods 5 at its Surprise and Shine event, and there’s one upgrade that immediately caught my attention: Active Noise Cancellation is finally coming to Apple’s entry-level open-ear AirPods. Starting at $129, AirPods 5 also bring improved sound, Siri AI, Live Translation, and better durability.

Here’s everything you need to know about AirPods 5, including their price, features, battery life, and whether the $149 model with a Wireless Charging Case is worth the extra money.

Apple brings Active Noise Cancellation to entry-level AirPods

If I had to pick one feature that defines AirPods 5, it’s ANC.

Apple has finally brought Active Noise Cancellation to its more affordable open-ear AirPods. And this isn’t just Apple quietly checking a box on the feature list. The company says AirPods 5 can remove up to 50% more external noise than AirPods 4 with ANC, thanks to a new multiport acoustic architecture and improved computational audio algorithms.

That is particularly interesting because AirPods 5 don’t use silicone ear tips. Instead, they retain Apple’s open-ear approach. That means I can still hear some of the world around me while wearing them, but the earbuds actively work to reduce unwanted background noise.

AirPods 5 also include:

  • Transparency mode
  • Adaptive Audio
  • Conversation Awareness

Transparency mode has been improved to make nearby voices and sounds feel more natural. Adaptive Audio automatically blends ANC and Transparency mode depending on my surroundings, while Conversation Awareness lowers media volume when I start talking to someone.

AirPods 5 key features you need to know

ANC may be the headline feature, but there’s considerably more going on here.

Design: Familiar, but more durable

Apple isn’t completely reinventing the AirPods design with AirPods 5. Instead, the company is sticking with its open-ear form factor and focusing on what happens inside.

One of the more useful upgrades is durability. AirPods 5 offer an IP57 rating for resistance to dust, sweat, and water, making them better suited to workouts and everyday use. The earbuds also use Apple’s H2 chip, which powers features such as ANC and other computational audio capabilities.

This is important because AirPods 5 aren’t simply AirPods 4 with a new name. Apple has reworked the acoustic architecture and processing behind them.

Improved sound quality

Apple is borrowing some of the ideas behind its higher-end AirPods Pro and adapting them for AirPods 5.

The new earbuds feature an all-new multiport acoustic architecture and next-generation Adaptive EQ. Apple says this produces richer and more detailed sound across a wider range of ear shapes.

AirPods 5 also support:

  • Personalised Spatial Audio
  • Dynamic head tracking
  • Adaptive EQ
  • Computational audio

The Spatial Audio experience is designed to make supported content feel more immersive, with the sound appearing to surround me rather than simply coming from two tiny speakers. And because Adaptive EQ adjusts the sound based on how the earbuds fit, the experience isn’t designed around one perfect ear shape.

That’s a small but important detail for open-ear earbuds, where fit can have a noticeable impact on how music sounds.

Siri AI and Apple Intelligence

This is where AirPods 5 start feeling less like traditional earbuds and more like an extension of the iPhone. With a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone, Apple now lets you use Siri AI hands-free through AirPods.

Apple says the new Siri AI can understand personal context across things such as messages, emails, and photos, while also handling app actions and broader questions.

For example, I could ask Siri to find the restaurant reservation buried in an email or play a song someone recommended in a message. There’s also a surprisingly nice addition. Siri Interactions will let you respond to Siri by nodding your head for yes or shaking it for no. I can see it being useful when I don’t want to speak out loud.

There is an important catch, though. Siri AI is rolling out in beta with iOS 27, so this isn’t something every AirPods 5 owner will necessarily get right away. Apple says Siri AI initially rolls out in English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish support coming in October. Availability can also vary by region and language.

Live Translation on AirPods 5

Live Translation is probably the feature I’ll be watching most closely after launch.

Powered by Apple Intelligence, Live Translation lets AirPods users hear conversations translated into their preferred language.

Apple says you can set up the feature through the Translate app, download the required languages, and start Live Translation by:

  • Pressing both AirPods stems simultaneously
  • Saying, “Siri, start Live Translation”
  • Using the Action button on a compatible iPhone

The feature is available across the AirPods lineup with compatible devices, software, firmware, and Apple Intelligence activated, although Apple notes that language and regional availability vary.

Battery life on AirPods 5

Battery life depends on which AirPods 5 model I choose.

The standard AirPods 5 provide up to four hours of listening with ANC enabled on a single charge.

The AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case increase that to five hours with ANC, while the charging case provides up to 22 hours of listening with ANC.

That extra hour isn’t groundbreaking on its own, but it becomes more compelling when combined with the additional controls and charging options available on the $149 model.

AirPods 5 price, compatibility, and availability

Here’s the simple breakdown:

Apple opened preorders on September 9, and both models become available in stores on September 18, 2026.

At this price, the standard AirPods 5 become the most affordable way to get this combination of ANC and Apple’s newer AirPods features.

For the full feature set, Apple recommends pairing AirPods 5 with an Apple device running the latest operating system software. Some of the more advanced features require an Apple Intelligence-enabled device.

AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case: What do you get for the extra $20?

Here’s where I’d think a little more before placing an order.

Apple charges $20 more for AirPods 5 with the Wireless Charging Case, bringing the price to $149. And for me, that $20 looks surprisingly reasonable.

The upgraded model gives me:

  • Wireless Charging Case
  • Qi wireless charging
  • Apple Watch charger support
  • USB-C charging
  • Up to five hours of ANC listening
  • Up to 22 hours with ANC using the case
  • On-stem volume control
  • Built-in speaker for Find My

The volume swipe is especially interesting. Apple says AirPods 5 introduce a force sensor with volume swipe, allowing users to swipe up or down on the stem to adjust volume. It’s the first time Apple has brought this capability to its open-ear AirPods.

And honestly, that’s the sort of feature I appreciate more than another headline-grabbing AI feature.

What I like about AirPods 5

  • ANC at $129: Apple has taken a feature that previously pushed me toward more expensive AirPods and put it into a $129 open-ear model.
  • The open-ear approach: Not everyone likes silicone ear tips. AirPods 5 give people who prefer Apple’s traditional open-ear fit a way to get ANC without switching to an in-ear design.
  • Siri AI makes more sense with AirPods: When I’m walking, driving, cooking, or carrying something, pulling out an iPhone isn’t always convenient. Having Siri understand personal context in AirPods interactions feels much more natural.
  • The $149 model is well thought out: The upgraded case adds better battery life and volume swipe.
  • Better durability: The improved dust, sweat, and water resistance is another welcome change for something I’m likely to wear while working out or commuting.

What I don’t like about AirPods 5

AirPods 5 look impressive, but I wouldn’t call them perfect.

  • Open-ear ANC still has limits: Apple can use microphones, computational audio, and clever acoustic engineering to reduce external noise, but an open-ear earbud doesn’t create the same physical isolation as a sealed in-ear design.
  • Advanced features are not for everyone: Siri AI is rolling out as a beta, while Live Translation requires compatible Apple hardware, software, firmware, and supported languages or regions.
  • There’s no charging cable in the box: Apple doesn’t include a USB-C charging cable or power adapter with AirPods 5.

Final thoughts

AirPods 5 could be the most interesting AirPods upgrade of 2026. It has taken several features that used to push buyers toward higher-end AirPods and brought them down to a $129 starting price.

The headline is obviously Active Noise Cancellation, but the bigger picture is more interesting. Improved acoustics, Adaptive EQ, Personalised Spatial Audio, Siri AI, Live Translation, better durability, and a more capable charging case all come together in one package.

If I wanted the cheapest way into the new AirPods experience, I’d choose the $129 AirPods 5. But if I were spending my own money, I’d probably choose the $149 AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case. For just $20 more, I get longer ANC battery life, wireless charging, Apple Watch charging support, and the new volume swipe control.

What do you think about the new AirPods 5? Let me know in the comments below!

title.rendered: iPhone Duo: Everything You Need to Know About Apple’s First Foldable iPhone

content.rendered:
Apple introduced iPhone Duo during its September 9 event, making it the company’s first foldable iPhone. The official iPhone Duo product page confirms a 7.6-inch inner display, a 5.4-inch outer screen, and Touch ID in the side button. In the U.S., preorders begin October 16 at 5:00 a.m. PT, with availability starting October 23.

Apple’s pages also draw a useful boundary. The phone uses a two-camera rear system and Touch ID. The battery and performance numbers are Apple’s own test claims.

The same A20 Pro chip powers iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but those phones use a conventional design and a three-camera Pro system.

Two OLED displays in a foldable design

iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR all-screen OLED folding display on the inside and a 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR all-screen OLED display on the outside. The inner panel has a nano-texture finish and wide-angle OLEDs.

Both screens include Dynamic Island, Always-On display, and ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. Apple lists 1000 nits of typical max brightness, 1600 nits of HDR peak brightness, and 3000 nits of outdoor peak brightness, with a 1-nit minimum brightness.

The official dimensions are:

  • Open: 6.48 inches wide, 4.64 inches high, and 0.21 inches thick.
  • Folded: 3.31 inches wide, 4.64 inches high, and 0.44 inches thick.
  • Weight: 8.96 ounces, or 254 grams.

Apple says the two screens keep a consistent aspect ratio, so content can move between the inner and outer displays without changing its basic shape. It also says the inner display uses multiple thin layers and optically clear adhesives that let the layers glide as the phone folds. The page describes Apple’s foldable display design, but it does not establish how the display will hold up in everyday use.

Titanium, Ceramic Shield, and Touch ID

The frame and hinge cover use Grade 5 titanium. Apple’s technical specifications list Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, Ceramic Shield on the back, and a scratch-resistant coating on the inner display. The phone has an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance, tested to a maximum depth of 6 meters for up to 30 minutes under IEC standard 60529.

iPhone Duo comes in Night Sky and Star White. It uses Touch ID instead of Face ID, with the fingerprint sensor built into the side button. Apple says the same sensor works whether the phone is open or folded.

iOS 27 adds more room for apps

iPhone Duo ships with iOS 27, which Apple has adapted for the two-screen design. In landscape mode, Split View lets you use two apps side by side on the inner display. In portrait mode, the wider layout gives you more room for the keyboard and browsing, while a video can stay pinned at the top as you use another app.

The phone can also sit at different angles. Apple shows it standing in StandBy mode as a clock, photo frame, or widget display. It can sit in a seated position for watching a show or following a workout, and it can stand on its own for hands-free video calls. When closed, the outer display is meant for quick, one-handed use.

The larger canvas also supports Apple Pencil (USB-C), although Apple says that support is coming later this year. For broader software context, see what changed in iOS 27 compared with iOS 26.

A20 Pro and Apple Intelligence

The A20 Pro chip has a 6-core CPU, a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the Neural Engine is designed for intensive AI workloads and pairs the chip with a vapor chamber thermal management system. Those are Apple’s hardware and performance claims, not independent benchmark or thermal results.

For the chip’s core design, Apple comparisons, and cooling system, see our A20 Pro guide.

Apple Intelligence powers Siri AI on iPhone Duo. Apple describes a more conversational assistant with personal context, broad world knowledge, Camera-based help, intelligent photo editing, and productivity features inside apps. The product page says Siri AI is rolling out in English, and Apple notes that feature availability can vary. The new Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27 provide a wider look at the software update, but the final availability still depends on Apple’s language and regional limits.

Two 48MP rear cameras, with 2x optical-quality zoom

The rear camera system has two listed cameras:

  • 48MP Fusion Main camera with a 26mm focal length, f/1.6 aperture, sensor-shift optical image stabilisation, and support for 24MP and 48MP photos.
  • 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera with a 13mm focal length, f/2.2 aperture, and a 120-degree field of view.

Apple lists 2x optical-quality zoom in, 2x optical zoom out, a 4x optical-quality zoom range, and digital zoom up to 10x. Its technical specifications also mention a 12MP optical-quality 2x Telephoto output under the Fusion Main camera. Apple does not list a separate telephoto lens for iPhone Duo, so that 2x mode should not be described as a third rear camera.

The outer camera is a 12MP Centre Stage camera. The inner display has an under-display FaceTime camera that records 1080p video. Apple also lists Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue, Duo FaceTime, Dual Capture, and Centre Stage for photos and video calls. The current iPhone Duo pages do not give it the separate Pro camera system listed for Apple’s Pro models.

USB-C, MagSafe, Qi2, and eSIM

iPhone Duo has a USB-C connector for charging, DisplayPort output, and USB 3 data transfer at up to 10Gb/s. Its wireless charging system supports MagSafe up to 25W and Qi2 up to 25W.

Apple’s technical specifications list the N1 wireless networking chip, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and the C2 cellular modem. The phone is eSIM-only and supports two active eSIMs while storing eight or more eSIMs. It does not support a physical SIM card.

Battery and charging claims

iPhone Duo uses two built-in rechargeable lithium-ion batteries. Apple claims up to 24 hours of typical use, up to 44 hours of video playback when using the outer display, and up to 31 hours when using the inner display. For streamed video, Apple lists up to 37 hours on the outer display and up to 26 hours on the inner display.

With a 60W-capable adapter or higher and a USB-C cable, Apple says the phone can reach 50% charge in around 20 minutes. With a 35W adapter or higher and a MagSafe Charger, it says 50% takes around 30 minutes. The adapters and MagSafe Charger are sold separately. These figures are Apple’s test claims, not real-world battery results.

U.S. price and availability

Apple’s U.S. Store page lists four storage options for iPhone Duo:

U.S. preorders start Friday, October 16, at 5:00 a.m. PT on Apple’s website and in the Apple Store app. iPhone Duo will be available from October 23 at Apple and through select carriers and partner stores.

title.rendered: These iPhones support iOS 27: Full list of compatible devices

content.rendered:
Apple has officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at its “Surprise and Shine” event, with both new Pro models arriving with iOS 27. First announced at WWDC 2026, Apple’s latest iPhone software is set to roll out as a free update on September 14. In a surprise move, no iPhones are losing support this year.

If you’re wondering whether your existing iPhone will get the new software, here’s the full list of iOS 27-compatible devices.

iOS 27 supported devices

Apple has confirmed that iOS 27 supports every iPhone capable of running iOS 26, along with the newly launched iPhone lineup.

  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro
  • iPhone 17, iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17e
  • iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 15, iPhone 15 Plus, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Plus, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone 14 Pro Max
  • iPhone 13, iPhone 13 mini, iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 13 Pro Max
  • iPhone 12, iPhone 12 mini, iPhone 12 Pro, iPhone 12 Pro Max
  • iPhone SE (2nd generation) and newer
  • iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, iPhone 11 Pro Max

Apple isn’t ending support for any iPhone

The biggest surprise isn’t a new device gaining support. It’s the fact that Apple didn’t remove any.

As a result, the devices many expected to lose support remain compatible with iOS 27.

  • iPhone 11
  • iPhone 11 Pro
  • iPhone 11 Pro Max
  • iPhone SE (2nd generation)

That means the iPhone 11 lineup has now received another year of major iOS support, extending its software lifespan beyond many earlier expectations.

For users still holding onto these devices, iOS 27 extends their run of major software updates by another year.

Will every iPhone get every iOS 27 feature?

The compatibility list may be unchanged, but Apple’s hardware requirements for certain features aren’t. Apple Intelligence, for instance, continues to require an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or a newer model. That means devices like the iPhone 11 and iPhone 12 series can install iOS 27 but won’t get Apple Intelligence features.

iOS 27 release timeline

Apple released the first developer beta of iOS 27 immediately after the WWDC 2026 keynote.

Another year for the iPhone 11…

With iOS 27, Apple continues its long-standing software support streak by keeping every iPhone supported by iOS 26 on the compatibility list. While some of the newest features remain limited to newer hardware, iPhone 11 users get at least one more year of major iOS updates.

Is your iPhone getting iOS 27? Let us know which model you’re using and whether you plan to install the update in the comments below.

title.rendered: iOS 27 features: Everything Apple announced at WWDC 2026

content.rendered:
iOS 27 is here, and Apple is putting Apple Intelligence at the center of the update. From a rebuilt Siri and AI-powered Shortcuts to new tools in Photos and Safari, the latest iPhone software brings changes to many of the apps people use every day.

The headline addition is Siri AI, a completely rebuilt version of Siri that can understand your personal context, hold natural conversations, and help you complete tasks across apps. But that’s only part of the story. Apple has also upgraded Safari, Photos, Shortcuts, Passwords, Messages, and several other apps while making the entire operating system faster and more responsive.

If you’ve been waiting for Apple Intelligence to move beyond demos and become part of everyday iPhone use, iOS 27 is Apple’s biggest step yet.

Here’s everything new in iOS 27, along with its release date and supported devices.

Table of Contents
  • Siri AI brings conversations, Visual Intelligence, and personal context
  • Safari can organize tabs and monitor websites for you
  • Liquid Glass gets more customization
  • Photos get Spatial Reframing, Extended, and better Clean Up
  • Shortcuts can create automations from natural language
  • Wallet App updates
  • Passwords can automatically update weak passwords
  • Apple Intelligence expands across core apps
  • iOS 27 is faster across the board
  • New parental controls and child safety tools
  • Shared Albums get Android and Windows support
  • iOS 27 compatible devices
  • iOS 27 release date
  • Is iOS 27 worth the upgrade?

Siri AI brings conversations, Visual Intelligence, and personal context

Apple spent years promising a smarter Siri. With iOS 27, it has finally arrived.

Siri AI is a completely rebuilt assistant powered by Apple Intelligence. It can understand information from across your apps, maintain natural conversations, and help complete tasks that previously required jumping between multiple apps.

For example, you can ask Siri where a friend recently moved, find photos from a specific trip, create reminders based on information from the web, or draft a message using details from previous conversations.

Apple has also introduced a dedicated Siri app that stores your conversation history and syncs it across supported Apple devices through iCloud.

Other Siri improvements include:

  • More natural and expressive voices
  • Improved dictation accuracy
  • Visual Intelligence integration
  • Richer conversational responses
  • Better app awareness and task completion

Safari can organize tabs and monitor websites for you

If you’re someone who constantly ends up with dozens of open tabs, Safari finally has a solution.

iOS 27 introduces automatic tab organization powered by Apple Intelligence. Safari can analyze your open tabs, identify related pages, and group them into topics automatically.

For example, if you’re planning a vacation, Safari can place hotel bookings, restaurant research, airline pages, and travel guides into the same group without any manual effort.

Apple is also introducing a new feature called Notify Me.

Instead of repeatedly checking a website for updates, you can ask Safari to watch the page for you. When something changes, such as tickets becoming available or a product returning to stock, Safari sends you a notification.

Safari also gains a feature called Describe an Extension. You can simply describe what you want a website to do, and Safari can create a custom extension that modifies the page accordingly.

Liquid Glass gets more customization

After introducing Liquid Glass last year, Apple is giving users more control over the look of the interface.

A new transparency slider allows you to adjust the appearance of Liquid Glass elements across the system. You can choose a cleaner, more transparent appearance or a stronger tinted effect depending on your preference.

Photos get Spatial Reframing, Extended, and better Clean Up

The Photos app receives three major Apple Intelligence upgrades.

  • Clean Up: Apple has improved the existing Clean Up tool, making it better at removing distracting objects while generating more natural-looking replacements.
  • Extend: The new Extend tool lets you expand the edges of an image, giving you more room for cropping, social media posts, or creative projects.
  • Spatial Reframing: This tool allows you to adjust the camera perspective after the photo has already been taken. You can move subjects into better positions, improve symmetry, and correct framing issues without needing to retake the picture.

Apple uses AI to generate the missing parts naturally, helping edits look more realistic.

Shortcuts can create automations from natural language

The Shortcuts app has always been powerful, but many users found it intimidating. Apple is solving that problem with Apple Intelligence.
Instead of manually building an automation step by step, you can simply describe what you want in plain English.

For example, you can type:

“When I leave work, text my partner that I’m on my way home and include my ETA.”

Shortcuts automatically creates the automation, adds the necessary actions, and even allows you to refine it further using natural language.

For many users, this could be the first time Shortcuts feels approachable.

Wallet App updates

Apple is adding a couple of new features to the Wallet app in iOS 27.

The first is support for digitizing physical passes. Instead of carrying certain paper-based passes, users can add supported versions to Wallet and access them directly from their iPhone.

Apple is also making it easier to split expenses. When paying with Apple Pay, users can divide a bill and settle balances using Apple Cash without switching between multiple apps.

Passwords can automatically update weak passwords

Managing passwords is important, but updating dozens of accounts can be a hassle.

With iOS 27, the Passwords app can automatically update eligible accounts to stronger passwords.

Using Apple Intelligence and Safari together, your iPhone can navigate supported websites, sign in securely, and replace weak credentials with stronger alternatives.

The result is better security with much less effort.

Apple Intelligence expands across core apps

Apple Intelligence is now deeply integrated across the apps many people use every day.

  • In Messages, your iPhone can suggest actions based on conversations, create reminders, and help locate photos mentioned in chats.
  • Mail offers smarter suggestions based on the contents of incoming messages.
  • Calendar can create events simply by understanding natural language.
  • The Phone app gains a feature called Call Context, which can automatically surface useful information before a call. For example, if you’re calling an airline, your iPhone may display the confirmation code it found in Mail so you don’t have to search for it manually.

iOS 27 is faster across the board

Apple also spent time improving performance throughout the operating system.

According to Apple:

  • Apps launch up to 30% faster
  • New photos appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster
  • AirDrop transfers are up to 80% faster
  • Network transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular are more reliable
  • Search results appear faster across Spotlight, Mail, and Photos

Another notable change is an upgraded CPU scheduler for older iPhones. Apple says the improvements extend all the way back to the iPhone 11, helping the devices manage system resources more efficiently.

New parental controls and child safety tools

Families aren’t being left out of this update. iOS 27 introduces Ask to Browse for website approvals, expands Communication Safety to include violent content, and refreshes Screen Time with new controls for managing app access throughout the day.

Shared Albums get Android and Windows support

If you’ve ever created a Shared Album only to realize that some friends or family members couldn’t participate because they use Android or Windows devices, iOS 27 removes that limitation. Apple now lets Android and Windows users join Shared Albums and add their own photos and videos.

Apple is also removing another long-standing limitation. Shared Albums now support full-resolution photos and videos, so the memories you share won’t lose quality in the process.

Must read: How to create a Shared Album on iPhone

iOS 27 compatible devices

Apple is keeping the same compatibility list as iOS 26, meaning every supported iPhone from the iPhone 11 lineup onward can run iOS 27. Moreover, the newly launched iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo will arrive with iOS 27.

However, some Apple Intelligence features will remain limited to newer iPhone models.

iOS 27 release date

Apple unveiled iOS 27 during its WWDC 2026 keynote on June 8, 2026, and the developer beta launched immediately, while the public beta arrived in July 2026.

Apple released the final version of iOS 27 to all users on September 14, 2026.

Is iOS 27 worth the upgrade?

iOS 27 isn’t defined by a single headline feature. Instead, Apple has woven Apple Intelligence throughout the operating system, from Siri and Safari to Photos, Shortcuts, and Passwords. If these features work as advertised, iOS 27 could end up feeling less like a traditional software update and more like a smarter version of the iPhone people already use every day.

Which iOS 27 feature are you most excited to try first? Let us know in the comments below.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: GTA 6 global release times: When does it launch in your region?

content.rendered:
If you’re planning to jump into GTA 6 as soon as possible, you’ll want to pay close attention to its release date and time. Why is that the case? Well, the game won’t have a global release on November 19, 2026. What Rockstar Games is planning this time around is a midnight release in every region.

This means gamers in countries such as New Zealand could get their hands on the game much earlier than those in Central America and Mexico. So, if you’re wondering when exactly GTA 6 will be available in your region, there’s no need to worry, as we’ve got you covered. Let’s take a look at GTA 6 global release times and dates.

GTA 6 launch times by region

As we’ve mentioned before, the GTA 6 release time will depend on your region, with the game becoming available at 12:00 AM local time. Both Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation players will be able to jump into the game at the same time in each region.

If you want to play GTA 6 as early as possible, Xbox players can change their console’s time zone to New Zealand through settings. However, this is a bit complicated on PlayStation as it requires purchasing the game on a new account.

With that in mind, here’s a complete breakdown of GTA 6 global release date and time, starting with the first region to get the game and ending with the last. –

GTA 6 PS5 edition controllers can now be pre-ordered

The GTA 6 pre-orders are now live for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series/X consoles. There are two separate editions to choose from, each with its own perks and cosmetics that you’ll be able to obtain once the game becomes playable on November 19, 2026. However, if you’re a die-hard fan of the franchise and want to get something extra, you can also pick up the exclusive GTA 6 PS5 edition controllers.

In a recent State of Play event, Sony revealed a brand-new DualSense controller based on GTA 6. Available in both black and white variants for $84.99, the controllers fully embody the aesthetic of Leonida, with palm trees on the handles and a giant “VI” logo across the touchpad.

These might seem a bit pricey, but they’re a must-have for collectors and fans. If you want to get your hands on this controller before launch, the GTA 6-themed DualSense controllers are available to pre-order through Sony and major retailers.

Conclusion

Many expected GTA 6 to have a simultaneous global launch, but as we’ve now learned, Rockstar is instead going with a midnight release in each specific region. This does mean that some players will be able to access the game much earlier than others, but there are ways to bypass this limitation depending on which console you’re playing on.

  • Why GTA 6 needs a first-person mode
