title.rendered: Fortnite v42.10 update patch notes: All changes confirmed for Battle Royale and OG Mode

content.rendered:
A notable Fortnite update, v42.10, is on schedule to launch on Thursday, September 3. Unlike last week’s update, this one packs three different sprites among other changes coming for the Battle Royale mode and also marks the start of Season X in Fortnite OG.

Over the past several days, Fortnite’s official social handles have been building hype for the forthcoming content drop. In doing so, they have put the spotlight on some of the most prominent features and new additions in this update, ranging from fan-made items to changes in the loot pool. In this article, you can find all such revealed changes coming to both Fortnite Battle Royale and Fortnite OG.

Fortnite Override Battle Royale updates

New sprites

The next lineup of incoming sprites is dominated by two fan-made ones, namely Avila215’s X-Ray Sprite and Enorull’s Onigiri Sprite. Originally, the latter fan’s Bullet Sprite was going to feature in the update, but it was swapped with another one of his sprite entries for undisclosed reasons.

  • X-Ray Sprite: It lets you see enemies through walls for a brief time.
  • Onigiri Sprite: It provides you with extra health upon using healing items.
  • Unknown knight-like sprite: The ability granted is unknown.

New Match Overrides

Match Overrides have significantly shaped the gameplay in the Battle Royale mode during the Fortnite Override season. These appear as giant cartridges on the map and allow the first player to interact with any one of them to choose from a range of different boost options, such as Sonic Speed, which steadily increases sprint speed and Speed Shooter, which increases the rate of fire and reload speed. Whichever boost is picked gets applied for all players in that particular match.

The following are the two new Match Overrides announced for Thursday’s update. Besides them, three more are confirmed to join, but there’s no information about what they are called.

  • Big Heads
  • Prop Hunt

New weapons

  • Holo Twister Assault Rifle
  • Deadeye Assault Rifle
  • Wrecker Revolver*

*Although Fortnite’s announcement image showed Striker Burst as the third weapon to be added in the loot pool, it was later corrected and revealed to be Wrecker Revolver instead.

Fortnite OG Season X updates

Apart from the Battle Royale mode, a flurry of changes are also planned to hit OG Mode as it transitions from Fortnite OG Season 9 to Season X. From new OG Pass skins to new points of interest on the map, there is a good variety of stuff in the update coming out this week.

New OG Pass items

  • X-Lord female variant skin
  • Ultima Knight variant skin
  • Catalyst variant skin

New locations on the map

  • Starry Suburbs
  • The Meteor
  • Tilted Town

New loot pool items

  • Junk Rift
  • Automatic Sniper Rifle
  • Glitched Forageable
  • B.R.U.T.E.

Victory Umbrella

A new victory umbrella inspired by the X glider is coming in Fortnite OG Season X. This item will be available to those who bag a Victory Royale in any standard match during the forthcoming season.

Confirmed future additions

Other than the items mentioned above, a few others have also been revealed to be dropping later during Season X. This glimpse gives us an exciting look at the near future of Fortnite OG mode.

  • SR Tactical Sub-Machine Gun
  • Shield Bubble
  • Zapper Trap
  • Spicy Taco Forageable

Fortnite v42.10 update release schedule

All the aforementioned changes and new additions will roll out on September 3, after a certain period of server downtime, which is expected to start at 1 AM PT or 4 AM ET and is expected to last about 3 hours. It’s worth noting that matchmaking should be inactive about 30 minutes before this downtime. You can expect to jump back into Fortnite and enjoy the new update at a fixed time as laid out below.

Wrapping up

Given the volume of content packed in the Fortnite v42.10 update, it seems fair to say that once the update drops, players will have a lot of places to explore and a lot of items to collect. This should help the game raise its engagement levels, an area which has dwindled over the years, as reports have shown.

On the surface, Epic Games seems to understand well the task of doing everything in their control to boost Fortnite’s daily player count. Whether or not the developer will be able to execute the task well before any serious call, such as the major layoffs earlier in 2026, needs to be made is another discussion. However, if ingenious features—such as the introduction of sprites in gameplay—continue to come out at a good rate, the Tim Sweeney-led company should be able to steer the ship back on track.

  • Fortnite Override: Full list of admin panel codes and how to use them

title.rendered: iOS 27 may let you switch your phone number between two iPhones

content.rendered:
Apple appears ready to let one phone number move between two iPhones in iOS 27. Its beta iPhone quick switch documentation describes active and passive devices for the same number, while a MacRumors forum demo shows the setup screens for a feature called “iPhone Handoff.”

This could be useful if you want to keep a newer iPhone as your main device and use an older one for travel, exercise, or situations where you do not want to carry your everyday phone. It is still a beta feature, and carrier support will decide when you can use it.

How iPhone Handoff is supposed to work

The setup appears under Settings > Cellular. You choose a main iPhone and a companion iPhone, then transfer a companion eSIM to the second device. The main iPhone keeps the primary eSIM and remains the place where cellular settings are managed.

The eSIM transfer process is familiar, but the result is different. Instead of permanently moving your line to a new phone, iPhone Handoff lets the active phone change between two enrolled iPhones.

The demo suggests that unlocking one of the phones makes it the active device for the number. iOS may show a Dynamic Island notification when the service moves. Location sharing also follows the iPhone that is currently using the number.

Apple’s developer documentation uses the terms active and passive rather than promising that both phones stay fully connected at the same time. Apps can receive a notification when the state changes, which gives developers a way to move app data or credentials to the phone you are using.

This is different from regular Handoff

Apple already uses Handoff to move activities such as a Safari page or a document from one device to another. The new iPhone Handoff feature deals with cellular service. It changes which iPhone carries your phone number, so the two features should not be confused.

Carrier support is the biggest question

You will need two iPhones running iOS 27, but that will not be enough on its own. The forum demo says carrier support is required and points to T-Mobile in the United States and Telekom.de in Germany as early examples. It also says T-Mobile’s enrollment server had the feature disabled during testing.

That means an iOS 27 beta installation does not guarantee that the option will appear in Settings. Apple has not published a final carrier list or confirmed when enrollment will open for the public.

iPhone Handoff is coming with iOS 27

iOS 27 is still in beta and is expected to launch in September 2026. Apple first mentioned the capability at WWDC, but the beta demo provides the clearest look at how it may work. The feature name, carrier requirements, and setup flow could still change before the final release.

For the broader update, see the iOS 27 feature roundup. For now, iPhone Handoff looks like a practical option for people who already own two iPhones and want to use one number instead of setting up a second line.

title.rendered: Claude Code can now use your Mac in the background while you work

content.rendered:
Anthropic is making Claude’s computer-use feature less disruptive on Mac. In an official post from Claude’s X account, the company says Claude can now click, type, and open apps in the background through Claude Cowork and Claude Code while you continue using your computer.

The update is aimed at Pro and Max users. It is useful for repetitive desktop work, but it does not turn Claude into a fully unattended assistant. You still need to approve app access, and your Mac must remain awake with Claude Desktop open.

Claude can control apps without taking over your screen

Anthropic’s current help documentation says background windows work on macOS 15 or later. Claude can interact with approved apps without taking over your pointer or keyboard, and it generally waits if you are in the middle of typing.

That makes computer use more practical for tasks such as moving information between apps, checking a dashboard, or running a repetitive workflow while you do something else. The earlier Claude Mac computer-use rollout required handing more of the desktop to the agent. Background windows reduce that friction.

Permissions still matter

Computer use is off by default. Claude’s Code documentation says Mac users must grant Accessibility permission so Claude can click and type, along with Screen Recording permission so it can see the screen. Claude also asks for approval before it uses a specific app.

Those permissions are important because computer use operates on the real desktop. Anthropic warns that screenshots can include anything visible in an approved app, including private documents or personal information. It also says the feature can struggle with complex workflows, so background mode is better suited to repeatable, low-risk tasks than sensitive work.

Who gets background computer use?

Anthropic’s help page lists computer use as a beta feature for Claude Pro and Max. It is available in Claude Cowork and Claude Code inside the Claude Desktop app. Team and Enterprise plans do not have access to computer use at this time.

The wider computer-use feature is also documented for Windows, but the background-window behavior in this update is the Mac experience and requires macOS 15 or later. The Claude Desktop app must stay open, and the computer must remain awake while the task runs.

Developers already using Claude Code with Apple’s iOS Simulator may find this useful for workflows that need both the simulator and other Mac apps. For everyone else, the practical change is simple: Claude can keep working in a background window while you keep the rest of the desktop under your control.

title.rendered: I compared Pixel Buds Pro 2 vs. AirPods Pro 3: Which is actually better for everyday use?

content.rendered:
Premium wireless earbuds have become incredibly good, making it harder than ever to choose between them. The Google Pixel Buds Pro 2 and Apple AirPods Pro 3 are two of the biggest names in the market, promising excellent sound, powerful noise cancellation, smart features, and all-day comfort.

But specs only tell part of the story. For everyday use, what really matters is how these earbuds feel when you’re commuting, taking calls, working out, listening to music, or simply wearing them for hours. So, in this Pixel Buds Pro 2 vs AirPods Pro 3 comparison, I’ll focus on the differences that actually matter. So, you can decide which one you should buy.

Pixel Buds Pro 2 vs AirPods Pro 3: Quick comparison

On paper, this looks surprisingly close. In real life, though, these two earbuds feel very different.

Pixel Buds Pro 2 vs AirPods Pro 3: What’s the actual difference I felt

The easiest mistake when comparing premium earbuds is obsessing over tiny technical differences. A bit better noise cancellation, an additional hour of battery life, or a slightly upgraded Bluetooth. The truth is that most people will not be able to spot these differences.

What you will notice is friction. That’s where the Pixel Buds Pro 2 vs AirPods Pro 3 comparison gets interesting.

Design and everyday comfort

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 take a refreshingly practical approach to comfort. Google redesigned them to be smaller and lighter than their predecessor, and the twist-to-adjust stabilizer is one of those features that sounds minor until I actually used it throughout the day.

Working at a desk? Keep the fit relaxed. Heading to the gym? Twist them for a more secure hold. That flexibility gives the Pixel Buds Pro 2 a personality that feels unusually practical.

Google also offers four ear tip sizes, and the compact design was developed using extensive ear-shape data. The result is a pair of earbuds clearly designed around long-term wear rather than simply looking futuristic.

The AirPods Pro 3 take a different route. Apple’s design remains instantly recognizable, but Apple has expanded fit options with five ear tip sizes, including XXS. I use the built-in Ear Tip Fit Test to find the right eartip for the best sound and noise cancellation.

If you’ve historically struggled to find earbuds that seal properly, more tip sizes and a fit test can make a bigger difference than a new audio codec ever will.

My take: For everyday movement, workouts, and people who constantly adjust their earbuds, I prefer the Pixel Buds Pro 2 approach.

Sound quality

Here’s where I think the conversation gets unnecessarily tribal. People often want one simple answer: Which one sounds better, Pixel Buds Pro 2 or AirPods Pro 3? However, at this stage, premium earbuds have advanced to the point where it is all about the kind of music you listen to.

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 use custom 11mm dynamic drivers, with Google emphasizing powerful bass, richer mids, and smoother treble. There’s also spatial audio with head tracking and a 5-band EQ for people who actually want to customize their sound. Whenever I want more bass, cleaner vocals, or a flatter sound, I have more room to experiment.

The AirPods Pro 3 take the opposite approach. Apple’s strength has always been tuning for consistency. The custom driver, Adaptive EQ, and Personalized Spatial Audio are designed to deliver a polished sound without requiring you to spend 20 minutes moving sliders.

And honestly, that’s probably what most people want. I simply put them in, press play, and they sound good. However, in response to user requests, Apple has finally added custom EQ settings to AirPods in iOS 27.

My take: If I were recommending earbuds to an everyday listener who doesn’t care about EQ, codecs, or audio settings, I’d lean toward the AirPods Pro 3.

Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency Mode

This is where premium earbuds earn their price.

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 use Google’s Silent Seal 2.0 technology alongside the Tensor A1 chip. Its Adaptive Audio dynamically reduces environmental noise while maintaining awareness of what’s happening around you. Google also introduced Dynamic ANC, which adjusts noise cancellation in response to small changes in the earbud seal.

The AirPods Pro 3 combine Active Noise Cancellation with Adaptive Audio and Transparency Mode, and I really like Conversation Awareness, which reduces the music when I am talking to someone. In addition to the software features, the acoustic architecture and foam-infused ear tips enhance passive isolation.

Both are clearly designed to do more than simply offer an ON/OFF ANC switch. And that’s important.

My take: Apple wins the “set it and forget it” experience.

Call quality and voice features

This category matters far more than people admit. We all imagine ourselves buying premium earbuds for music. Then reality happens. Zoom calls, family calls, random meetings, voice notes.

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 come prepared for this chaos with beamforming microphones, wind-blocking mesh, Clear Calling, Conversation Detection, and AI-assisted voice processing. Google has also leaned heavily into Gemini integration. You can ask it to enable Active Noise Cancellation or change the sound profile.

The AirPods Pro 3 fight back with Voice Isolation, studio-quality audio recording, and microphones that also work closely with Apple’s computational audio features to improve voice clarity.

Beyond calls, Siri makes everyday tasks hands-free. Apple Intelligence also expands the experience with smarter Siri interactions and Live Translation,

My take: AirPods Pro 3 are best if you take calls on busy streets or in crowded spaces.

Battery life and charging

Battery specs are easy to ignore until the day your earbuds die halfway through a flight. Then suddenly, battery life becomes the most important feature in the world.

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 offer up to 8 hours of listening time with ANC enabled and up to 30 hours with the charging case. Without ANC, I could use them for up to 2 days on a single charge.

The AirPods Pro 3 also offer up to 8 hours of listening time with ANC enabled, but Apple’s case provides up to 24 hours of total listening time with ANC.

That’s a meaningful win for Google. Both support quick wired charging and Qi wireless charging. The AirPods Pro 3 also offer greater charging flexibility, as the case works with MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and Qi-certified chargers.

My take: Pixel wins the battery battle.

Ecosystem features: Gemini vs Siri and Apple Intelligence

Both are deeply connected to their respective ecosystems, but Google and Apple are taking noticeably different approaches.

With Gemini integration, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 can act as a hands-free gateway to Google’s ecosystem. I heavily depend on Gemini to brainstorm ideas with Gemini Live, manage tasks, add notes to Google Keep, schedule events in Google Calendar, and reply to messages without constantly reaching for my phone.

You can ask Gemini to adjust settings, such as enabling ANC or changing audio preferences, using just your voice. Moreover, Live Translate helps communicate in different languages in real time, and integration with Pixel Watch sleep detection pauses audio, disables touch controls, and silences notifications when you fall asleep.

The AirPods Pro 3 take a more ecosystem-focused approach. Siri lets you handle calls, messages, notifications, music, and everyday requests without touching your iPhone, while Apple Intelligence aims to make those interactions smarter and more context-aware.

Features such as Live Translation also expand what the AirPods can do, while Apple’s tight integration means everything works naturally across your iPhone and other Apple devices. The experience feels less like actively talking to an AI assistant and more like having technology quietly working in the background.

My take: If you want conversational AI and hands-free productivity, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 have the edge. But I am already invested in Apple’s ecosystem, so the AirPods Pro 3 remain hard to beat.

Fitness and daily lifestyle features

This category produced one of the more interesting surprises for me.

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 are clearly designed for movement. The twist-to-adjust stabilizer is practical, the earbuds are sweat- and water-resistant, and the secure fit makes them appealing for workouts.

But Apple has added something unexpected to the AirPods Pro 3: heart rate sensing during workouts. That changes the conversation. Your earbuds are now becoming part of your fitness ecosystem. The question is whether you actually need that feature.

Personally, I think that depends on what you’re already wearing. If you own an Apple Watch, the heart rate sensor in the AirPods Pro 3 may feel redundant. However, if you’re exercising without a smartwatch, it becomes more interesting. Moreover, it offers an FDA-approved Hearing Test and Hearing Aid feature for users with mild-to-moderate hearing loss.

My take: Pixel wins for fit; AirPods win for features.

Price and value for money

Price is one area where the difference is simple: the Pixel Buds Pro 2 cost $229, while the AirPods Pro 3 cost $249. That’s only a $20 gap, but value isn’t just about buying the cheaper earbuds.

For $229, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 are a really good buy for Android users looking for features like excellent ANC, battery life, integration with Gemini, Live Translate, and customizable audio controls.

The AirPods Pro 3 cost slightly more at $249, but Apple justifies the premium with deep ecosystem integration, advanced health features, seamless device switching, and Apple Intelligence-powered experiences.

My take: Pixel Buds Pro 2 for value, AirPods Pro 3 for Apple users.

Final verdict: Which should you buy?

After comparing the Pixel Buds Pro 2 vs AirPods Pro 3 from an everyday-use perspective, I don’t think there is a universal winner.

But I do think there is a clear answer for most people.

Buy the Pixel Buds Pro 2 if you:

  • Use a Pixel or Android phone
  • Want stronger total battery life
  • Prefer a more secure fit for workouts
  • Like customizable sound with EQ controls
  • Interested in Gemini and AI features
  • Want premium ANC without being locked into Apple

Buy the AirPods Pro 3 if you:

  • Use an iPhone and other Apple devices
  • Want the most seamless connectivity experience
  • Value intelligent, automatic audio features
  • Want advanced health and fitness features
  • Prefer earbuds that require almost zero setup or management

My opinion: The AirPods Pro 3 are the better everyday earbuds for iPhone users. But for Android users, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 are the smarter buy. They’re comfortable, powerful, customizable, and battery-friendly.

You may like to read: AirPods 5 vs AirPods 4: Which one should you buy?

title.rendered: Instagram will limit reach for unlabeled AI-generated profiles

content.rendered:
Instagram is changing how it treats accounts built around AI-generated people. In an announcement on Instagram’s Creators blog, the platform said it is renaming the account-level “AI creator” label to “AI-generated profile” and will limit the reach of profiles that feature an AI-generated person but do not use the label.

This is a recommendation penalty, not a ban on virtual influencers. Instagram says creators who add the label proactively will not see a change to their profile’s reach. It has not shared a percentage or explained exactly how much exposure an affected account could lose.

The label targets synthetic identities

The label is about who the profile represents, not every tool used to make a post. Instagram says creators who use AI for photo edits, captions, graphics, or other parts of a creative process do not need the profile-level label. A real creator using Instagram’s Restyle AI editing tool to change a photo is a different case from a profile built around an AI-generated person.

Instagram already uses post-level “AI info” labels. Meta’s policy says those labels can cover AI-generated or AI-altered images, videos, and audio. Content that was only modified by an AI tool may show the label in a post’s menu. Instagram says the new profile label can appear alongside an account’s content when a particular post does not already carry an AI label.

Meta’s separate Muse Image feature also raised questions about using public Instagram content to make AI-generated images. That is a different issue from the identity rule, and the relevant privacy setting can be turned off.

What happens if an account skips the label

Instagram says its systems will notify detected unlabeled profiles. Owners can check Account Status to see whether the profile has become ineligible for recommendations. In practical terms, that means fewer chances to reach people outside the account’s existing audience through Instagram’s discovery surfaces.

Instagram has been giving users more control over the topics that shape feed recommendations, but it has not said how large the reduction will be or whether every detected profile will be treated the same way.

To restore recommendation eligibility, a creator can edit the profile and turn on “AI-generated profile”. If the creator believes Instagram made a mistake, they can appeal through Account Status. Instagram says a successful appeal makes the profile and its content eligible for recommendations again.

A new enforcement step for an existing label

Instagram began testing the account-level “AI creator” label earlier this year. At that stage, it was optional and did not affect distribution. The current announcement changes the wording and adds a reach consequence for profiles Instagram detects as AI-generated but not properly labeled.

For operators of fully synthetic influencer accounts, the practical choice is to disclose the AI identity or risk losing recommendation reach. Human creators who use AI for editing and other production tasks are outside the rule as Instagram has described it.

excerpt.rendered: Instagram renames its AI creator label to AI-generated profile and may limit recommendations for unlabeled AI personas. Human creators using AI tools are not targeted.

title.rendered: Apple lets Mac App Store apps drop Intel support, but Intel Macs still work

content.rendered:
Apple is loosening a Mac App Store rule that has kept universal macOS apps compatible with Intel Macs. A September 1 developer notice, first reported by MacRumors, says universal Mac App Store apps that require macOS 13 or later can now remove Intel support and ship future updates as arm64-only.

This is an optional change for developers, not a shutdown of the Mac App Store on Intel hardware. Apple’s separate developer update on Rosetta confirms the wider move away from Intel code, but it does not say that every Mac App Store app must drop Intel support immediately.

Which apps are covered

Apple’s wording applies to a specific group of apps:

  • A universal macOS app with both Intel and Apple silicon code.
  • An app distributed through the Mac App Store.
  • An app whose minimum requirement is macOS 13 or later.
  • A future update in which the developer chooses to remove the Intel build.

The notice does not name any apps, and it does not set a date when all Mac App Store developers must make the switch. Developers can submit an arm64-only build to simplify development and reduce the app’s download and on-device size.

That also means an app with a minimum requirement below macOS 13 is not covered by this specific wording. The same is true for apps that developers leave as universal builds. The change is about Mac App Store submissions, not a new requirement for every app distributed on macOS.

What happens to Intel Macs

If a developer submits an arm64-only update, an Intel Mac will stay on the last version that supports its processor and will not receive later updates for that app. MacRumors reports that Intel users can continue using that last compatible version, but a specific app’s future support and redownload options remain up to its developer.

Apple has already set the larger hardware limit. macOS 26 Tahoe is the last macOS release with full Intel support, while macOS 27 Golden Gate supports Apple silicon Macs only. Apple says macOS 27 will ship this fall. The macOS 27 compatibility list shows which newer Macs can make the jump, and the macOS 26 Tahoe list helps Intel Mac owners check whether Tahoe is their final major release.

Intel Macs will not suddenly stop working. Apple’s deployment documentation says the company will continue providing software security updates for Intel-based Mac computers for three years. That does not guarantee new features or ongoing updates for every third-party app, so keeping the current compatible app version may become increasingly important.

Apple silicon users face a separate app deadline

The Rosetta part of this transition affects Apple silicon Macs running Intel-only apps. Apple says macOS 26.4 and later may show a warning when one of those apps launches. macOS 27 is the last release with general-purpose Rosetta support, so Intel-only Mac apps will not run on Apple silicon after that release. Apple plans to keep a limited Rosetta subset for older, unmaintained games.

If you use an Apple silicon Mac, select an app in Finder, press Command-I, and check the “Kind” field. “Application (Intel)” means the app still relies on Rosetta. “Application (Universal)” and “Application (Apple silicon)” are ready for the newer architecture. Apple recommends looking for an update in the App Store or on the developer’s website.

For Intel Mac owners, the practical change is app by app. The Mac App Store remains available, macOS 26 remains the last major system release, and developers can now decide when an eligible app leaves Intel behind.

title.rendered: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 with stronger coding and lower cache costs

content.rendered:
Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.1 on September 1, 2026, as the successor to Fable 5. The company calls it its most capable generally available Claude model, built for long-running coding, research, and knowledge work.

The release arrives less than three months after Claude Fable 5 became Anthropic’s first public Mythos-class model. Fable 5.1 is aimed at tasks that take hours, use tools across multiple steps, and need the model to review its own work.

Fable 5.1 focuses on long-running work

Anthropic says the gains are concentrated in tasks that need Claude to keep context, use tools, and check its work:

  • Coding: It can handle multi-file features, large refactors, migrations, debugging, and code review across long sessions. It can write tests and use vision to compare its output with a design.
  • Research and files: It follows multistep web research and can turn a question into a finished document, spreadsheet, or slide deck.
  • Computer use and vision: It operates browsers and desktop apps more reliably, recovers from failed steps, and reads dense charts, tables, and filings inside PDFs.

For developers, Fable 5.1 has a 1-million-token context window, a maximum output of 128,000 tokens, and the API ID claude-fable-5-1. Anthropic’s own benchmark table reports 52.6% for Fable 5.1 versus 24.7% for Fable 5 on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, and 73.4% versus 70.5% on CursorBench 3.2.0. Those are company-reported results, not independent tests.

For Apple developers, the release also arrives alongside Claude Code’s recent iOS Simulator support on Mac. The feature lets Claude Code build, run, and debug iPhone apps while the simulator sits beside the conversation.

Cache reads are cheaper, but base rates stay the same

Fable 5.1 keeps Fable 5’s API rates of $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. The model documentation lists cache reads at $0.25 per million tokens, down 75% from Fable 5’s $1 rate.

Anthropic estimates that change will lower typical workloads by around 25%. Highly agentic workloads could save up to about 45%, but those are Anthropic’s workload estimates rather than a guaranteed subscription discount.

Access depends on the plan

Fable 5.1 is available on Claude’s web, mobile, desktop, Cowork, Code, Design, Microsoft 365, and Claude Tag products. It is available on paid Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, but not on the Free plan.

The current plan rules differ by tier. Max users and premium Team or seat-based Enterprise users can use Fable models for up to 50% of their weekly usage limits at no extra cost. Pro users and standard Team or seat-based Enterprise users need usage credits from the start. API and usage-based Enterprise access use standard token billing. Developers can also use the model through Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry.

Long-running work is also the focus of Claude Cowork’s move to iPhone and web, which lets users start, check, and steer remote work while a session continues away from the desktop.

Fable 5.1 is public, Mythos 5.1 is restricted

Anthropic launched Claude Mythos 5.1 alongside Fable 5.1. The two models share the same underlying model, but Mythos has different, more permissive safeguards and is limited to trusted access programs for vetted cyberdefenders and life sciences professionals.

Fable 5.1 remains the public version, but flagged cybersecurity and biology requests may be routed to Claude Opus 4.8 or Opus 5 instead. Anthropic says users are not charged Fable rates for requests handled by those fallback models.

excerpt.rendered: Claude Fable 5.1 is now generally available on paid plans, with stronger agentic work, a 1M-token context window, lower cache-read costs, and safeguards.

title.rendered: Meta launches Muse Voice Transcribe for real-time dictation on Mac

content.rendered:
Meta has launched Muse Voice Transcribe, its first real-time audio perception model from Meta Superintelligence Labs. Meta’s announcement says it now powers dictation in Meta AI for Mac and voice input in Muse Code. Hold the Fn key on a Mac and the words are typed into the active app.

This is a model release with an immediate user-facing feature. Meta is also opening it to developers through the Meta Model API, so the same speech system can be used for live transcription rather than processing a recording at the end.

What Muse Voice Transcribe can do

Muse Voice Transcribe streams text while a person speaks. It combines automatic speech recognition with speaker diarization, which labels who is talking, and endpointing, which detects when a person has finished speaking.

Meta says the model can handle more than 20 speakers, audio sessions longer than an hour, and code-switching within or between sentences. It was trained on more than 70 languages, although only 25 are extensively validated for the initial release. Language, keyword, and context biasing can help with names and specialized terms.

Its main technical idea is “adaptive delay.” The model decides how long to listen before committing each word, waiting for more context when a word is difficult and moving faster when the speech is clear. Meta says this gives Muse Voice Transcribe a strong speed and accuracy tradeoff, and claims the top spot on Artificial Analysis’ streaming speech-to-text and public diarization benchmarks as of September 1.

Those rankings are launch-day claims from Meta. They do not guarantee the same results for every language, accent, noisy recording, or Mac app.

Availability, price, and Mac support

Meta says Muse Voice Transcribe is available today through the Meta Model API, Meta AI for Mac, and Muse Code. The Meta AI Mac app is a free beta download, although Meta says it is testing usage limits for some compute-heavy features.

For developers, 9to5Mac reports that API access costs $3 per 1,000 audio minutes, or about $0.18 per hour. The official launch post does not list a separate subscription for Muse Voice Transcribe inside the Mac app.

The Mac app itself is clearly labeled beta. Meta’s public announcement does not publish a Muse-specific hardware or macOS requirements table. An earlier 9to5Mac hands-on found the Meta AI app running natively on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later, but that is an observed app requirement, not an official Muse specification.

The release builds on Meta AI’s recent Mac app, which already brought window sharing and dictation across apps. The same model also adds voice input to Muse Code, Meta’s terminal-based coding agent.

Privacy is still the part Meta has not explained

Mark Zuckerberg said the Meta Model API has a zero-data-retention tier. Meta’s launch post does not say whether that setting applies to dictation in the Mac app, whether audio is processed locally, or how long app-side transcripts remain available.

That distinction matters because Fn-key dictation can place text into any active app. For casual notes, the feature looks convenient. For private work, check the product’s current privacy terms before dictating sensitive material.

title.rendered: GTA 6 map comparison: How much bigger is Vice City than GTA 5’s Los Santos

content.rendered:
At long last, we got our first look at GTA 6 gameplay on Thursday, which also put the spotlight on the various locations found in Vice City and Leonida. From derelict ghettos to posh downtown neighborhoods, the extended look at the game, which premiered on Netflix, gave a lot of visual fodder for anticipating fans.

Ever since the announcement of GTA 6 being set in a new iteration of Vice City, Rockstar’s own take on the American city of Miami, enthusiasts have been speculating about the game’s map. Thanks to two different trailers, several screenshots, and a half-hour-long gameplay video, the community now has a better idea of what to expect from GTA 6’s setting.

GTA 6 vs GTA 5 map size

Throughout its existence, almost each GTA mainline game has provided a bigger in-game world to explore compared to its predecessor. The one instance where that trend didn’t hold was the map of GTA 4, where its size was significantly smaller than that of GTA San Andreas’ map. However, the former may still have ‘felt’ bigger to certain players, given that Liberty City of the HD era was denser with more details and personality.

But, in GTA 6’s case, the map has once again increased in its length and breadth, per TGG’s report on his conversation with Rockstar Games Head of Development Rob Nelson. According to the popular YouTuber, GTA 6’s map is twice the size of GTA 5’s, and similarly, Vice City is also double the size of Los Santos.

Moreover, the total area of the forthcoming game’s world, which includes Vice City and its nearby counties, is eleven times bigger than GTA 5’s world, which consists of Los Santos and Blaine County. The counties that significantly add to the area of GTA 6’s map were revealed to be Vice-Dale County (where Vice City is situated), Mariana County, Kelly County, Lummox County, and Leonard County, as previously leaked by a hacker group called Cyberleek.

GTA 6 vs RDR 2 map size

Red Dead Redemption 2, which hit the shelves in 2018, is Rockstar’s most recent feat in the open-world sandbox genre. The winner of various accolades, it was also a groundbreaking release that completely raised the industry’s standards for immersion and attention to detail. Based on that, it’s no wonder that the studio’s fans are still comparing GTA 6 with the Wild West-inspired game that came out nearly 8 years ago.

According to the aforementioned source, Nelson gave insight into how GTA 6’s map stacks up against RDR 2’s—and it’s a surprisingly unexpected answer. According to him, Vice City and its surroundings combine to form a map thrice the size of RDR 2’s.

It’s worth noting that this statement would essentially establish RDR 2’s world to be fairly smaller than even GTA 5, which released 5 years prior. While this is indeed true, a section of fans may have found the former game to be bigger in experience. An explanation for that is the difference in traversal modes between RDR 2 and GTA 5, where, in the former’s case, traveling across the map on horseback makes its world feel much larger than it actually is.

Since, for GTA 6, Rockstar not only takes from the GTA series so far but has also borrowed some traits from its Red Dead franchise (as evident in the extended look), we are likely to get the sheer vastness of GTA 5 combined with the immersive density of RDR 2 in the forthcoming title.

Author’s take

Over the past decade or so, we have seen Rockstar’s penchant for making authentic open worlds further evolve and become even better than before. The record-breaking commercial success of GTA 5 and RDR 2 is a testament to its open-ended adventures faring extremely well among players.

From what I’ve noticed in the official videos and the leaks so far, there is impressive variety and vastness in terms of both interior and exterior locations. So, the current feeling around GTA 6’s map is nothing short of exciting. On top of that, the population density and numerous different NPC models enhance the realism of GTA 6’s world. These two features should elevate each other and offer what could be the closest a Rockstar project has ever come to producing a world that truly feels ‘alive’.

title.rendered: Roblox Arsenal codes (September 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Arsenal Codes on September 08, 2026

Arsenal turns every kill into a new weapon, so matches move fast even when you are still learning the maps. Its codes mostly unlock cosmetics, including skins, announcer voices, taunts, teleports, and calling cards. Claim them before spending BattleBucks in the shop. Copy the codes exactly, especially the ones that use all caps or unusual spacing.

All working Roblox Arsenal codes

  • 10YRS: Redeem for rhumbnail Beret skin
  • xonae: Redeem for a Xonae Announcer Voice
  • TRGTBOARD: Redeem for Hoverboard Taunt
  • FATE: teleports to a creepy map called ‘Fate’ with no other players.
  • ROLVE: unlocks Rabblerouser skin
  • POKE: Redeem for Poke Skin
  • Bandites: Redeem for Bandites Announcer Voice
  • GARCELLO: Redeem for Garcello Skin, Garcello Kill Effect, and an Emote
  • enforcer: Enforcer announcer

Expired or disputed Roblox Arsenal codes

scarybug, merrychristmas25, wake up, JOHN, F00LISH, E, POG, BLOXY, KITTEN, yoaprilfools25yeah, BATTLESHOP2026, RIVALRY2026, and NEWYEAR2026.

How to redeem Roblox Arsenal codes

  1. Open Arsenal on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the main menu to load.
  3. Click the gift-box or codes icon in the bottom-left corner.
  4. Paste a code into the text box.
  5. Click Redeem.

Why a Roblox Arsenal code may not work

3BILLY, ANNA, BLOXY, BRUTE, CBROX, CRACKED, DHMUBRUH, E, EPRIKA, F00LISH, FLAMINGO, GOODNIGHT, HAMMERTIME, HEROBRINE, JOHN, KITTEN, MERRYCHRISTMAS25, NEVERBROKEN, NEWMILO, PET, POG, SCARYBUG, SOON, THE 2021 SPOOKY CODE, THE BANANA MAN, TROLLFACE, TROLLING…, WAKE UP

Where to find more Roblox Arsenal codes

ROLVe tends to share codes around updates, events, milestones, and creator collaborations. Join the official Arsenal Discord and check the Arsenal Roblox page after a new update. The ROLVe Roblox community is another place to watch for announcements.

title.rendered: How to recover deleted photos from iPhone or iPad: 6 methods that actually work

content.rendered:
I know that moment of panic when you accidentally delete a photo and immediately wish you could undo it. Maybe it was a favorite family picture, a travel memory, or an important screenshot. But don’t panic just yet.

In many cases, deleted photos aren’t gone forever. Depending on when they were deleted and how your device is set up, you may be able to restore them. In this guide, I’ll walk you through the most effective ways to recover deleted photos from an iPhone or iPad, from the obvious fixes to the advanced options when the photos seem permanently removed.

Before you start: Understand what happens when you delete photos

The problem arises because most people mistakenly believe that deleting something means the file is gone forever. Usually, it doesn’t.

When you delete a photo or video from your iPhone or iPad, it usually moves to the Recently Deleted album. Apple keeps deleted items there for up to 30 days, giving you a window to recover them if you change your mind or delete something by mistake.

However, things can get more complicated if you also use iCloud Photos. When iCloud Photos is enabled, your photo library syncs across devices using the same Apple Account. That means changes, including deletions, can also sync across your iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

It’s also important not to confuse iCloud Photos with iCloud Backup. A backup stores a snapshot of your device data at a particular point in time. Understanding this difference will help you choose the right recovery method.

So before trying anything drastic, I always take a moment to check where those photos may still exist. Don’t rush into resetting your device or installing recovery software.

Method 1: Recover photos from the Recently Deleted album

This is the first place I look. If you deleted the photos recently, recovery can take less than a minute.

  1. Open the Photos app and move to the Collections tab.
  2. Scroll to the Utilities section and select Recently Deleted.
  3. Tap View Album.
  4. Authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode.
  5. Select the photos you want to restore.
  6. Tap the three-dot icon > Recover.
  7. Finally, select Recover Photo to confirm.

The best part is you can recover multiple photos and videos at once. It’s fast, free, and risk-free. You don’t need to restore a backup or install questionable software.

However, if the photo isn’t there, it may still exist. Move through the next methods before declaring the photo permanently lost.

Method 2: Check iCloud Photos immediately

If you have accidentally deleted the photos from your Recently Deleted album on your iPhone, one of the first places I’d check to recover them is iCloud Photos. In some situations, a copy of your photo may still be available in your iCloud library or on another device connected to your Apple Account. The key is to act promptly.

First, immediately disconnect the iPhone or iPad from the internet where the photos were deleted. This can prevent additional syncing while you check whether the photos still exist elsewhere.

Next, use a Mac or another device and follow these steps:

  1. Open a web browser and visit iCloud.com.
  2. Sign in with your Apple ID and password.
  3. Scroll and click the Photos tile.
  4. Check the Recently Deleted section in the sidebar.
  5. If you find your photos, select them and click Recover or download a copy immediately.

It’s important to be realistic here: if the photos were deleted more than 30 days ago, they may no longer appear in iCloud’s Recently Deleted folder.

Tip: Do you have an old iPhone, iPad, or Mac signed in to the same Apple Account that has not been connected to the internet recently? Check the Photos app on each one of them. If one device hasn’t fully synced, your missing photos may still be there.

Method 3: Recover permanently deleted photos after 30 days using an iCloud backup

If more than 30 days have passed and your photos have disappeared from the Recently Deleted album, recovering them becomes more challenging. But I didn’t give up and checked whether I had an older iCloud backup.

The backup is a snapshot of your iPhone or iPad from a specific point in time. If your missing photos existed when that backup was created, restoring it may restore them.

However, there’s one major catch: you can’t simply restore a few photos from an iCloud backup. Restoring a backup replaces the current data on your device with the data from that earlier backup. That’s why I strongly recommend checking the backup date before proceeding.

First, look for a backup created before your photos disappeared:

  1. Open Settings on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Tap your name at the top.
  3. Go to iCloud > iCloud Backup.
  4. Check whether you have an available backup and note its date.
  5. Make sure the backup was created before you permanently deleted the photos.

If you find a suitable backup, take a moment to save any important files, messages, or photos currently on your device. You may transfer photos and videos to a computer or services like Google Photos. Restoring an older backup could replace newer data.

Once you’ve confirmed that an older backup is worth restoring, follow these steps:

  1. Erase your iPhone or iPad to return it to the setup screen.
  2. Turn on your device and follow the on-screen setup instructions.
  3. When you reach the Apps & Data screen, choose Restore from iCloud Backup.
  4. Sign in with the Apple Account connected to your backup.
  5. Select the backup created before your photos were deleted.
  6. Keep your device connected to Wi-Fi while the backup restores.

After the restoration process is complete, launch the Photos app to confirm the missing photos have been restored successfully. The backup restore process takes time; be patient and allow time for the synchronization to complete.

Important: If you use iCloud Photos, your photos may sync separately from your standard iCloud device backup. In that situation, this method may not bring back photos that were already permanently deleted from iCloud Photos.

Method 4: Recover photos from Finder using a Mac backup

Don’t have an iCloud backup? That doesn’t necessarily mean your deleted photos are gone forever. If you’ve ever backed up your iPhone or iPad to a Mac, you may have a local copy of your device data stored on your computer. This proved useful when my missing photos weren’t available in iCloud or in the Recently Deleted album.

The most important thing is the backup date. Ideally, you need a backup created before the photos were deleted.

First, check whether your Mac has an older backup of your iPhone or iPad:

  1. Connect your iPhone or iPad to the Mac using a USB cable.
  2. Open Finder.
  3. Select your iPhone or iPad from the sidebar.
  4. Look for available backups and check their dates.
  5. Find a backup created before the photos were deleted.

If you find a suitable backup, you can restore it by following these steps. Before clicking Restore, I always save anything important.

  1. Keep your iPhone or iPad connected to your Mac.
  2. Open Finder and select your device.
  3. Click Restore Backup.
  4. Choose the backup created before your photos disappeared.
  5. Check the backup date and size to make sure you’ve selected the right one.
  6. If the backup is encrypted, enter the backup password when prompted.
  7. Click Restore and wait for the process to finish.
  8. Keep your device connected until it restarts and completes syncing.

After the restoration is complete, open the Photos app and check whether your deleted pictures have returned. I recommend choosing the most relevant backup based on its date and size and keeping the device connected until the restore and sync are complete.

Tip: If you use a Windows PC instead of a Mac, the process is similar. You can restore a computer backup using the Apple Devices app on Windows or iTunes on older setups.

Method 5: Look in Messages, Mail, and shared conversations

This is one of my favourite recovery tricks because it’s easy to forget how many copies of our photos we accidentally create.

Think about it. Have you ever sent the missing photo to a friend, family member, coworker, group chat, or yourself? If yes, there’s a chance the photo is still sitting inside that conversation.

Check Messages

Open relevant conversations and look through:

  • iMessage attachments
  • Shared photos
  • Old conversations
  • Group chats

You may be able to save a copy directly back to your Photos library.

Check messaging apps

Don’t stop at Apple’s Messages app.

I always look through apps such as:

  • WhatsApp
  • Telegram
  • Messenger
  • Signal
  • Other chat apps I regularly use

If the photo was shared but the conversation still exists, you may have an easy recovery option.

Check your email

Search your inbox and sent mail for:

  • Attachments
  • Photo names
  • Important dates
  • Names of people you shared the images with

The recovered version may not always be the original full-resolution file, but a slightly compressed copy is still better than losing a meaningful photo forever.

Method 6: Check third-party cloud storage services

If you’ve ever installed a cloud storage app, don’t underestimate it. Most people do not even remember setting up the automatic photo upload months or years ago.

Check services such as:

  • Google Photos
  • Microsoft OneDrive
  • Dropbox
  • Amazon Photos
  • Other cloud backup apps

The key places to inspect are your main photo library, Trash or Bin folders, archived items, and automatically uploaded camera folders. Browse by date, location, or people to quickly find photos and videos. If you recover it, download a copy immediately.

Once, I accidentally deleted my summer vacation album from my iPhone. Fortunately, they were automatically uploaded to OneDrive.

What to do if you permanently deleted the photos

Let’s address the scenario nobody wants to hear: You’ve checked Recently Deleted, iCloud Library, Shared Albums, Backups, Messages, old devices, and even social media. But the photo still isn’t there.

What now?

The honest answer is that the photos may no longer be recoverable. This is quite a bummer, but it’s also a good reminder to protect important memories with more than one backup going forward.

Also, avoid random actions such as:

  • Repeatedly resetting the device.
  • Installing multiple unknown recovery apps.
  • Giving suspicious software access to your Apple Account.
  • Paying for tools that promise guaranteed recovery.

Take a systematic approach instead.

Can iPhone photo recovery software help?

Here’s my blunt opinion: Be skeptical of anyone who promises to recover every permanently deleted iPhone photo.

Modern iPhones are heavily encrypted and tightly controlled. Recovering data isn’t as simple as plugging in a device and magically scanning every deleted file like old desktop hard-drive recovery.

Some third-party tools may help in specific situations, particularly when recoverable copies exist in backups, local storage, or other accessible data sources. But there is no universal magic button.

Before using iPhone photo recovery software, ask:

  • What exactly is the tool recovering?
  • Is it scanning the iPhone directly or searching backups?
  • Does it support your version of iOS or iPadOS?
  • Can you preview results before paying?
  • Does the company have a trustworthy reputation?
  • What data permissions are you giving the software?

While looking for such tools, I always avoid the ones that demand payment before showing whether anything is recoverable and make vague claims about bypassing Apple’s security.

Popular third-party tools to recover deleted iPhone photos are,

  • D-Back iPhone Data Recovery
  • PhoneRescue
  • EaseUS

Most of this software is paid. So, make sure you thoroughly check their website before buying a license.

Tips to prevent losing photos in the future

Recovering deleted photos is stressful. So, I always choose prevention.

Here are the habits I strongly recommend.

  • Don’t rely on a single backup: Keep important photos in multiple locations, such as your iPhone or iPad, a computer backup, and a second cloud storage service or an external drive. However, don’t duplicate every screenshot obsessively.
  • Back up before major cleanups: Planning to delete duplicate photos or screenshots? Back up first. It’s easy to tap too quickly, select the wrong images, or delete a photo you thought was a duplicate.
  • Review Recently Deleted often: Apple’s Recently Deleted album gives you a safety net, but it’s not permanent. Make it a habit to check it if you’ve recently performed a major photo cleanup.
  • Verify your photos are backed up: Check whether your recent photos are safely synced to iCloud Photos. Open Settings, tap your name > iCloud > Photos, and make sure Sync this iPhone/iPad is turned on.

My advice: If losing a photo would genuinely upset me, I want at least two independent copies of it.

Get back your important pictures!

Accidentally deleting photos from your iPhone or iPad can be stressful, but they aren’t always gone forever. Start with the simplest options, such as checking the Recently Deleted album and iCloud Photos, before moving on to backups, other devices, or cloud storage services.

If you’ve tried all the recovery methods and still can’t find your photos, recovery may not always be possible. My biggest takeaway? Don’t wait until you lose an important photo to think about backups. Keep your important photos stored in more than one place, so the next accidental deletion doesn’t have to turn into a panic.

title.rendered: How to get the Lilith skin and Borderlands bundle

content.rendered:
Lilith, one of the most important characters in the Borderlands franchise, has landed in Fortnite as a character skin for the very first time. Alongside the Lilith skin, a wide range of other Borderlands-inspired cosmetics have also hit the Shop, including the returning Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins.

This Fortnite x Borderlands crossover is a limited-time event, and the Borderlands items are only available for purchase until September 5, 2026, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. While the Lilith and Mad Moxxi outfits are selling for 1,500 V-Bucks, the Psycho Bandit outfit has a price tag of 2,000 V-Bucks.

For those who only want the Moxxi skin and her associated cosmetics, the Mad Moxxi Bundle is another option, worth 2,000 V-Bucks, that they can go for. Besides the skin, it specifically includes the character’s own themed back bling and pickaxe as well.

Steps to claim the Lilith skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. After that, scroll all the way to the “Borderlands” section and select your desired skin.
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to complete the transaction.

Certain skin purchases come bundled with another free cosmetic, and the Lilith skin is one of those. By purchasing this outfit, you also get the Siren Wings back bling, which is worth 400 V-Bucks, for free.

Other Borderlands cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Psycho Bandit

Price: 2,000 V-Bucks
Also includes: Psycho Buzz Axes, Claptrap

2. Mad Moxxi

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Also includes: Mad Moxxi (Shader Off) outfit

3. Siren Wings (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks
Also available with: Lilith skin

4. Claptrap (back bling)

Exclusively available with: Psycho Bandit skin

5. Psycho Buzz Axes (pickaxe)

Exclusively available with: Psycho Bandit skin

6. Moxxi’s Tip Jar (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Mad Moxxi Bundle

7. Underdome Megaphone (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Mad Moxxi Bundle

8. Moxxi’s Lip Service (emote)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Mad Moxxi Bundle

9. Torgue (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Mad Moxxi Bundle

10. Maliwan (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Mad Moxxi Bundle

11. Jakobs (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Mad Moxxi Bundle

Wrapping up

Based on the worldwide fanfare that Borderlands enjoys, it won’t be far-fetched to say that Fortnite skins based on iconic series characters, such as Lilith and Mad Moxxi, have its fans excited. These items provide a fun way for followers of the 2K-owned RPG franchise to express their fondness for the game in the highly social in-game world of Fortnite.

Throughout Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4, video game IPs are set to take center stage. So, it’s only natural that we have so far already seen franchises such as Crash Bandicoot, Tomb Raider, Sonic the Hedgehog, among others get featured in the Item Shop. In the coming weeks, there are several more IPs to make their presence felt, including a few confirmed ones such as Persona and Kingdom Hearts.

FAQs

Has Lilith appeared in Fortnite before?

No, this is the first time a Lilith-inspired outfit has made its way into the game. Contrarily, the Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins have previously appeared in the Shop.

Is there a Borderlands bundle that includes all three skins?

No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

Which other video game cosmetics are available in the Fortnite Shop right now?

At the time of writing, you can also purchase cosmetics related to the Crash Bandicoot and Spyro franchises.

More to explore:

  • Gwenpool skin returns to Fortnite: Here’s how you can get it
  • How to get the Mongraal skin in Fortnite

mainEntity.name: What does Mega Man Sprite do in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite enhances your mobility by reducing friction while sliding across the map.

mainEntity.name: Can you level up Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can level up the Mega Man Sprite by equipping it and earning XP through activities such as opening containers, getting eliminations, and collecting other Sprites.

mainEntity.name: What's the best way to get Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best way to obtain the Mega Man Sprite is through Blue Cheat Codes, which can be found across the map.

mainEntity.name: Has Lilith appeared in Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, this is the first time a Lilith-inspired outfit has made its way into the game. Contrarily, the Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins have previously appeared in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Borderlands bundle that includes all three skins?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which other video game cosmetics are available in the Fortnite Shop right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, you can also purchase cosmetics related to the Crash Bandicoot and Spyro franchises.

title.rendered: How to get Spyro the Dragon sidekick in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Spyro and Crash Bandicoot, two of the most nostalgic PlayStation franchises ever, have hit Fortnite amid a lot of anticipation. This major collab has resulted in a range of themed cosmetics, including Spyro as a sidekick and Crash as a character skin, debuting in the online game’s Shop section.

Both Spyro and Crash Bandicoot items in Fortnite are up for grabs only until September 11, 2026, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. Similarly, both Spyro the Dragon sidekick and the Crash Bandicoot skin are priced at 1,500 V-Bucks. You can alternatively bag both, alongside a bunch of other cosmetics, by purchasing the Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon Bundle for 3,000 V-Bucks.

Steps to claim Spyro the Dragon sidekick in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon section and select the desired item.
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your choice.

Once you have purchased the Spyro sidekick, you can complete its related quests to unlock additional styles. These styles offer more aesthetic variety for the beloved purple dragon, helping diversify your experience when you have this item equipped. The other variants tweak Spyro’s appearance by mainly turning his scales into green, orange, pink, and blue, depending on the selected style.

Other Crash Bandicoot & Spyro cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Crash Bandicoot

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Includes: Bandicoot (wrap)
Also available with: Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon Bundle

2. Aku Aku (back bling)

Price: 600 V-Bucks
Also available with: Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon Bundle

3. Crash’s Wumpa Mace (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon Bundle

4. Crash’s Victory (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon Bundle

5. Bandicoot (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon Bundle

Although you can buy all the aforementioned items individually, purchasing them via the Crash Bandicoot & Spyro the Dragon Bundle is more economical, as it offers a major 39% discount. In other words, you pay just 3,000 V-Bucks instead of a possible 4,900 V-Bucks for all items included in this promo.

Rounding up

With Spyro joining the list, Fortnite now boasts multiple different popular characters joining its list of sidekicks. Previous updates and Item Shop rotations have seen major names such as SpongeBob SquarePants, Tails from the Sonic the Hedgehog series, and Towelie from the South Park franchise get added into the mix.

As more Fortnite collabs roll out, it is inevitable that even more recognizable characters eventually get added as sidekicks in the game. Given the video game IP-focused theme of Fortnite Override, players can confidently expect the ongoing season to deliver more sidekicks from this entertainment medium in the coming weeks.

  • How to get Calm Capy sidekick in Fortnite
  • How to get the Sir Wyvern sidekick in Fortnite

title.rendered: Tim Cook sends final memo to Apple employees before CEO handoff

content.rendered:
Tim Cook has sent his final memo to Apple employees as CEO. The message appeared on August 31, one day before Apple’s planned leadership handoff. In a memo obtained by 9to5Mac, Cook thanked staff, reflected on his 15-year tenure, and backed John Ternus as the executive set to take over on September 1.

Cook thanked the team behind Apple

Cook’s note focused on the people who helped build Apple during his time at the top. He credited employees for the company’s success and called serving as CEO a “privilege of a lifetime.”

He also made clear that the move is not a departure from Apple. Cook said he is stepping away from the role, not leaving the company, and praised Ternus as “brilliant and wonderful and capable.”

In a separate post on X, Cook thanked the Apple community and wrote, “My title changes tomorrow.” He added that his affection for Apple customers would not change.

Ternus is set to take over on September 1

Apple has been preparing for the handoff since April, when it announced that John Ternus would replace Cook as CEO. Apple’s official newsroom announcement set the transition for September 1 and said Cook would become executive chairman of the board.

Apple’s Form 8-K filing records the same effective date and adds that Ternus will join the board. Arthur Levinson, Apple’s then non-executive chairman, will become lead independent director. Ternus joined Apple in 2001 and became senior vice president of Hardware Engineering in 2021, according to the filing.

Cook will stay involved

Cook’s new role keeps him close to Apple. The company says he will help with certain aspects of the business, including engaging with policymakers around the world. Ternus will take the CEO role and day-to-day leadership.

excerpt.rendered: Tim Cook’s final memo thanks Apple employees and backs John Ternus as his successor. The planned September 1 handoff moves Cook to executive chairman, not out of Apple.

mainEntity.name: What does Mega Man Sprite do in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite enhances your mobility by reducing friction while sliding across the map.

mainEntity.name: Can you level up Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can level up the Mega Man Sprite by equipping it and earning XP through activities such as opening containers, getting eliminations, and collecting other Sprites.

mainEntity.name: What's the best way to get Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best way to obtain the Mega Man Sprite is through Blue Cheat Codes, which can be found across the map.

mainEntity.name: Has Lilith appeared in Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, this is the first time a Lilith-inspired outfit has made its way into the game. Contrarily, the Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins have previously appeared in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Borderlands bundle that includes all three skins?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which other video game cosmetics are available in the Fortnite Shop right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, you can also purchase cosmetics related to the Crash Bandicoot and Spyro franchises.

title.rendered: Apple releases iOS 27 beta 8 ahead of the fall launch

content.rendered:
Apple has released iOS 27.0 developer beta 8, the latest test build for iPhone. Apple’s developer release page lists build 24A5430a, released on August 31.

The new seed arrived one week after iOS 27 beta 7, continuing Apple’s weekly beta cadence near the end of testing. 9to5Mac later updated its report on the release to say the corresponding public beta is available too and will likely be public beta 6.

Beta 8 has no confirmed headline change

As of September 1, Apple’s public release listing confirms the build and release date, but does not include a beta-8-specific list of fixes or new features.

For now, it is safer to treat beta 8 as a late-stage testing update rather than a new feature drop. Apple has not tied Siri AI, the Liquid Glass transparency slider, or any other iOS 27 addition specifically to this build.

The bigger iOS 27 changes are still coming

The wider iOS 27 update is still centered on Siri AI. In its WWDC26 announcement, Apple described a rebuilt assistant with personal context, onscreen awareness, web knowledge, and actions across apps. It also announced a dedicated Siri app, wider Apple Intelligence features, and more control over the Liquid Glass design.

The iOS 27 features guide breaks down the larger update. Those features belong to iOS 27 as a whole, not necessarily to beta 8.

Who can install iOS 27 beta 8?

Developers with beta access can open Settings, go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates, and select iOS 27 Developer Beta. Public testers can enroll through Apple’s Beta Software Program and choose iOS 27 Public Beta. For step-by-step instructions, see our guide to installing the iOS 27 public beta.

Beta 8 is still pre-release software. Back up your iPhone first, and avoid installing it on the device you rely on most if bugs or app compatibility problems would cause trouble. Apple has only promised the final iOS 27 update for this fall, so this release suggests that testing is moving into its final stretch, not that the final build is locked.

mainEntity.name: What does Mega Man Sprite do in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite enhances your mobility by reducing friction while sliding across the map.

mainEntity.name: Can you level up Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can level up the Mega Man Sprite by equipping it and earning XP through activities such as opening containers, getting eliminations, and collecting other Sprites.

mainEntity.name: What's the best way to get Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best way to obtain the Mega Man Sprite is through Blue Cheat Codes, which can be found across the map.

mainEntity.name: Has Lilith appeared in Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, this is the first time a Lilith-inspired outfit has made its way into the game. Contrarily, the Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins have previously appeared in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Borderlands bundle that includes all three skins?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which other video game cosmetics are available in the Fortnite Shop right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, you can also purchase cosmetics related to the Crash Bandicoot and Spyro franchises.
