title.rendered: How to get Calm Capy sidekick in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Fortnite sidekicks have been growing in number and also in terms of variety over time. The recently added Hype Circuit promotion further introduced a capybara-inspired sidekick called Calm Capy.

This particular sidekick is a customizable Fortnite item and is priced at 1,200 V-Bucks. Calm Capy, as well as the other cosmetics in its promo, are currently up for grabs in Fortnite until August 25 at 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. You can check out the guide below to learn how to claim this item for yourself.

Steps to claim Calm Capy sidekick in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Then, scroll down all the way to the Hype Circuit section and select the Calm Capy sidekick.
  3. At last, press and hold the Purchase button to complete your transaction.

More sidekicks and other cosmetics in the Hype Circuit section

Apart from adding Calm Capy into the mix, the Hype Circuit section also brought back two previously introduced sidekicks, namely Remus and Kit. Both of them were originally rolled out for the first time in Fortnite in January 2026. On top of these sidekicks, the Hype Circuit promo features a range of skins and other cosmetics.

1. Remus

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks

2. Kit

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks

3. Cozy Capys (kicks)

Price: 600 V-Bucks

4. Fishstick

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Saltwater Satchel (back bling)

5. Jellie

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Shelly (back bling)

6. Wolfie

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Wolf Tour Essentials (back bling)

7. Bad Kit

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: GHOST (outfit style)

Sidekicks in Fortnite: The status quo and the promising future

Although sidekicks do not serve a purpose beyond your own immersion, their consistent presence in the Item Shop suggests players may still be going for them for their own personal preference. The wide catalog that Fortnite devs have created thus far is also a testament to their dedication toward diversifying this aspect of the game.

As a consequence, today Fortnite not only boasts an impressive range of original sidekicks but also flaunts the ones derived from some of the most popular franchises in pop culture. From DC’s Krypto to SpongeBob SquarePants, the IP depth in the sidekicks category is not to be taken for granted. However, since this Fortnite feature itself is less than a year old, the room for introducing many more recognizable characters as sidekicks is quite large.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • How to earn Sidekick Points in Fortnite
  • How to get the Sir Wyvern sidekick in Fortnite

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

title.rendered: Fortnite Override: Full list of admin panel codes and how to use them

content.rendered:
If you were paying attention to the numerous teases in the build-up to Fortnite Override’s arrival, you would know that hacking and cryptic codes were as much of a motif in them as video games were. And now, we know why.

The various codes dropped throughout that period were actually admin panel codes or lobby hacks that can be entered in Fortnite to unlock useful items and resources, including unique Chapter 7 Season 4 sprites and lots of Sprite Dust.

Given below is an exhaustive list of admin panel codes in Fortnite and their corresponding rewards. These codes are not case-sensitive and are all working as of the time of writing.

List of Fortnite Override admin panel codes (Updated: September 17)

*Only works if you have completed Geno’s Story quests

How to use admin panel codes in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4

  1. In the Fortnite home screen, press and hold X (on Xbox)/Square (on PS5) or click on the “admin panel” button near the top-right corner
  2. Now, type in your desired code and press X (on Xbox)/Square (on PS5) or click on “Submit“.
  3. Finally, press A (on Xbox)/Cross (on PS5) or click on Claim to add the reward to your inventory.

Wrapping up

Thanks to these admin panel codes, Fortnite players have an easy way to get a head start in the new season. These codes not only provide free sprites but also valuable Sprite Dust that should prove crucial for those who often purchase items at Extraction Sites or recall lost sprites.

Over time, you can expect Fortnite devs to introduce more of such lobby hacks. Whenever that happens, we will update the list above with the new codes. So, make sure to either keep tabs on this article or on Epic Games’ official channels to get hold of Fortnite admin panel codes as soon as they are pushed into the game.

  • How to acquire power-ups in Fortnite Override

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

mainEntity.name: 2. Which other Xbox franchises have appeared in Fortnite besides Halo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: 3. Which other FPS protagonists, other than Master Chief, have been added to Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Other FPS heroes in Fortnite's skins catalog include popular characters such as Doom Slayer from Doom, V from Cyberpunk 2077, and Tracer, Genji, & D.Va from Overwatch.

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

title.rendered: Fortnite Override Battle Pass: All skins, emotes and rewards

content.rendered:
Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 Override finally made its way into the highly popular battle royale game on August 20, and with it came a brand-new Battle Pass containing a fresh lineup of cosmetics. What’s special about this season and its related content is the sheer amount of video game IP collabs, which have roped in AAA franchises such as Street Fighter and indie titles such as Peak.

Keeping in line with the season’s video game-heavy theme, the Battle Pass this time is headlined by Sonic the Hedgehog. In addition, it also features a plethora of gaming-related cosmetics, ranging from a back bling modeled around a handheld game console to a Minecraft-like boxy character skin.

Fortnite Override Battle Pass price

The Battle Pass for Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 can be purchased for 800 V-Bucks and is available till October 31, 2026. Given that actively playing throughout the season and amassing XP can generate up to 800 V-Bucks by itself, you can very well make back the in-game currency you spend on it. Moreover, you can also buy the pass alongside progress worth 25 levels in exchange for 2,600 V-Bucks.

Alternatively, the Fortnite Override Battle Pass can be unlocked for free if you have the Fortnite Crew membership, which also packs certain other benefits, worth $11.99 per month. If you have an existing Game Pass Ultimate subscription, priced at $22.99 per month, it also grants you Fortnite Crew at no extra cost.

Fortnite Override Battle Pass skins and set rewards

1. Sonic The Hedgehog

Unlocked at: Level 5

2. Wrixel

Unlocked at: Level 10

3. Phantom

Unlocked at: Level 10

4. Mali

Unlocked at: Level 35

5. Bastian

Unlocked at: Level 35

6. K1tty W1ns

Unlocked at: Level 60

7. Grace Crowne

Unlocked at: Level 60

8. Geno

Unlocked at: Level 85

Bonus rewards

Unlocked by: Unlocking the Geno Set

Rounding up

For many Fortnite players and enthusiasts of gaming culture, the current Battle Pass should be an intriguing investment. At the same time, they may want to check out the launch week Item Shop additions, which feature Shadow The Hedgehog, Knuckles, Lara Croft, and Eggman.

Besides the various themed skins and in-game accessories, Fortnite Override has notably also rolled out gaming-inspired sprites. Among those included in the first batch are Sonic Sprite, Tails Sprite, Shadow Sprite, and 8-Bit Sprite. As this season goes beyond its early days, it will be interesting to see if the new lineup of sprites can deliver the praiseworthy engagement levels that the Fortnite Runners season sprites did.

  • 10 rarest Fortnite pickaxes and how players got them
  • Confirmed game characters in Fortnite Override
  • How to get Calm Capy sidekick in Fortnite

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

mainEntity.name: 2. Which other Xbox franchises have appeared in Fortnite besides Halo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

title.rendered: I tested the best Google Pixel 11 cases: Here’s what I’d buy for the 11, 11 Pro & 11 Pro XL

content.rendered:
Google has officially launched its next-generation flagship phones: the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL. The new lineup keeps Google’s familiar Pixel design but gives it a more refined glass finish, a slimmer camera bar, brighter displays on the Pro models, and improved durability.

But durable doesn’t mean drop-proof. So, my first priority is to buy a good case to protect the glass back, display edges, and camera bar from drops, scratches, and bumps of everyday use. After trying many, I’ve narrowed down the best Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL cases for different types of users. Here are the top eight options you can buy today.

What I looked for when testing Pixel 11 cases

I don’t judge a phone case by its appearance alone. A case can look fantastic and still be miserable to live with.

Here are the things I cared about most when evaluating these Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL cases.

1. Protection without unnecessary bulk

First comes protection.

I looked for raised edges around the display and camera, reinforced corners, shock-absorbing materials, and a design that can handle the sort of accidental drops that actually happen in real life.

But there’s a catch: more protection isn’t automatically better. If a case adds extra weight to the sleek Pixel phone, I’m going to pass unless there’s something special about it.

2. Grip and everyday handling

A case must help you handle your phone better.

I paid attention to how secure the edges feel in the hand, whether the back attracts fingerprints, and whether the case feels comfortable during one-handed use.

This matters especially on the larger Pixel 11 Pro XL, where a little extra grip can make a surprisingly big difference.

3. Camera and screen protection

The new all-glass camera bar is one of the first things I’d want protected on any Pixel 11.

I looked for raised camera lips and screen bezels that provide some separation between the phone and a table or other hard surface.

4. Wireless charging and magnetic accessories

This is increasingly important with the Pixel 11 generation.

Google’s Pixelsnap ecosystem brings magnetic wireless charging and accessories to the Pixel lineup, while compatible third-party cases can also support magnetic accessories.

So I considered whether each case works well with magnetic charging and accessories rather than treating wireless charging as a nice-to-have.

5. Fit and button feel

A case can have all the protection in the world, but if it doesn’t fit properly, I don’t want it on my Pixel. This is especially important when choosing between the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL. The two phones look almost identical, but they differ in size: the Pro measures 6.0 × 2.8 inches, while the Pro XL measures 6.4 × 3.0 inches.

That means Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL cases are generally not interchangeable. So, before ordering any Pixel 11 Pro case, double-check the exact model. A proper fit will provide you with responsive buttons, a correct cutout for the camera bar, and easy access to the USB-C port.

6. Thickness and weight

This is where cases become personal.

Since I appreciate the nice form factor of the Pixel 11, bulky and heavy cases are not my preference, even though they provide better drop protection.

Conversely, if you’ve shattered two phones in the last year, saving a few millimeters of thickness isn’t necessarily the smartest trade-off.

That’s why this list includes both ultra-slim cases and genuinely protective options.

Top 8 cases I’d recommend for Pixel 11, 11 Pro, and 11 Pro XL

Here I have listed 8 types of cases for the Pixel 11 series, tailored to different user needs.

1. Google Pixelsnap Silicone Case: Best overall

If you want the safest all-around choice, I’d start with Google’s own Pixelsnap Case.

There is something reassuring about using a first-party case. The fit is designed around the Pixel 11 itself, the case matches the actual phone colors, and Pixelsnap compatibility makes it particularly appealing if you plan to use Google’s magnetic accessories. That’s the biggest reason I’d choose it over a random inexpensive case.

The minimal appearance with Google branding looks premium. In addition, Google claims that the phone case has been rigorously drop-tested for maximum protection. I like its soft silicone feel in the hand.

Pros

  • First-party Pixel fit
  • Clean, understated design
  • Built-in Pixelsnap magnetic compatibility
  • Raised edges help protect the display and camera bar

Cons

  • More expensive than many third-party cases
  • Silicone-style finish can attract dust and lint
  • Protection is good for everyday use, but not aimed at extreme drops

My verdict: If you don’t want to overthink your purchase, this is the Pixel 11 case I’d buy first.

Check out on Amazon

2. Spigen Ultra Hybrid MagFit: Best clear case for Pixel 11 series

I am a fan of good transparent cases because they let the phone’s design do the talking. The Spigen Ultra Hybrid MagFit is the option I’d choose if you want everyday protection without hiding your Pixel’s sleek design.

Its hybrid construction combines a flexible TPU bumper with a rigid polycarbonate back and Air Cushion in the corners, while the built-in N52 magnetic system makes it more useful with compatible MagSafe accessories. I also love Spigen’s clear case because of its DuraClear anti-yellowing resin coating.

Pros

  • Excellent balance between protection and bulk
  • MagFit magnets work with Pixelsnap-compatible accessories
  • Strong value for a clear case

Cons

  • Clear materials can eventually show scratches or discoloration
  • Slightly bulkier than an ultra-slim case
  • Doesn’t offer the rugged protection of a heavy-duty case

My verdict: My favorite all-rounder. It gives you the protection you need without hiding the Pixel or making it unnecessarily bulky.

Check out on Amazon

3. PITAKA Ultra Slim Pixel 11 Case: Get the caseless feeling

If your philosophy is “I bought a thin phone, so why would I put a giant case on it?”, PITAKA is the obvious candidate. This Ultra Slim case provides a near-caseless feel while still getting some protection. It weighs only 0.72oz and has a thickness of 0.05 in.

Thanks to the finely woven aramid fiber, it gives a grippy hand feel and resists scratches, fingerprints, and stains. I give this case a plus for its NFC Aaron button that quickly opens your favorite app. Although it’s so slim, PITAKA integrated a magnetic ring to support MagSafe accessories and Qi2 charging.

Pros

  • Extremely thin and lightweight to maintain much of the Pixel’s original feel
  • The metal-accented camera protection edge looks premium
  • Excellent for minimalist users
  • Easy to slip into a pocket

Cons

  • Expensive for such a minimalist case
  • Less impact protection than rugged cases
  • Not the right choice for frequent phone droppers

My verdict: This is the case I’d choose for someone who prioritizes thinness, low weight, and premium materials over maximum drop protection.

Check out on Amazon

4. Ringke Onyx Magnetic Case: Rugged protection on a budget

Ringke is the choice I’d make when I want something practical rather than flashy. The Onyx case offers military-grade drop protection, although it’s only 2mm thick. It uses lightweight, flexible TPU that feels comfortable in the hand, while the textured sides add extra grip and help prevent accidental slips.

The matte, fingerprint-resistant surface texture is another nice touch, as I don’t like seeing smudges all over my case. Ringke also adds built-in dual lanyard holes, allowing you to attach a wrist strap or phone charm for extra security. The biggest advantage, though, is support for NFC and wireless charging.

Pros

  • Good everyday protection
  • Anti-fingerprint finish keeps it looking cleaner
  • Corner air pockets protect from accidental drops
  • Slim profile without feeling flimsy

Cons

  • Not as rugged as a heavy-duty protective case
  • Textured finish may feel less premium than smooth cases
  • Lanyard is not included

My verdict: If you want a slim Pixel 11 case with excellent grip, magnetic compatibility, and practical everyday protection, the Ringke Onyx is one of the best options.

Check out on Amazon

5. TORRAS Q3 Spin Case: Best Pixel 11 case with a magnetic stand

A kickstand sounds gimmicky until you actually use one. The TORRAS Q3 Spin is much more interesting than a basic stand case. Its 360° rotating stand with an 8-layered aluminum hinge lets me adjust the viewing angle for videos, calls, recipes, presentations, or hands-free photos.

Protection hasn’t been forgotten either. The case has a four-layer shock-absorbing bumper and is certified for 16ft drop protection, while still maintaining a slim 0.04-inch profile. I also like its Nappa-textured side rails that add grip, while a nano-coating helps resist fingerprints and oil. The magnetic functionality also makes it more versatile than a basic kickstand case.

I’d particularly recommend it for the Pixel 11 Pro XL, where the larger screen makes hands-free viewing much more useful.

Pros

  • 30,000+ hinge-fold rating
  • Strong N52 magnetic system for Qi2 and Pixelsnap compatibility
  • More practical than a basic protective case
  • Good fit for larger Pixel models

Cons

  • More expensive than basic cases
  • Kickstand adds some weight
  • Not ideal if you want a completely minimalist look

My verdict: If you actually use your phone for media, calls, recipes, or travel navigation, the kickstand earns its keep.

Check out on Amazon: Pixel 11/11 Pro | Pixel 11 Pro XL

6. FNTCASE Pixel 11 Case with Screen Protector: Best value for money

Not everyone wants to spend $40–$50 on a phone case. And honestly, they shouldn’t have to. FNTCASE offers a protective case bundled with a tempered glass screen protector for Pixel 11, 11 Pro, and 11 Pro XL at a great price. It uses 38 N52 magnets, giving it a much stronger hold for magnetic chargers, power banks, car mounts, and wireless charging stands.

Protection is another major strength. The case combines a rigid PC back with flexible TPU bumpers and four corner airbags, offering up to 14ft drop protection. I also like the translucent matte finish. It lets the Pixel logo remain visible while the frosted texture provides a non-slip grip. A nano antioxidant layer helps resist oil stains, fingerprints, sweat, and minor scratches.

Pros

  • Affordable with good features
  • 3-layer construction for military-grade drop protection
  • Multiple color options
  • Uses 50%+ recycled materials

Cons

  • Bulkier than slim cases
  • Materials and finish aren’t as premium as Google’s or PITAKA’s

My verdict: The feature-packed budget pick I’d actually consider for everyone.

Check out on Amazon

7. Oterkin Pixel 11 Wallet Case with Kickstand: Great for daily convenience

Wallet cases are divisive. Some people love carrying one item instead of two. Others can’t stand the added thickness. I’m firmly in the first camp when traveling.

The Oterkin Wallet Case combines drop protection, RFID-blocking card storage, and a kickstand, making it a practical choice for people who want to leave their traditional wallet at home. You can carry four to five cards plus cash in it. I like its textured finish on the wallet section, which improves grip and makes it more comfortable to hold

The biggest catch? The wallet section indicates wireless charging isn’t supported, so you’ll need to remove the case to use it. Also, it’s not the sleekest option here, but that isn’t really the point. You’re buying it for carrying cards.

Pros

  • Convenient for travel
  • Built-in portrait and landscape kickstand
  • Claimed 15-foot drop protection
  • Raised edges and corner airbags

Cons

  • No wireless charging with cards stored
  • Bulkier than a standard case
  • Less suitable for minimalist users

My verdict: A practical Pixel 11 wallet case for anyone who values convenience and protection over a slim profile.

Check out on Amazon

8. SPIDERCASE Waterproof Case: Best Pixel 11 case for outdoor protection

This is the one I’d buy when ordinary protection isn’t enough. If you take your Pixel 11 hiking, camping, to the beach, or simply want maximum protection from everyday accidents, the SPIDERCASE is built for that job. It offers 360-degree waterproof protection with an IP68 rating.

The manufacturer claims it has been tested for one hour in up to 6.6 feet (2 meters) of water, using silicone seals and a locking design to keep water out. It can withstand drops from up to 12 feet as well. Additionally, you get built-in screen and camera protectors that resist scratches, dust, water, and fingerprints.

I also like the attention to everyday usability. Precisely cut openings keep the charging port, speakers, and cameras accessible, while independently covered buttons give responsive feedback.

Pros

  • Extra defense against everyday environmental hazards
  • Built-in screen and camera protectors for 360-degree coverage
  • Better suited to outdoor use
  • Precise ports and responsive buttons

Cons

  • Bulkier than regular cases
  • Only black color option
  • Fingerprint-protector installation requires extra care

My verdict: A serious waterproof Pixel 11 case for anyone who wants armor-like protection rather than a slim everyday cover.

Check out on Amazon

Why choosing the right Pixel 11 case matters

Putting on a Pixel 11 case isn’t just about making your phone look better. It’s about protecting a phone that can cost well over $1,000 from the kind of accidents that happen in seconds-a drop on concrete, a slip off the car dashboard, or a scratch from keys in your pocket.

The tricky part is that the best Pixel 11 case isn’t the same for everyone.

  • If you want to keep the phone’s slim feel, a case like PITAKA makes more sense than a bulky rugged cover.
  • If you spend a lot of time outdoors, SPIDERCASE’s waterproof protection is far more valuable.
  • And if you use magnetic chargers, wallets, or car mounts, Pixelsnap and MagSafe compatibility should be high on your checklist.

Fit matters just as much. The Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL are different sizes, so you need a case made specifically for your model. Then there’s grip. A case with a textured or anti-slip finish can make the phone much easier to hold, potentially preventing the drop you’re trying to protect against in the first place.

Ultimately, don’t buy a Pixel 11 case simply because it has the most features. Choose the protection level, size, grip, thickness, and features that match how you actually use your phone. That’s what turns a good case into the right case.

Protect your flagship in style!

After narrowing down these best Pixel 11 cases, my overall winner is the Google Pixelsnap Case. It’s the least complicated recommendation with excellent compatibility, a purpose-built fit, clean styling, and a design that makes sense for Google’s latest Pixel generation.

Nevertheless, my second choice will be Spigen Ultra Hybrid MagFit. Why? Because it hits the sweet spot. You get to see the Pixel, you get useful protection, and you don’t have to pay a premium simply for the Google logo.

There’s no universal winner because every Pixel owner has a different definition of “best.” But there is a case here for almost every kind of Pixel 11 owner. Which one did you choose? Let me know in the comments below!

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

title.rendered: WhatsApp is testing Liquid Glass updates for its drawing editor and video player on iPhone

content.rendered:
WhatsApp’s Liquid Glass redesign still is not finished. WABetaInfo found work on two more iPhone screens: the drawing editor and the video player. The changes appeared in WhatsApp beta version 26.33.10.18, but they are still in development and not available to beta testers yet.

What is changing

The drawing editor is the screen you see when you mark up a photo or video before sending it. Its top row of buttons for adding text, drawing, and stickers still uses the old flat style. WhatsApp is working on giving those controls the same frosted-glass look as the rest of the app.

WhatsApp is also testing the design on the video player’s progress bar at the top of the screen. Neither change alters how these screens work; they are visual updates.

The redesign is still rolling out

WhatsApp started rolling out Liquid Glass more broadly in May after months of limited testing. Since then, the chat list, Updates tab, sidebar, reactions, context menus, voice message player, and chat interface have all moved to the new look. The iPad app followed in June, and Meta has been readying Liquid Glass for the Mac app since before its July rollout.

The rollout has been slow enough that some iPhone users still do not have the redesign. These two screens are also not finished, so the visual transition is not complete yet.

There is no release timeline yet

WABetaInfo connects the work to iOS 27’s expected launch, but WhatsApp and Meta have not announced a deadline. Apple is not planning a major Liquid Glass redesign in iOS 27, but that does not confirm when WhatsApp will finish these screens.

There is no timeline yet for when the drawing editor and video player changes reach beta testers or the public app.

excerpt.rendered: WABetaInfo spotted Liquid Glass work for WhatsApp’s drawing editor and video player on iOS. The changes are in development and would complete the app’s redesign before iOS 27.

title.rendered: 5 best Backrooms games on Roblox for horror fans

content.rendered:
If solving puzzles to escape an eerie, endless-looking maze is your idea of fun, then Backrooms games should thoroughly entertain you. Luckily, a good variety of such titles is also available to play on Roblox, one of the biggest game platforms in the world.

Several of these Backrooms games attract thousands of Roblox players every day and deliver the very experience that defines the appeal of the genre. Below, you can learn more about the Backrooms genre and also find a curated list of popular Backrooms games within Roblox that have a high approval rating as well as considerable player engagement at any time of day.

The Backrooms, explained

The Backrooms is a fictional liminal space characterized by empty rooms and a creepy overall atmosphere. It originated from an image shared on 4chan, a long-running internet forum. These Backrooms are often depicted as a series of rooms and hallways, painted in a pale shade of yellow and lit by fluorescent lights.

Over time, this enticing premise has been experimented with numerous times by those in the creative field. Such instances have notably resulted in projects that implement The Backrooms concept in a way that leverages psychological horror to entertain the audience. In particular, Kane Parsons’ Backrooms web series is credited with contributing significantly to the genre and boosting its popularity.

Top Backrooms games on Roblox

1. Apeirophobia

This haunting Backrooms-type adventure puts you in a maze of rooms where danger lurks at every corner. So, your objective revolves around exploring the place, solving puzzles, and evading enemies in a bid to escape the ominous. Apeirophobia capitalizes on the horror factor of this genre with its bleak-looking locations and the creepy foes at its disposal.

The game currently boasts over 585,000 likes against a dislike count of 51,000. In other words, more than 90% of its user ratings are positive.

Play Now

2. Build Your Backrooms

Perhaps one big reason for Build Your Backrooms’ popularity is how it turns the tables on the Backrooms genre. Instead of putting you in the liminal space of a backroom, it lets you create Backrooms of your own, place monsters in them, and test them by putting other players in the map as if they were lab hamsters. Alternatively, you can also join Backrooms created by someone else.

What’s truly impressive is that it has an approval rating of over 98%, the highest among the Roblox games on this list. This is thanks to the huge number of upvotes it has received over time, which now sits beyond 406,000.

Play Now

3. M.E.G. Endless Reality

This particular backroom experience puts you in the shoes of an employee under Major Explorer Group, an organization popular among backrooms enthusiasts that is tasked with entering the maze-like void and performing assigned tasks. Naturally, in this game, your goal is to carry out various missions in the backrooms, ranging from rescuing lost individuals to sealing off aberrant no-clip zones.

With over 90% positive ratings, M.E.G. Endless Reality is a very highly rated backrooms experience on Roblox. Its more than 166,000 likes, despite the game still being in alpha, certainly speak volumes about its quality.

Play Now

4. Unseen Liminality

Unseen Liminality takes inspiration from another Roblox backrooms game, Beyond Liminal, but has apparently amassed a bigger following than the original. Its gameplay consists of exploration and evasion from threats, all driven by the player’s curiosity to discover secrets hidden in the backrooms.

Even though Unseen Liminality is still in beta, it has a strongly positive reception on Roblox. At the time of writing, it sits at over 120,000 likes compared to less than 8,800 dislikes—meaning every 9 out of 10 users found it worthwhile.

Play Now

5. Backrooms Company

If having a uniquely challenging run in each session is of importance to you, Backrooms Company is the fix. It throws you into a backrooms-esque spooky map, which differs for each turn, and requires you to obtain evidence while you are there. Then, all that remains is for you to make it back to the headquarters before anything goes awry.

Notably, this early alpha release also has a fairly positive rating, with over 17,000 likes. Overall, the approval rating for this game stands at over 80%.

Play Now

Final word

The Backrooms, in recent years, has undoubtedly cultivated a niche but dedicated fanbase. Courtesy of Roblox, a wide range of backroom games are playable for free and without needing any high-end system specifications.

Since quite a few of the backroom games on Roblox mentioned above are still in alpha or beta stages, there is a good room for improvement for these titles in the future. Given that they already have a good level of traction, carefully listening to player feedback and promptly delivering updates should be enough to ensure these games evolve into their best possible versions by the time of their respective full release.

  • Best scary Roblox games to play right now

title.rendered: ChatGPT can now read and send your Apple Messages on Mac, but permissions are the catch

content.rendered:
OpenAI’s August 20 release notes confirm that the ChatGPT desktop app for Mac can now use an Apple Messages plugin on Apple Silicon Macs. In ChatGPT Work and Codex, it can search iMessage, SMS, and RCS chats, draft replies, and send messages through Apple’s Messages app.

The feature is limited to the macOS desktop app’s Work and Codex modes, and it requires permission to access Messages on the Mac.

What the plugin can do

Once installed from Plugins, open a new chat in ChatGPT Work or Codex and ask it to find, summarize, or draft a message from conversations already on your Mac.

OpenAI suggests trying prompts like:

  • Check my calendar and reply to [name] with a few times I’m free for dinner next week
  • Suggest follow-ups from yesterday in messages
  • Find birthdays in @messages and add them to my calendar
  • Find potential spam messages I can delete

It can search message history, pull details from old threads, and prepare a reply. It can also send the message through the desktop app after you approve it. You can’t text ChatGPT remotely through Messages, and the plugin doesn’t work in regular ChatGPT chats, on the web, or on mobile.

The permission trade-off is real

OpenAI says you must grant the requested macOS permissions before the plugin can read Messages. The Apple silicon requirement is also explicit; the release is limited to the arm64 build of the ChatGPT desktop app, so Intel Macs are not supported.

By default, ChatGPT asks you to approve the message and its recipients before anything is sent. You can choose “Always allow sending to this chat” to skip future confirmations for that thread, but OpenAI warns that this removes your final review. Its plugin guide also documents a known issue where full-access tasks may not show the send confirmation.

Workspace admins can disable the plugin through the existing Computer Use control.

How to try it

Install Apple Messages from Plugins in the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, then start a new Work or Codex conversation. The plugin is available on all ChatGPT plans, including Free, but only on the Apple Silicon build of the app. You also need Messages set up on your Mac.

If you regularly triage messages on your Mac, the plugin can save you from copying and pasting. If you are not comfortable giving ChatGPT access to your message history, skip it and keep per-send approval enabled.

title.rendered: Apple Music will show ‘Made With AI’ labels on songs later this year

content.rendered:
Apple Music will make AI-generated music easier to spot. In an email to creators on August 20, Apple said the AI Transparency Tags it introduced in March will become visible to listeners as “Made With AI” labels later this year. 9to5Mac obtained the email.

When a track gets the label

Content providers will be required to tag any release where AI was used to create “a material portion of the content,” including tracks that are AI-platform generated. Apple defines those as anything “primarily derived from a generative AI service.”

The tags cover four parts of a release: the sound recording, the composition and lyrics, the artwork, and the music video. Apple says the goal is to give listeners “as much transparency as possible,” and points creators to its Music Style Guide for details.

There is no exact launch date yet, and Apple has not said what happens if a provider skips the tag.

The tags were optional until now

When Apple announced Transparency Tags in March, disclosure was voluntary. Labels and distributors decided what qualified as AI-generated, similar to genres and credits. The new email makes tagging a requirement wherever AI played a material role in the content.

Over a third of new uploads are fully AI-made

The numbers explain the timing. Apple Music’s Oliver Schusser said on Billboard’s On the Record podcast that more than a third of the music uploaded to the service each month is fully AI-generated. Those tracks account for less than 0.5% of actual listening.

Streaming rivals are handling the flood differently. Spotify keeps music from AI Personas out of editorial and algorithmic recommendations by default, and its Verified badge flags authentic artists instead. Deezer excludes fully AI-generated tracks from recommendations and editorial playlists, and says fully AI music crossed 50% of its daily uploads for the first time in July.

Visible AI labels are spreading beyond music, too. WhatsApp is testing an AI-content label for Channel updates.

Apple’s labels arrive later this year. Listeners will then be able to spot the disclosure at a glance instead of relying on credits or outside tools.

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

title.rendered: Driving Empire codes (September 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Driving Empire Codes on September 19, 2026

Driving Empire is one of those Roblox games where the car you want always costs more cash than you have. Grinding races and deliveries for your next ride takes hours, and the new Audi body kits only make the wishlist longer. Codes are the shortcut: free cash, tuning kits, and sometimes a full car for typing a word into a box. Right now, that includes the limited Rocket Car and a Nissan GT-R, so redeem the working codes below before Voldex pulls them.

All working Driving Empire codes

  • UWU: Redeem for 75,000 Cash (NEW)
  • RECORD: Redeem for 75,000 Cash (NEW)
  • USA250: Redeem for Rocket Car (NEW)
  • 2MLIKES: Redeem to get 2017 Nissan GT-R (Bolt)
  • 200KMEMBERS: Claim code for 75k Cash
  • ZOOM: Redeem for 2023 Fairway Zoomer
  • AIRDROP: 75k Cash
  • CARTER: Redeem for 50k Cash

Expired Driving Empire codes

10KITS, 1BVISITS, 1MILCASH, 1MILLIONLIKES, 450KLIKES, 500KLIK3S, 50YEARS911TURBO, 550KLIK3S, 600KL1KES, 650KL1KES, 700KL1KES, 700MV1SITS, 700MVISITS, 750KLIKES, 800KLIKES, 850KLIKES, 900KLIKES, 900MIL, 950KLIKES, C4N4D4, CALL911, CARCRUSHERS, CUSTOMIZATION2025, EMPIRE, GOBBLEGOBBLE, HAPPY2026, HAPPYXMAS, MARCH2026, MEMBERS, NASCAR100M, NEWYEAR2025, OOPSMYBADLOL, RDCNASCAR25, ROBLOX, SPOOKFEST2022, SPOOKY, THANKYOU, VALENTINES, VALENTINES2023, VEGAS2025, WHOOPS, WINTERFEST2023, ZOOM -2023 FAIRWAY ZOOMER

How to redeem Driving Empire codes

The code box is hidden inside the settings menu, not on the main screen.

  1. Open Driving Empire on Roblox.
  2. Click the gear icon in the top-left corner.
  3. Type or paste the code into the Input code box.
  4. Hit Submit.

Cash lands on your balance instantly, and free cars like the Rocket Car show up in your garage.

Why a Driving Empire code may not work

  • It expired: Voldex disables codes without warning, especially event ones.
  • A character is off: Watch for 0 vs O and 1 vs I. Pasting beats typing.
  • Wrong capitalization: Codes are case-sensitive, so type them exactly as listed above.
  • Already redeemed: Each code works once per account.
  • Old server: If a code dropped with an update, hop to a fresh server and try again.

Where to find new Driving Empire codes

Voldex drops codes around updates, events, holidays, and follower milestones, so the official channels are the first places new ones show up:

  • Driving Empire on Roblox
  • Driving Empire on X
  • Driving Empire Discord

Those channels bury codes between update teasers and memes, so bookmark this page if you just want the working list without the scrolling. If you want more free rewards, check out the latest A One Piece Game code, Bee Swarm Simulator codes, Search For The Needle codes and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

title.rendered: I found 12 hidden clues to tell if someone has Snapchat Plus: Here’s what actually works

content.rendered:
I used to think spotting a Snapchat Plus subscriber was easy: look for the little star and move on. Then I started noticing something more interesting.

Some people had no visible badge at all, yet they were using features that regular Snapchat accounts simply don’t get. Others had flashy Bitmoji backgrounds or unusual Snap behavior that looked like Snapchat Plus, but turned out to be nothing more than a misleading clue.

So I dug into the features and found 12 clues worth knowing, but they aren’t equally reliable. One is a genuine giveaway. A handful are strong pieces of supporting evidence. And several popular tricks are simply not proof that someone pays for the subscription.

Here’s how to tell if someone has Snapchat Plus.

What is Snapchat Plus?

Snapchat+ (also called Snapchat Plus) is an optional paid subscription. It gives subscribers access to exclusive, experimental, and pre-release features and tools that aren’t available to everyone.

Think of it as Snapchat’s VIP club, offering perks such as:

  • Snapchat Plus badge,
  • Custom Story expiration, Story timestamps, Story Rewatch,
  • Unique Bitmoji backgrounds and exclusive Bitmoji pets and cars,
  • Premium chat wallpapers,
  • Instant Streaks,
  • Peek a Peek,
  • Post View Emoji,
  • Replay Again,
  • Friend Solar System,
  • AI-generated profile backgrounds,
  • Advanced analytics, among others.

Many of these premium options leave visible clues, like special badges, unique icons, or customizations, that can help you spot who’s using Snapchat Plus, which we’ll explore in detail below.

However, a subscriber can turn off some features, never use others, and even hide the Snapchat+ badge. So, my rule of thumb is don’t treat one unusual Snapchat feature as proof. Look for a pattern.

How to tell if someone has Snapchat Plus

1. Look for the Snapchat Plus badge (star icon) next to their name

Reliability: 10/10 — the closest thing to definitive proof.

This is the obvious one, but there’s an important catch.

Snapchat Plus subscribers can display a special black star badge next to their display name. Snapchat says the badge is off by default, meaning a person can absolutely have the premium features without showing it.

How to spot it:

  1. Open Snapchat and go to the Friends tab.
  2. Tap on your friend’s Bitmoji or profile picture to view their profile.
  3. Look for a star icon next to their display name.

So whenever I see the Snapchat Plus badge, that’s my strongest clue. However, if you don’t see it, that does not mean they aren’t subscribed. That’s the first mistake I see people make when trying to identify Snapchat Plus users.

2. Stories visible for more than 24 hours

Reliability: 7/10 — useful, but not foolproof.

Normal Snapchat friend Stories are generally available for 24 hours. Snapchat Plus includes Custom Story Expiration, which lets eligible subscribers keep their Stories up for as long as a week.

  1. Check your friend’s Story.
  2. If the same Story is still visible after a full day, it’s a strong sign they’re using Snapchat Plus.

However, there’s a catch! Once I noticed my friend’s vacation Story was up for three days straight and concluded that “they have Plus.” But the reality was that they reposted their Story to keep it up longer. So, always double-check that it’s the same content and not a fresh post.

3. Unique Bitmoji or AI-generated profile backgrounds

Reliability: 6/10 — a good supporting clue.

This is one of the more visually obvious Snapchat Plus features.

The Plus perks include exclusive Bitmoji backgrounds such as galaxy scenes, neon designs, and custom AI artwork, as well as generative profile backgrounds. It can give a person’s 3D header behind their avatar a look you don’t normally see on a standard account. Snapchat also lists AI creative tools among its subscriber features.

How to spot it:

  1. Go to your friend’s profile.
  2. Look for a distinctive generated or premium-looking background.
  3. Now, you may open your Snapchat profile, tap your Bitmoji, select Scene, and check if your friend’s background is showing there with a lock icon.

But here’s my warning: don’t use aesthetics alone as proof. Snapchat regularly changes its creative tools, and not every unusual background means the person is currently paying for Snapchat Plus. Treat it as a clue that becomes much stronger when paired with other evidence.

4. Premium chat wallpapers

Reliability: 8/10 — one of the better visual clues.

Plus subscribers can set premium chat wallpapers, including custom images from their camera roll and AI-generated artworks.

  1. Open a chat with your friend.
  2. Notice if the wallpaper is unique, super fancy, or custom, like their personal images.
  3. Now, tap the friend’s name > Wallpaper > Select Wallpaper or Change, then view all from Snapchat. Check if their wallpaper is showing under the lock sign.

However, not all premium or AI-generated wallpapers are obvious. So, I wouldn’t call it absolute proof.

5. Extra Snap replays — the “replayed twice” clue

Reliability: 9/10 — a very strong behavioral clue.

One day, I received two notifications from the same friend that my Snap was replayed. That one thing revealed that they are a Plus member.

Snapchat Plus subscribers get Replay Again, which allows them to replay a Snap twice immediately after viewing it. For regular users, it’s one-and-done.

How to spot it:

  1. Send a Snap to your friend.
  2. If you get notifications that your Snap was replayed twice, they’re using Snapchat Plus.

However, note that only the sender can see the replay notifications, so you’ll need to be the one sending Snaps to notice this.

6. Friend Solar System icons (planets)

Reliability: 9/10 — strong clue when you actually see the feature.

This is probably the most fun Snapchat Plus feature to spot.

Snapchat’s Friend Solar System assigns planets to friends based on their position in a subscriber’s Best Friends list. Mercury represents one position, Venus second, then Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

Once, my friend told me that I am her Earth. It was a bit confusing at first. But later she showed me that my Best Friend profile is represented as a planet on her Snapchat. That’s a confirmation of Plus membership.

There is one wrinkle: Solar System is off by default for first-time subscribers, according to Snapchat. So, again, absence doesn’t prove anything. But if the feature is visibly active, put a big checkmark next to Snapchat Plus.

7. Custom Post View Emojis

Reliability: 8/10 — surprisingly good clue.

Snapchat Plus subscribers can choose a Post View Emoji that appears next to their name in Chat after someone views a Snap they’ve sent.

You might simply notice an unusual emoji like a cupcake, smiley, flower, or anything appearing beside someone’s name after you’ve viewed their Snap.

But not all subscribers use this feature, and emojis can be easy to miss. That’s exactly why I consider it a hidden clue. If the emoji is consistently associated with that person’s post-view behavior, Snapchat Plus becomes a strong possibility.

8. Unique Snap Map icons like pets, cars, and other options

Reliability: 7/10 — a useful visual clue, but don’t overstate it.

Snapchat Plus includes exclusive Bitmoji Pet and Car options, giving subscribers additional ways to customize their Bitmoji’s appearance on Snap Map.

How to spot it:

  1. Open the Snap Map.
  2. Look for unique Bitmojis, like they’re riding in a distinctive car or accompanied by a special pet.

But this is not a “gotcha.” Some icons might appear during special events, but if a friend always has a pet or car by their side, it’s likely a Plus feature.

9. Instant Snap Streaks

Reliability: 8/10 — strong clue when you know what you’re looking at.

This one surprised me because it seems as if Snapchat is breaking its own Streak rules.

Normally, you need to Snap back and forth for three days to start a Streak. Snapchat Plus lets you skip the wait and start a Snap Streak immediately.

How to spot it:

  1. Start chatting with a new friend.
  2. If you see the fire emoji (Streak) appear right away, they’re likely a Plus subscriber.

Note that the feature appears only when a subscriber has Instant Streak enabled. You also need to pay close attention to new Streaks to consider it as a clue.

10. Half Swipe / Peek a Peek

Reliability: 5/10 — only if they confront you.

Snapchat Plus’s Peek a Peek feature is essentially a half-swipe detector.

Normally, you can half-swipe on a friend’s chat to preview their message without opening it fully. This means they won’t see the “Opened” status, and you can easily act like you never read it.

With Peek a Peek, Snapchat alerts the other person when you half-swipe and peek at their chat. They can see an eyes emoji in the Chat feed or the friend’s Bitmoji at the side of the screen if they’re looking at the chat at the same time. It’s basically Snapchat’s way of saying, “They read it, they just didn’t open it.” 

How to spot it:

When you half-swipe on someone’s chat to preview their message, and they confront you about it later, there’s a good chance they’re using Snapchat Plus.

Important: This is a subtle indicator that appears only when the person is on the Chats tab. Also, the Snapchat Plus user must enable Peek a Peek from their Snapchat Plus settings for it to work.

11. Snaps clicked with GenAI-powered Lenses

Reliability: 3/10

This sounds convincing because Snapchat Plus includes AI creative tools.

If you notice someone sharing Snaps with cool AI effects, you can try the same Lens yourself. Open their Snap or Story and look for the Try Lens option. Tap it, and Snapchat will open the camera with that Lens ready to use.

Once you try it, you may notice that the Lens is powered by Generative AI or is a premium Lens. Look for the sparkle icon next to the Lens name or on the screen while the effect is active.

Keep in mind, though, that an AI-powered Lens alone doesn’t confirm that someone has Snapchat Plus. Some AI Lenses may also be available to regular Snapchat users. So, use this as one clue and check for other Snapchat Plus features before assuming they have a subscription.

12. Comic Bitmoji

Comic Bitmoji is a Snapchat Plus feature that lets users turn their Bitmoji into a comic-style character. Instead of the regular Bitmoji look, their avatar has a more dramatic, illustrated vibe, almost like it belongs in a comic strip.

It’s mostly a cosmetic upgrade, but it stands out because the Bitmoji looks noticeably different from the standard version.

How to spot it:

So if someone’s Bitmoji suddenly looks more “comic-like” with sharper outlines and a more stylized appearance, they most probably have Snapchat Plus.

But this is not a guaranteed sign on its own, since Snapchat also occasionally rolls out Bitmoji-style updates. But if the comic look appears as a distinct style option (not the default Bitmoji look), it’s a strong hint that the person is a Plus subscriber.

Limitations and things to keep in mind

Before you start investigating your entire friend list, there are a few important limitations.

  • The Snapchat+ badge can be hidden: Snapchat says the Plus badge is off by default. A subscriber can choose whether to display it. So “no star = no Snapchat Plus” is simply wrong.
  • Features can be turned off: Several premium features are optional. Solar System, for example, is off by default for first-time subscribers and can be toggled on or off. That means two people with subscriptions can have completely different-looking accounts.
  • Not all features are visible to others: Some perks, like advanced analytics or app icon changes, are private.
  • Features roll out at different times: Snapchat Plus includes experimental and pre-release features, so availability can vary. If you see a feature on one person’s account but not another’s, that doesn’t mean one person has Plus and the other doesn’t.
  • Don’t confuse Snapchat Plus with verification badges: Subscription badges don’t include Gold Star or Yellow Star. They are for verified public profiles and business profiles.

How to hide your Snapchat Plus status

If you’re the Snapchat Plus subscriber rather than the detective, you may be wondering how to make your subscription less obvious.

The simplest step is to turn off the Snapchat Plus badge.

  1. Open Snapchat and go to your profile.
  2. Tap on the Snapchat+ menu.
  3. Turn off the Snapchat+ Badge option.

But hiding the badge doesn’t make every Plus feature invisible.

If you actively use subscriber-exclusive features such as Post View Emoji, custom chat wallpapers, Instant Streaks, or Replay Again, friends may still encounter those features. If privacy matters, the better strategy is to avoid enabling the highly recognizable subscriber features.

Final thoughts

After going through the whole list of signs, I came away with a much simpler answer than I expected. The smartest way is to stop looking for one magical tell and start looking for a cluster of exclusive features.

And honestly, that’s what makes Snapchat Plus interesting: the subscription isn’t designed to announce itself everywhere. It’s designed to give people small advantages and customization options that become obvious only when you know exactly what to look for.

So the next time a friend’s Snapchat suddenly has planets, strange post-view emojis, custom wallpapers, or an extra replay, you’ll know what that Snapchat icon or notification means.

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

mainEntity.name: 2. Which other Xbox franchises have appeared in Fortnite besides Halo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: 3. Which other FPS protagonists, other than Master Chief, have been added to Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Other FPS heroes in Fortnite's skins catalog include popular characters such as Doom Slayer from Doom, V from Cyberpunk 2077, and Tracer, Genji, & D.Va from Overwatch.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

keyPoints.title: Snapchat Plus Overview
keyPoints.explanation: Snapchat Plus is a paid subscription offering exclusive features like longer Stories, custom looks, and early access, with visible clues for spotting subscribers.

keyPoints.title: Reasons to Detect Snapchat Plus Users
keyPoints.explanation: Knowing if someone has Snapchat Plus helps understand feature usage, spot exclusive content, or decide whether to subscribe yourself.

keyPoints.title: Sign 1: Snapchat+ Badge
keyPoints.explanation: A star icon next to a user's name indicates a Plus subscription, but it's optional and not always visible.

keyPoints.title: Sign 2: Longer Stories
keyPoints.explanation: Stories that last longer than 24 hours suggest the user benefits from Snapchat Plus perks.

keyPoints.title: Sign 3: Unique Profiles and Map Icons
keyPoints.explanation: Exclusive Bitmoji backgrounds, AI-generated wallpapers, special map icons, and custom replays are key indicators of Plus subscription.

title.rendered: This Apple Watch trick makes replying to messages much faster

content.rendered:
Most Apple Watch replies go the same way: tap the notification, dictate a line, fix the wrong word, send. For “ok,” “on my way,” or “call you later,” that’s more effort than the message deserves. One setting in the Watch app, which most people never open, turns those replies into a single tap.

That trick comes first. The rest are the other shortcuts worth turning on, with the model limits where they apply.

Turn your common replies into one-tap buttons

Every message notification on the watch ends with canned replies like “Yes,” “No,” “Thanks,” and “Talk later.” Replace that list with the lines you actually send, and replying becomes: tap the notification, tap your line, done.

  1. Open the Watch app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap My Watch, then Apps.
  3. Tap Messages
  4. Tap Default Replies.
  5. Tap any reply to rewrite it, or tap Add reply at the bottom to add your own.
  6. Tap Edit to delete the ones you never use and drag the rest into order.

Put the five or six lines you send daily at the top: “On my way,” “In a meeting, call you back,” “Running 10 mins late,” “Yes, send it,” “Home in 20.” Specific lines beat generic ones because they save the follow-up text.

On the watch, the list sits below the reply box and any suggested replies whenever you open a message or tap a notification. Scroll down with the Digital Crown to reach it.

Reply without touching the screen with Double Tap

On Apple Watch Series 9 or later, SE 3, and Ultra 2 or later, you can answer a text with your other hand still holding the shopping bag. When a message comes in:

  1. Tap your index finger and thumb together twice to open it.
  2. Double-tap again to start dictating.
  3. Speak your reply.
  4. Double-tap once more to send it.

It works out of the box, but if it does nothing:

  1. Open Settings on the watch.
  2. Tap Gestures, then Double Tap.
  3. Make sure the gesture is on and try again with the screen awake and the watch unlocked.

Double Tap is also disabled in Low Power Mode, during Sleep Focus, and when AssistiveTouch hand gestures are on. If you’ve never set it up, start with how to use the Double Tap gesture on Apple Watch.

Use Smart Replies when the suggestion fits

On watchOS 26, the suggested replies under a message are generated from the conversation itself. When someone asks “Are you free at 7?”:

  1. Open the message on your watch.
  2. Scroll to the suggested replies.
  3. Tap the reply that fits, such as “Yes, 7 works.”

It sends immediately. The watch can also suggest actions, like starting a Check In when a friend asks when you’ll arrive.

The catch: this needs the device language set to English and a Series 9, Series 10, Series 11, Ultra 2, or Ultra 3. Older watches still show the fixed suggestions, which is another reason to customize Default Replies.

Speak punctuation and emoji while dictating

Dictation is still the fastest way to send a full sentence, and it’s faster when you don’t go back to fix it:

  1. Tap the microphone button on the reply screen.
  2. Speak your message and say “question mark,” “comma,” or “period” where you want punctuation.
  3. Say “thumbs up emoji” or “heart emoji” to add an emoji without opening the picker.
  4. Tap Send and ignore minor slips.

The other person will get the message without you wrestling with the keyboard.

If the mic button is missing from the reply screen on watchOS 26:

  1. Open iPhone Settings.
  2. Tap General > Keyboard > Keyboards.
  3. Tap Edit and move English (US) to the top.

If your dictation comes out in the wrong language, change the dictation language on Apple Watch instead of retyping.

Send a Tapback instead of a word

Plenty of messages only need acknowledgment. To send a Tapback:

  1. Open the conversation.
  2. Double-tap the message on the screen.
  3. Pick a Tapback, like a thumbs up or heart.

It doesn’t create a new message bubble the other person has to read.

To answer one specific message in a busy group chat:

  1. Swipe right on the message you want to answer.
  2. Tap Reply.
  3. Enter and send your response.

Your response stays attached to that message instead of landing at the bottom of the thread.

Let Siri and your AirPods do the whole thing

If you wear AirPods, you can reply without looking at the watch at all:

  1. Open Settings on the watch.
  2. Tap Siri > Announce Notifications and turn it on.
  3. When Siri reads an incoming text, say, “Reply I’ll be there in five.”
  4. Turn on Reply without Confirmation at the bottom of that screen if you want Siri to skip the final confirmation.

With AirPods 4, AirPods Pro 2 or 3, or AirPods Max 2, a nod answers a call and a head shake dismisses a notification.

Without AirPods:

  1. Open Settings on the watch.
  2. Tap Siri > Raise to Speak and turn it on.
  3. Raise the watch and say, “Text Mom I’m running late,” without the wake word.

Series 9 and later, SE 3, and Ultra 2 and later run Siri on the watch itself, so there’s no pause while it waits for the network. There’s more Siri can do on Apple Watch once it’s set up this way.

Record an audio message for anything longer

When a reply runs past a sentence or two, dictation starts making mistakes, and the keyboard gets tedious. Send an audio message instead:

  1. Open the conversation.
  2. Tap the Apps button next to the text field.
  3. Tap Audio.
  4. Record what you want to say.
  5. Tap Send.

The other person gets a voice clip, which is fine for friends and family and less fine for your manager.

Hand off to the iPhone when you’re typing anyway

Sometimes the watch is the wrong tool. Hand the reply to your iPhone instead:

  1. Start a reply on the watch.
  2. Tap the Apple Watch Keyboard Input notification on your iPhone.
  3. Continue typing the same message on the full keyboard.

That’s faster than closing the watch, unlocking the phone, and finding the thread.

For a single name or word dictation keeps getting wrong, the watch’s QWERTY keyboard with swipe typing works on Series 7 and later and the Ultra models, but not on the SE or Series 6. Scribble, where you draw letters with a finger, works on every model.

Dismiss what you won’t answer

Not every text deserves a reply right now. On Series 9 or later, SE 3, and Ultra 2 or later:

  1. Raise your wrist when the notification arrives.
  2. Quickly flick your wrist away and back.

The notification disappears, and you return to the watch face without tapping anything. The setup is in How to use the wrist flick gesture on Apple Watch.

Do the Default Replies first. It takes two minutes, works on every Apple Watch, and covers most of what you send from the wrist. Turn on the gestures and Siri options if your watch supports them, then work through more Apple Watch tips and tricks that save time the same way.

title.rendered: Meta AI gets a Mac app that can see your screen and read your Instagram stats

content.rendered:
Meta AI now has a native Mac app in beta. Meta announced it on August 19 as part of a push toward small businesses and creators. The desktop app can read a shared window, type dictated text into any app, and pull engagement data from your Facebook and Instagram accounts.

The beta is free and downloads directly from the Meta AI site, not the Mac App Store.

The Mac app can read a shared window and dictate anywhere

Two features are desktop-only. You can attach a Mac window to a conversation, and Meta AI reads the visible text and captures a screenshot so it can answer questions about what you are working on. That requires Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions. The app also offers systemwide dictation: hold a shortcut, speak, and the words land in Mail, a document, or any other app.

Pressing Option-Space opens a compact Meta AI composer over your current app. You can also hide the Dock icon so the assistant stays behind the keyboard shortcut. According to a 9to5Mac hands-on, the app is a native build using AppKit and SwiftUI, weighs about 16MB installed, and needs an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or later. Meta has not published official requirements.

Meta is positioning it around business data

The main differentiator is access to business data. If you connect a professional Facebook or Instagram account, Meta AI can answer questions about reach, saves, shares, comments, and profile visits, analyze ad campaign performance, and benchmark your results against similar brands using public data. Most rival chatbots can help write a caption, but Meta AI can also work from the account’s own performance data.

It also connects to Google Workspace, so it can pull from Gmail, Docs, Sheets, and Slides. From there, it can build decks, docs, spreadsheets, and reports, or run recurring jobs like a weekly performance summary.

The app is free for now, but Meta is testing usage limits on compute-heavy features. Hit a daily or monthly cap, and you get offered a Meta One subscription for more headroom. Meta has not shared what that costs yet.

The privacy trade-off is real

Meta’s generative AI privacy policy says your interactions with Meta AI can be used to train its models. That matters more when the Mac app can read your screen and connected Google Workspace files. Incognito Mode is available for chats you want kept separate, and you can turn off Meta AI inside WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook if you do not want to use it there.

Meta already has Muse Code on the Mac, while the Meta AI app launched on iPhone and Android in April 2025. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini also have desktop apps with screen-aware features. Meta’s bet is that access to Instagram analytics will make its assistant more useful to creators and small businesses.

title.rendered: EU welcomes Apple’s new App Store terms, Epic calls them junk fees

content.rendered:
The European Commission says it welcomes the new EU App Store business terms Apple announced on August 18. That suggests the regulator is willing to work with Apple’s revised framework, but the case is not closed. Epic Games, which has spent years challenging Apple’s fees, says the new terms still break the law.

Apple is replacing several EU fee structures with one set of terms

Apple is scrapping its patchwork of EU fee structures and moving every developer to a single set of terms from October 1, 2026. The per-install Core Technology Fee is gone, along with the Initial Acquisition Fee and the Store Services Fee.

In their place, Apple charges a flat commission based on how an app is distributed and how users pay:

  • 26% for App Store sales through Apple’s In-App Purchase, with 15% for Small Business Program developers and subscriptions after year one
  • 20% for App Store apps that use an alternative payment processor, dropping to 10% for small businesses
  • 15% for purchases made through link-outs to the web, dropping to 10% for small businesses
  • 5% Core Technology Commission for apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web

Developers can also offer Apple’s In-App Purchase alongside alternative payment options in the same app, something Apple never allowed before. Small marketplace operators earning under 10 million euros a year can get the 5% commission waived entirely.

The Commission will monitor the rollout

“The Commission welcomes Apple’s changes to their business terms, which follow a close dialogue between the Commission and Apple,” a European Commission spokesperson said in a statement shared with the press. The statement refers to the non-compliance decision on Apple’s steering rules and the preliminary findings on alternative distribution from April 2025.

That April 2025 decision came with a 500 million euro fine, which Apple is still fighting in court. The Commission has not formally closed its case. It will monitor how Apple implements the new terms, so the welcome is not a declaration that the dispute is over.

Epic says the fees still break the DMA

Epic Games rejected the new terms within hours, calling the new tiers “junk fees” that do nothing to open up iOS to real competition.

Epic’s argument is simple: the DMA says developers must be able to steer users to the web “free of charge” and make “effective use” of competing stores. In Epic’s reading, any commission above zero on those transactions violates the law, so a 15% link-out fee and a 5% cut on Epic Games Store purchases are just the old tax with new labels.

The Commission’s welcome suggests it considers the framework workable for now. Regulators spent more than a year in talks with Apple after the fine, and the fee levels Epic objects to are the ones that came out of that dialogue.

The new terms start October 1

The new terms kick in across the EU on October 1. Apple, which has long argued the DMA delays features and creates security risks for European users, gets regulatory breathing room just as its App Store model faces pressure everywhere else. EU developers finally get one rulebook instead of three overlapping ones.

Epic has no path to veto the deal, but it can keep lobbying the Commission and challenging Apple in court, which it has never been shy about. And if Apple’s implementation falls short of what regulators expect, the monitoring phase gives Brussels an easy way to reopen the fight.

title.rendered: Apple fires back at OpenAI’s bid to dismiss its trade secret lawsuit

content.rendered:
Apple is asking a federal judge to keep its trade secret case against OpenAI alive. In an opposition filed on August 19 in federal court in San Jose, Apple says OpenAI’s motion to dismiss “relies on distortion, speculation, and improper extrinsic evidence” and asks the court to deny it in full.

The filing answers the motion OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan filed on August 5. That motion called Apple’s July lawsuit meritless and asked the court to end the case before discovery begins.

Apple repeats its core allegations

Apple’s response revisits the allegations in its original complaint. It says Liu, a senior system electrical engineer who spent eight years at Apple, exploited an authentication bug to access Apple’s confidential network repository for weeks after joining OpenAI. Apple alleges that he downloaded dozens of engineering files, including a presentation on how Apple builds and tests its main logic boards, and reacted to his own access in writing with “LOL … so funny.”

The filing also alleges that Tan, now OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, used Apple’s internal project codenames to quiz job candidates about unreleased products. Apple says he asked a then-current employee to bring “some parts” she worked on, including batteries and logic boards, to interviews for “show and tell.”

Apple also accuses OpenAI and io Products of building the behavior into their hiring process: structuring interviews to pull out engineering and supplier details, encouraging candidates to bring prototypes and CAD files, coaching new hires to dodge Apple’s exit procedures, and getting one of Apple’s manufacturing partners to perform a proprietary metal-finishing technique on OpenAI products.

Apple challenges OpenAI’s defenses

OpenAI’s motion says Apple never identified real trade secrets, showed actual misappropriation, or explained how it was harmed. It portrays Liu as an ex-employee helping a former colleague at an Apple manager’s request, and says Tan kept an Apple offboarding document for legitimate compliance reasons.

Apple’s answer to the Liu defense is the sharpest line in the filing: “A manager’s transition question is not authorization to raid Apple’s confidential repository.” It adds that the defendants cite nothing suggesting anyone at Apple knew about or approved the downloads.

Apple also objects to how OpenAI built its motion, saying the company leaned on outside messages, third-party websites, and attorney claims about Apple’s security practices. That kind of extrinsic evidence, Apple argues, has no place at the dismissal stage, where the court must accept the complaint’s allegations as true.

OpenAI’s public response remains firm. In a blog post titled “Apple is getting this wrong,” the company says it does not have and does not want any Apple trade secrets, and calls the lawsuit “careless, aggressive and oddly personal.”

What happens next

OpenAI’s reply is due August 26, and Judge Edward J. Davila hears arguments on the motion to dismiss on October 1 in San Jose. Apple’s separate push for a preliminary injunction, which could restrict OpenAI’s hardware work while the case plays out, runs on its own schedule: opposition briefs are due August 31, with replies by September 14.

If the motion fails, OpenAI faces discovery into its hardware program as it works toward its first devices. If it succeeds, Apple may get a chance to amend its complaint, a possibility Apple’s filing acknowledges.

mainEntity.name: 1. When did Master Chief first land in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

mainEntity.name: 2. Which other Xbox franchises have appeared in Fortnite besides Halo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: 3. Which other FPS protagonists, other than Master Chief, have been added to Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Other FPS heroes in Fortnite's skins catalog include popular characters such as Doom Slayer from Doom, V from Cyberpunk 2077, and Tracer, Genji, & D.Va from Overwatch.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

title.rendered: What happens to your sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 | Sprite Garden explained

content.rendered:
Fortnite recently announced a big change coming to your existing collection of sprites. Not only did they confirm a new set of sprites will replace the existing ones in Chapter 7 Season 4, but they also shared future plans for what happens to those critters you collected in Fortnite Runners.

On August 7, Fortnite officially gave the green light for the sprites gameplay feature to carry over into Fortnite Override. This was met positively by many sections of fans, as this particular aspect of the game has turned out to be very popular among players. Below, you can learn more about how the transition from Season 3 to Season 4 will affect your sprites. You can also find out everything you need to know about the newly revealed Sprite Garden map.

What happens to Chapter 7 Season 3 sprites in Season 4

Fortnite Runners brought a whopping 117 sprites (including variants) for players to catch. Courtesy of the various Sprite Hours, where the spawn rate of a particular sprite or variant is temporarily boosted, which took place at different points throughout the season, many players have put together a long lineup of their own extracted sprites.

Now, apparently, all the sprites from Chapter 7 Season 3 will be restricted to a new Fortnite map called Sprite Garden. For the Season 4 Battle Royale modes, a new set of sprites will be released, which will consist of a mix of fan-made sprites and those made by the devs. It’s worth paying attention that the devs also shared that certain previously added sprites may even be re-released, allowing them to be used beyond the Sprite Garden.

The inclusion of fan-made sprites came about after a public “Design a Sprite” contest was organized by Epic Games. Some of these sprites have already been unveiled and offer benefits as shared below.

  • Bullet Sprite: Ammo boxes grant slightly more ammunition than usual.
  • Dumpster Dive Sprite: Jumping into dumpsters will provide loot.
  • Honey Sprite: When attacked, a beehive spawns, releasing a swarm of bees onto your enemy, which will inflict light damage for a span of time.
  • Pond Sprite: Your movement speed in water increases with each level, offering boosted jump height and reduced fall damage at level 5.
  • X-Ray Sprite: Offers the ability to see through walls and other obstacles for a limited time.

Moreover, it was also noted that Fortnite Override will bring more ways to “discover” sprites, both in and out of the game. Even though it isn’t clear what this statement entails, it does suggest that sprite extraction during matches may not be the only way you can add sprites to your collection in Chapter 7 Season 4. Additionally, it was further revealed that owned gizmos, such as the Portable Extractor, and Sprite Dust will be reset for the new season.

Sprite Garden in Fortnite, explained

Sprite Garden is the island map where you would be able to equip and showcase Fortnite Runners season sprites, while also being able to visit your friends’ garden sanctuaries, possibly to take a look at their respective sprite collections. Additionally, the sprites you obtain in the Fortnite Override season will also appear in this mode as you grow your collection.

Besides the Sprite Garden, you can further display the Season 3 sprites as part of your cosmetics via the Sprite Mastery Pod Back Bling and via the Guardian Outfit. These old sprites will also still appear in the Sprites tab, together with the new sprites that will join the game eventually.

Wrapping up

With how popular sprites have turned out to be among Fortnite players, it’s no doubt that Epic Games has decided to continue this feature. The novelty of fan-made sprites in Chapter 7 Season 4 could certainly feel like a breath of fresh air.

Based on what we know so far, the incoming fleet of sprites seems to offer exciting variety. From IP-inspired sprites such as Sonic the Hedgehog Sprite to community-powered ones such as the Bullet Sprite, there is no dearth of distinct boosts provided by these backpack-like companions. However, whether or not this variety translates into another successful season for Sprite is something only time will tell.

  • Confirmed game characters in Fortnite Override
  • How to get Calm Capy sidekick in Fortnite
